store_data.about_the_game:
NOT ANOTHER COPY — YOUR HEROES BECOME WHAT YOU MAKE THEM. WIELD STAVES TO MASTER MAGIC, FIGHT WITH WEAPONS TO BECOME A WARRIOR, ENDURE DAMAGE TO GROW INTO A TANK, OR WALK THE PATH OF NECROMANCY AND LEARN TO RAISE FALLEN ENEMIES. ACTIVE AND PASSIVE SKILLS ARE EARNED THROUGH HOW YOU PLAY, SURVIVE, AND EVOLVE.

ENTER A WORLD WHERE HEROES ARE NOT IMMORTAL

Summon heroes, tame powerful creatures, strengthen your Sanctuary, and enter tactical expeditions where every decision can permanently change your future.

In Isekai: Demon King, you are the Custodian — the one responsible for summoning, training, equipping, protecting, and guiding heroes through a brutal world ruled by demons, ancient beasts, corrupted entities, and enemies far beyond ordinary human power.

You do not fight as the main hero.

You create the heroes who will become legends.

Victory creates legends.



Failure can erase them forever.

TACTICAL TURN-BASED COMBAT

Build a 2x3 formation and command every action.

Position matters.

Front-line heroes gain defensive advantages.
Central positions favor Mana.
Rear positions favor speed.

Manage:

  • Turn order

  • Mana

  • Active skills

  • Passive abilities

  • Buffs and debuffs

  • Status effects

  • Elemental interactions

  • Equipment

  • Formation

  • Defensive actions

  • Target priority

  • Team synergy

A stronger team is not always enough.

Preparation, positioning, timing, and decision-making determine who survives.

EXTREME DIFFICULTY

Isekai: Demon King is designed to challenge you.

Not every enemy is meant to be defeated immediately.

Bosses demand preparation. Powerful enemies punish careless builds. A single mistake during a dangerous expedition can destroy months of progress on a hero.

Sometimes the correct decision is to fight.

Sometimes it is to change your formation.

Sometimes it is to retreat before everything is lost.

PERMANENT HERO DEATH

During dangerous expeditions and high-risk wars, heroes can die permanently.

There are no ordinary resurrection items.

There is no simple gold payment to undo death.

There is no advertisement that brings a dead hero back.

A hero who falls may lose everything they had built:

  • Levels

  • Equipment

  • Skills

  • Passive abilities

  • Battle history

  • Progression

  • Personal identity

Every hero you send into danger matters.

LEGACIES — DEATH DOES NOT ERASE EVERYTHING

Death may end a hero's life, but it does not necessarily end their influence.

Fallen heroes can create Legacies shaped by the lives they actually lived.

A Legacy may preserve:

  • Signature abilities

  • Important passive traits

  • Mastered techniques

  • Attribute bonuses

  • Combat affinities

  • Historical achievements

  • Memories of important battles

But inheriting a Legacy does not grant its full power instantly.

A new hero must live, fight, survive, and prove themselves before fully assimilating what was inherited.

What they successfully inherit becomes part of their own story.

If they die, a new Legacy may be born.

Legends are not copied. They are inherited through experience.

THE 200-FLOOR ASCENDING DUNGEON

Challenge a massive dungeon built around long-term progression.

The journey spans 200 increasingly dangerous floors, moving from common beasts and hostile creatures toward corrupted monsters, dragons, demon generals, commanders, final entities, and eventually forces connected directly to the Demon King.

Every floor is an expedition.

Expect:

  • Normal encounters

  • Dangerous battles

  • Elite enemies

  • Protected treasure

  • Environmental events

  • Limited rest opportunities

  • Pre-boss encounters

  • Mandatory Floor Guardians

  • Major bosses

  • Unique rewards

You cannot simply rush to the exit.

The Floor Guardian must fall before progression continues.

EXPEDITIONS AND EXTRACTION

Before entering a floor, prepare carefully.

Choose:

  • Your heroes

  • Formation

  • Equipment

  • Consumables

  • Backpack space

  • Expedition relics

  • Strategy

Your backpack has limited capacity.

Loot found during an expedition is not automatically safe.

Weapons, materials, consumables, keys, relics, ascension items and other physical rewards must survive the expedition with you.

Gold and Soul Fragments collected during the run are also temporary until the floor is successfully completed.

Retreat and your surviving heroes may return...

…but the expedition rewards can be lost.

You do not own what drops.



You own what you manage to bring home.

SUMMON HEROES — POTENTIAL, NOT AUTOMATIC POWER

Summoning gives you heroes with different:

  • Star ranks

  • Attributes

  • Roles

  • Elements

  • Skills

  • Passive abilities

  • Potential

  • Lineages

Higher rarity offers greater potential, but it does not automatically create the strongest hero.

A lower-rarity hero who survives, trains, evolves, gains equipment, develops skills and inherits powerful Legacies can become extraordinarily valuable.

Your strongest hero is not necessarily the hero you summoned yesterday.

It may be the one who survived everything.

POTENTIAL

Every summoned hero has a Potential level that influences their long-term growth.

Potential ranges from ordinary growth to exceptional talent.

Heroes with greater Potential gain more from their development and can reach extraordinary levels of specialization.

But Potential alone does not win battles.

Time, survival, equipment and decisions still matter.

ASCEND BEYOND YOUR ORIGINAL LIMITS

Heroes are not permanently trapped at the rank in which they were summoned.

Through Ascension, a hero can break beyond their original star limit.

Ascension does not require sacrificing duplicate heroes.

Instead, powerful materials obtained from:

  • Dungeon progression

  • Elite enemies

  • Bosses

  • World events

  • Demon commanders

  • High-level challenges

allow experienced heroes to surpass their previous limits.

The strongest heroes are built over time.

DEEP SKILL AND PASSIVE BUILDS

Heroes can learn more abilities than they can actively equip.

Build each hero by choosing which skills and passive abilities define their role.

Higher-rank heroes unlock increasingly complex build possibilities.

A hero can become:

  • A defensive protector

  • A high-speed attacker

  • A critical specialist

  • A control unit

  • A Mana-focused caster

  • A support character

  • A hybrid build

  • Something completely different through equipment and inherited power

Two heroes with the same origin do not have to become the same fighter.

DEEP EQUIPMENT SYSTEM

Equip heroes with weapons, armor, accessories, rings and necklaces across a deep equipment system.

Equipment can possess:

  • Levels

  • Stars

  • Rarity

  • Quality

  • Compatibility

  • Durability

  • History

  • Special effects

Heroes can equip gear above their current rank, but they may suffer significant penalties until they are strong enough to use it effectively.

Rare equipment can become part of a hero's identity.

Some items may survive longer than the heroes who once carried them.

FORGING

Gather materials from enemies, bosses and expeditions to create and improve equipment.

The Forge allows you to:

  • Craft equipment

  • Upgrade weapons and armor

  • Repair damaged gear

  • Reforge properties

  • Add affinities

  • Restore valuable equipment

  • Purify corrupted items

  • Create specialized builds

Craftsmanship itself can influence the final quality of an item.

EXPEDITION RELICS

Relics are not normal equipment.

They affect the entire expedition team and are selected before entering dangerous content.

Relics can specialize your party toward:

  • Combat

  • Survival

  • Exploration

  • Defense

  • Legacies

  • Lineages

  • Corruption

  • Divine power

Your available relic slots increase as you progress deeper into the world.

LINEAGES

Heroes may possess powerful Lineages that influence how they grow and fight.

Lineages can specialize characters toward different physical, magical, elemental or spiritual paths.

A Lineage represents what a hero is.

A Legacy represents what a hero became.

Combine both systems to create highly specialized heroes.

TAME CREATURES

Not every creature must be killed.

Encounter beasts, magical creatures, spirits and rare entities throughout the world and attempt to tame them.

Raise and develop captured creatures as part of your long-term progression.

Some are common companions.

Others are extremely rare rewards obtained through dangerous encounters and limited opportunities.

Certain powerful creatures — including young dragons — can become some of the most valuable additions to your Sanctuary.

BUILD YOUR SANCTUARY

Your Sanctuary is the center of your progression.

Develop facilities dedicated to:

  • Hero summoning

  • Barracks management

  • Rest and recovery

  • Food and preparation

  • Forging

  • Storage

  • Consumables

  • Legacies

  • Lineages

  • Creature taming

  • Training

  • Expedition planning

  • Relics

  • Custodian progression

Buildings unlock new functions as they improve.

The Sanctuary is not simply a menu between battles.

It is where wars are prepared before they begin.

BECOME A STRONGER CUSTODIAN

Your heroes are not the only ones who progress.

The Custodian develops their own Authority, improving how efficiently the Sanctuary operates and expanding the strategic options available to your roster.

Your power comes from leadership, preparation and the systems you build around your heroes.

WORLD EVENTS AND SPECIAL CHALLENGES

Participate in changing challenges outside normal dungeon progression.

Face:

  • Capture events

  • Rare creatures

  • Ancient dragons

  • World bosses

  • Limited encounters

  • Seasonal activities

  • Special rewards

  • High-level challenges

Some events are opportunities.

Others are tests designed specifically for your strongest teams.

RANKED PvP (Coming Soon)

Challenge other players in tactical online battles.

Progress through ranked arenas with different level caps designed to preserve strategic competition while allowing your permanent progression to remain meaningful.

Build formations specifically for PvP and adapt to opponents instead of simply overpowering them with levels.

CROSS-PLATFORM MULTIPLAYER (Coming Soon)

Battle players across supported platforms.

PC and mobile players can enter the same online PvP ecosystem, allowing the community to compete beyond a single device family.

FREE TO PLAY — NO ENERGY SYSTEM

Isekai: Demon King is Free to Play.

There is no traditional energy system that forces you to stop playing because an arbitrary meter reached zero.

Your real limitations are:

  • Difficulty

  • Risk

  • Resources

  • Preparation

  • Backpack capacity

  • Hero survival

  • Your own decisions

You can continue playing.

Whether your heroes continue surviving is another question.

ORIGINAL SOUNDTRACK

Enter the world of Isekai: Demon King accompanied by a fully original soundtrack created specifically for the game.

From the solemn atmosphere of the Sanctuary to dangerous expeditions and intense battles, the soundtrack evolves alongside the scale of your journey.

A GAME ABOUT CREATING LEGENDS

Isekai: Demon King is not simply about collecting characters.

It is about remembering them.

The hero who survived when everyone else died.

The weak recruit who eventually became your strongest warrior.

The veteran who carried the same weapon through hundreds of battles.

The hero who inherited an unfinished Legacy and completed it.

The one who defeated an impossible boss.

And the one who died protecting everyone else.

Every hero has a story.



Every expedition carries a risk.



Every victory changes your future.



Every death can become history.

Do not simply collect heroes.

CREATE LEGENDS.

  • Team synergy

A stronger team is not always enough.

Preparation, positioning, timing, and decision-making determine who survives.

EXTREME DIFFICULTY

Isekai: Demon King is designed to challenge you.

Not every enemy is meant to be defeated immediately.

Bosses demand preparation. Powerful enemies punish careless builds. A single mistake during a dangerous expedition can destroy months of progress on a hero.

Sometimes the correct decision is to fight.

Sometimes it is to change your formation.

Sometimes it is to retreat before everything is lost.

PERMANENT HERO DEATH

During dangerous expeditions and high-risk wars, heroes can die permanently.

There are no ordinary resurrection items.

There is no simple gold payment to undo death.

There is no advertisement that brings a dead hero back.

A hero who falls may lose everything they had built:

  • Levels

  • Equipment

  • Skills

  • Passive abilities

  • Battle history

  • Progression

  • Personal identity

Every hero you send into danger matters.

LEGACIES — DEATH DOES NOT ERASE EVERYTHING

Death may end a hero's life, but it does not necessarily end their influence.

Fallen heroes can create Legacies shaped by the lives they actually lived.

A Legacy may preserve:

  • Signature abilities

  • Important passive traits

  • Mastered techniques

  • Attribute bonuses

  • Combat affinities

  • Historical achievements

  • Memories of important battles

But inheriting a Legacy does not grant its full power instantly.

A new hero must live, fight, survive, and prove themselves before fully assimilating what was inherited.

What they successfully inherit becomes part of their own story.

If they die, a new Legacy may be born.

Legends are not copied. They are inherited through experience.

THE 200-FLOOR ASCENDING DUNGEON

Challenge a massive dungeon built around long-term progression.

The journey spans 200 increasingly dangerous floors, moving from common beasts and hostile creatures toward corrupted monsters, dragons, demon generals, commanders, final entities, and eventually forces connected directly to the Demon King.

Every floor is an expedition.

Expect:

  • Normal encounters

  • Dangerous battles

  • Elite enemies

  • Protected treasure

  • Environmental events

  • Limited rest opportunities

  • Pre-boss encounters

  • Mandatory Floor Guardians

  • Major bosses

  • Unique rewards

You cannot simply rush to the exit.

The Floor Guardian must fall before progression continues.

EXPEDITIONS AND EXTRACTION

Before entering a floor, prepare carefully.

Choose:

  • Your heroes

  • Formation

  • Equipment

  • Consumables

  • Backpack space

  • Expedition relics

  • Strategy

Your backpack has limited capacity.

Loot found during an expedition is not automatically safe.

Weapons, materials, consumables, keys, relics, ascension items and other physical rewards must survive the expedition with you.

Gold and Soul Fragments collected during the run are also temporary until the floor is successfully completed.

Retreat and your surviving heroes may return...

…but the expedition rewards can be lost.

You do not own what drops.



You own what you manage to bring home.

SUMMON HEROES — POTENTIAL, NOT AUTOMATIC POWER

Summoning gives you heroes with different:

  • Star ranks

  • Attributes

  • Roles

  • Elements

  • Skills

  • Passive abilities

  • Potential

  • Lineages

Higher rarity offers greater potential, but it does not automatically create the strongest hero.

A lower-rarity hero who survives, trains, evolves, gains equipment, develops skills and inherits powerful Legacies can become extraordinarily valuable.

Your strongest hero is not necessarily the hero you summoned yesterday.

It may be the one who survived everything.

POTENTIAL

Every summoned hero has a Potential level that influences their long-term growth.

Potential ranges from ordinary growth to exceptional talent.

Heroes with greater Potential gain more from their development and can reach extraordinary levels of specialization.

But Potential alone does not win battles.

Time, survival, equipment and decisions still matter.

ASCEND BEYOND YOUR ORIGINAL LIMITS

Heroes are not permanently trapped at the rank in which they were summoned.

Through Ascension, a hero can break beyond their original star limit.

Ascension does not require sacrificing duplicate heroes.

Instead, powerful materials obtained from:

  • Dungeon progression

  • Elite enemies

  • Bosses

  • World events

  • Demon commanders

  • High-level challenges

allow experienced heroes to surpass their previous limits.

The strongest heroes are built over time.

DEEP SKILL AND PASSIVE BUILDS

Heroes can learn more abilities than they can actively equip.

Build each hero by choosing which skills and passive abilities define their role.

Higher-rank heroes unlock increasingly complex build possibilities.

A hero can become:

  • A defensive protector

  • A high-speed attacker

  • A critical specialist

  • A control unit

  • A Mana-focused caster

  • A support character

  • A hybrid build

  • Something completely different through equipment and inherited power

Two heroes with the same origin do not have to become the same fighter.

DEEP EQUIPMENT SYSTEM

Equip heroes with weapons, armor, accessories, rings and necklaces across a deep equipment system.

Equipment can possess:

  • Levels

  • Stars

  • Rarity

  • Quality

  • Compatibility

  • Durability

  • History

  • Special effects

Heroes can equip gear above their current rank, but they may suffer significant penalties until they are strong enough to use it effectively.

Rare equipment can become part of a hero's identity.

Some items may survive longer than the heroes who once carried them.

FORGING

Gather materials from enemies, bosses and expeditions to create and improve equipment.

The Forge allows you to:

  • Craft equipment

  • Upgrade weapons and armor

  • Repair damaged gear

  • Reforge properties

  • Add affinities

  • Restore valuable equipment

  • Purify corrupted items

  • Create specialized builds

Craftsmanship itself can influence the final quality of an item.

EXPEDITION RELICS

Relics are not normal equipment.

They affect the entire expedition team and are selected before entering dangerous content.

Relics can specialize your party toward:

  • Combat

  • Survival

  • Exploration

  • Defense

  • Legacies

  • Lineages

  • Corruption

  • Divine power

Your available relic slots increase as you progress deeper into the world.

LINEAGES

Heroes may possess powerful Lineages that influence how they grow and fight.

Lineages can specialize characters toward different physical, magical, elemental or spiritual paths.

A Lineage represents what a hero is.

A Legacy represents what a hero became.

Combine both systems to create highly specialized heroes.

TAME CREATURES

Not every creature must be killed.

Encounter beasts, magical creatures, spirits and rare entities throughout the world and attempt to tame them.

Raise and develop captured creatures as part of your long-term progression.

Some are common companions.

Others are extremely rare rewards obtained through dangerous encounters and limited opportunities.

Certain powerful creatures — including young dragons — can become some of the most valuable additions to your Sanctuary.

BUILD YOUR SANCTUARY

Your Sanctuary is the center of your progression.

Develop facilities dedicated to:

  • Hero summoning

  • Barracks management

  • Rest and recovery

  • Food and preparation

  • Forging

  • Storage

  • Consumables

  • Legacies

  • Lineages

  • Creature taming

  • Training

  • Expedition planning

  • Relics

  • Custodian progression

Buildings unlock new functions as they improve.

The Sanctuary is not simply a menu between battles.

It is where wars are prepared before they begin.

BECOME A STRONGER CUSTODIAN

Your heroes are not the only ones who progress.

The Custodian develops their own Authority, improving how efficiently the Sanctuary operates and expanding the strategic options available to your roster.

Your power comes from leadership, preparation and the systems you build around your heroes.

WORLD EVENTS AND SPECIAL CHALLENGES

Participate in changing challenges outside normal dungeon progression.

Face:

  • Capture events

  • Rare creatures

  • Ancient dragons

  • World bosses

  • Limited encounters

  • Seasonal activities

  • Special rewards

  • High-level challenges

Some events are opportunities.

Others are tests designed specifically for your strongest teams.

RANKED PvP (Coming Soon)

Challenge other players in tactical online battles.

Progress through ranked arenas with different level caps designed to preserve strategic competition while allowing your permanent progression to remain meaningful.

Build formations specifically for PvP and adapt to opponents instead of simply overpowering them with levels.

CROSS-PLATFORM MULTIPLAYER (Coming Soon)

Battle players across supported platforms.

PC and mobile players can enter the same online PvP ecosystem, allowing the community to compete beyond a single device family.

FREE TO PLAY — NO ENERGY SYSTEM

Isekai: Demon King is Free to Play.

There is no traditional energy system that forces you to stop playing because an arbitrary meter reached zero.

Your real limitations are:

  • Difficulty

  • Risk

  • Resources

  • Preparation

  • Backpack capacity

  • Hero survival

  • Your own decisions

You can continue playing.

Whether your heroes continue surviving is another question.

ORIGINAL SOUNDTRACK

Enter the world of Isekai: Demon King accompanied by a fully original soundtrack created specifically for the game.

From the solemn atmosphere of the Sanctuary to dangerous expeditions and intense battles, the soundtrack evolves alongside the scale of your journey.

A GAME ABOUT CREATING LEGENDS

Isekai: Demon King is not simply about collecting characters.

It is about remembering them.

The hero who survived when everyone else died.

The weak recruit who eventually became your strongest warrior.

The veteran who carried the same weapon through hundreds of battles.

The hero who inherited an unfinished Legacy and completed it.

The one who defeated an impossible boss.

And the one who died protecting everyone else.

Every hero has a story.



Every expedition carries a risk.



Every victory changes your future.



Every death can become history.

Do not simply collect heroes.

CREATE LEGENDS.
store_data.short_description: A brutal tactical turn-based RPG where heroes grow through how you play. Summon and train unique fighters, master evolving active and passive skills, survive permadeath expeditions, build your Sanctuary, tame creatures, inherit Legacies, and battle in cross-platform PvP.

store_data.about_the_game:
Equip Your Polar Bear. Build the Ultimate King.

Give your polar bear weapons, shields, and all kinds of equipment to create the strongest fighter possible.

Point a sword straight ahead.
Surround the entire body with shields.

Attach weights to create a build that is harder to knock away.

Where you place each piece of equipment—and the angle you attach it at—is entirely up to you.

Once your polar bear is complete, it will automatically battle polar bears created by other players.

There is no need to wait for an opponent in real time.
Download another player’s equipment data and enjoy asynchronous online battles whenever you like.

Placement Is Strategy

Equipment can be attached not only to the polar bear itself, but also to other pieces of equipment.

Attach another sword to the tip of a sword.
Hide a gun behind a shield.

Within a limited equipment-cost budget, you must balance offense, defense, speed, and stability.

Your build may look a little strange, but if it wins, it works.

Unpredictable 2D Physics Battles

When the battle begins, both polar bears automatically move toward each other.

When swords collide, both fighters are knocked backward.

Crashing into a wall causes damage.

The last polar bear standing becomes the King.

Asynchronous Ranked Matches

Every player starts with 100 Rank Points.

In Ranked Matches, you will battle against player data from opponents with a similar rank.

Winning increases your Rank Points, while losing decreases them.
The amount gained or lost depends on the rank difference between you and your opponent.

Defeat stronger opponents and climb to the top of the rankings.

Practice Against CPU Opponents

Before entering online battles, you can test your equipment setup against fixed CPU opponents.

Experiment with weapon angles, shield placement, and knockback behavior as you fine-tune your own unique build.

CPU battles do not affect your Rank Points.

Available Equipment

Sword: A basic weapon that deals damage when it touches an opponent.

Gun: A ranged weapon that can attack from a distance.

Shield: A defensive item that blocks enemy weapons.

Weight: Reduces knockback.

More equipment is planned for future updates.

Key Features

  • Freely customize your polar bear by placing equipment wherever you like

  • Asynchronous online battles against equipment builds created by other players

  • 2D physics combat featuring rotation, gravity, collisions, and knockback

  • Rank Points and online rankings

  • Strategic build creation with a limited equipment-cost system

  • Practice battles against CPU opponents

  • Japanese and English language support

  • Completely free to play

Free to Play

SHIROKUMA KING can be enjoyed completely free from beginning to end.

If you enjoy the game, you can optionally purchase a supporter item to help fund future development and updates.

Supporter items provide no gameplay advantages and do not affect competitive balance.

Simply playing the game is already more than enough support.

Now, give your polar bear some weapons.

It will figure out the rest.

5073290.name: Vlad Voievod Dracula The Crusaders Tomb

store_data.about_the_game:
While being a prisoner to the Ottoman Court, waiting for the sultan's order, Vlad Dracula travels to slave markets, dungeons and prisons recruiting skilled warriors to help him take his Wallachian throne. This is when he hears about a great warrior held by the Genovese in the place called The Crusaders Tomb

Explore a beautiful pixel art game with carefully hand crafted levels, well placed enemies, weapons and ammo designed to bring back that beautiful old-school vibe. In Classicvania style you hit torches to receive sub-weapons and collect hearts (ammo) to power them. Find the famous "wall-meat" that refills your health, and get powerful sword upgrades hidden in the dungeon walls. Find secrets and discover the most valuable treasures by crouching in key locations.

If you enjoyed NES games like Castlevania I/III, Ninja Gaiden III, Batman the video game, Shatterhand, Journey to Sillius - this game might be perfect for you. Give it a try!

store_data.about_the_game:
A 3D arcade runner where visibility is a resource.

Bat Flapper is a fast-paced 3D arcade runner where you survive by sound instead of sight. Race through dark cave tunnels as a bat, using echo location to send pulses of sonar to reveal obstacles hidden in the darkness.

Your sonar energy is always draining, and the only way to recharge it is by eating glowing bugs scattered throughout the cave. Reaching them often means leaving the safest path, forcing you to choose between playing it safe and risking the darkness, or diving into danger to keep your sonar alive.

With quick restarts, simple controls, and a score-chasing gameplay loop, Bat Flapper is all about pushing a little farther each run while mastering on simple twist: You can’t dodge what you can’t hear... or can you?
store_data.detailed_description:
A 3D arcade runner where visibility is a resource.

Bat Flapper is a fast-paced 3D arcade runner where you survive by sound instead of sight. Race through dark cave tunnels as a bat, using echo location to send pulses of sonar to reveal obstacles hidden in the darkness.

Your sonar energy is always draining, and the only way to recharge it is by eating glowing bugs scattered throughout the cave. Reaching them often means leaving the safest path, forcing you to choose between playing it safe and risking the darkness, or diving into danger to keep your sonar alive.

With quick restarts, simple controls, and a score-chasing gameplay loop, Bat Flapper is all about pushing a little farther each run while mastering on simple twist: You can’t dodge what you can’t hear... or can you?
store_data.short_description: Fly as a bat through pitch-black caves where Echo-Location reveals danger. Eat glowing bugs to keep your passive sonar alive, dodge deadly obstacles, and chase high scores in a tense 3D arcade runner.

store_data.about_the_game:
THE DEVIL OWNS THE TABLE. YOU OWE THE RENT.


You have arrived at the worst casino imaginable. 

The Devil owns the table.

Your soul is collateral.

And every round, the rent goes up.

Aim your shot, drop the ball and watch it ricochet through the machine you have built. Every scoring peg it touches can earn money, multiply the payout, split the ball, redirect it, resurrect spent pegs or trigger something much worse.

Reach the quota and you survive another round.

Miss it and the House collects.

But unlike a normal pachinko machine, you build this one yourself.

THE BOARD IS THE BUILD

There is no shuffled deck deciding what happens once the ball starts moving.

You buy pegs.

You decide where they go.

And once placed, they become part of your machine.

Put a Bumper beneath a valuable cluster and launch the ball back through it.

Drop a Splitter above a Magnet and turn one ball into a swarm.

Surround Trapdoors with a Revenant and bring them back during the same drop.

Build elemental formations designed to detonate entire sections of the board.

Every placement changes what the next drop can become.

Across 100 hand-authored boards, layouts range from funnels and spirals to rings, lattices, skulls, coffins, crescents and other deliberately designed patterns. Each board has its own challenge, progression cap and personal record.

BUILD IMPOSSIBLE MACHINES

Your collection includes 20 peg types, from simple Coins and Bumpers to Portals, Magnets, Echoes, Splitters, Revenants and elemental pegs.

Different pegs don't just increase numbers. They change the physics and structure of the board.

  • Splitters multiply balls.

  • Magnets bend trajectories.

  • Portals send balls back into play.

  • Echoes repeat other peg effects.

  • Revenants revive spent Trapdoors.

  • Bumpers launch the ball back upward.

  • Fire, Spark, Earth and Water build elemental charge and reward completely different board shapes.

And in combat, Wards, Soul Wells and Skull pegs turn the same board-building system into a weapon.

YOUR DEMONS ARE YOUR BUILD

Beside the board sit five Arcana.

These aren't passive collectibles.

They activate from left to right, meaning their order is part of your strategy.

Adding to a multiplier before doubling it is very different from doubling it first.

Rearrange the same cards and you can create an entirely different scoring engine.

There are 16 Arcana, including Greed, Pride, The Fool, Death, Hydra, The Magician, The Serpent and The Twins, each with its own passive ability, upgrade paths and permanent power.

And eventually you face a cruel decision.

BURN THE CARD.

Every Arcana hides an Eternal Power.

To claim it, you must throw the card into the pit.

The card disappears.

Its slot becomes free.

But part of its power becomes permanent.

Burn Sloth and gain more drops every round.

Burn Pride and permanently increase your starting multiplier.

Burn Hydra and mutate Bumpers into Splitters.

Burn Death and even game over may not be the end.

The question isn't whether a powerful card should be sacrificed.

It's when.

95 UPGRADE PATHS

Pegs and Arcana don't have a single linear upgrade track.

They branch.

Increase raw Value.

Invest in Surge and reward long chaotic drops.

Raise Mint for double payouts.

Extend magnetic range.

Strengthen bumper force.

Improve Gambler odds.

Create additional Splitter balls.

Accelerate elemental charge.

Across the system are 95 upgrade paths, each five levels deep.

And because peg upgrades affect the entire peg type rather than a single object, upgrading Coins after building a board full of them can transform the entire machine at once.

SEVEN WAYS TO GO TO HELL

THE INDUCTION

A seven-chapter introduction that teaches the actual game by making you play it.

Learn placement, upgrades, Arcana order, burning, economy and combat before receiving your first permanent unlock grant.

THE SEVEN RINGS

Descend through a complete story campaign set across seven circles of casino-Hell.

Each ring represents a different vice and is ruled by the Arcana associated with it:

The Carnival of Folly
The Fool

The Banquet of Gluttony
Gluttony

The Hall of Sloth
Sloth

The Golden Vault
Greed and Usury

The Emerald Garden
Envy, Wormwood and The Serpent

The Court of Pride
Pride, Hubris and The Magician

The War Below
Wrath, Hydra and Death

The characters offering you power during a run are the same creatures waiting for you deeper below.

CLASSIC RUN

The pure Pegs of Hell experience.

Follow the Fate Trail, draft two pegs each round and construct the machine yourself while rent continues climbing.

BLIND PIT

No Fate Trail.

No draft.

Hell chooses two random pegs for you every round.

Build around whatever the Pit gives you.

PIT BOSS

Turn the game into an economy.

Bank your surplus.

Earn interest.

Buy pegs and upgrades from the Devil's shop.

Prices keep rising alongside the rent.

COLLECTIONS NIGHT

The rent collector has arrived.

Forget quotas.

Now your score is damage.

Enemies telegraph attacks before they happen, corrupt your board, block sockets, drain your Soul and force you to choose between building for maximum damage or sacrificing valuable board space for defence.

DAILY DESCENT

One seed.

One board.

One attempt.

The same challenge for everyone that day.

FATE IS VISIBLE

The golden trajectory you see while aiming isn't a vague approximation.

The game uses the same deterministic physics simulation for the prediction, the actual drop and replay.

If the Fate Trail says the ball will go somewhere, that is genuinely where it is heading.

Until your own board changes what happens next.

HELL REMEMBERS WHAT YOU EARN

Every dollar you've ever won contributes to permanent progression.

Use your lifetime winnings to unlock Rare and Legendary pegs and Arcana for future runs.

Your catalogues are presented as physical grimoires, containing every discovered peg and Arcana, their upgrades, maximum values and Eternal Powers.

Key Features

For the Steam feature section, I would make it much tighter than the long copy:

  • 100 hand-authored pachinko boards

  • 20 peg types that change scoring, physics, combat and elemental interactions

  • 16 Arcana with five active slots and player-controlled trigger order

  • 95 upgrade paths, each five levels deep

  • 16 Eternal Powers gained by permanently burning Arcana

  • 4 elemental systems built around different board formations

  • 7 game modes, including story, economy, combat and daily challenges

  • Seven-ring story campaign with 14 ring rulers

  • 6 debt collectors with telegraphed combat behaviour

  • Permanent progression funded by lifetime winnings

  • Deterministic physics with an accurate Fate Trail

  • 100 separate board records to master

  • 17 illustrated characters

  • Pixel-art casino-Hell presentation with a playable 3D cabinet and optional flat 2D view

store_data.about_the_game:
Enter the Backrooms. Find a way out.

Backrooms: Misstep is a first-person psychological horror game that sends you through a collection of strange, liminal environments where the rules are never quite what they seem.

Explore massive forgotten spaces, uncover objectives, avoid hostile entities, and learn the unique rules of each level as you search for a way forward.

From endless fluorescent hallways to deceptively peaceful neighborhoods, flooded environments, abandoned party rooms, and surreal rolling hills, every level introduces its own atmosphere, dangers, and mechanics.

EXPLORE THE UNKNOWN

Navigate interconnected rooms, hidden passages, false exits, and environments designed to make you question whether you are actually making progress.

SURVIVE UNIQUE ENTITIES

Different levels contain different threats. Learn how each entity behaves, when to run, when to hide, and when staying still might be your best option.

DISCOVER ORIGINAL LEVELS

Travel through a variety of Backrooms-inspired environments, each built around its own visual identity, objectives, and gameplay mechanics.

PLAY WITH A FRIEND

Experience the Backrooms together in online co-op as you explore, solve objectives, and try to survive what is waiting inside.

There is no guaranteed way out.

Just keep moving.

store_data.about_the_game:
Command a fleet on a frontier where five species are fighting over the same
ruins. Terran Dawn is an isometric space RTS: you mine asteroids, raise a
station from a single command core, research your way up a tech tree, design the
ships you fly, and take the fight to enemies doing exactly the same thing.

Five factions, five campaigns

84 missions across five campaigns, each following a different species — and each
playing differently.
  • Terran Federation — industrial, versatile, built around layered defence
    and point-defence interception.
  • Zythian — biological hulls and weapons that keep killing after the shot
    lands.
  • Mechanoid — machine assemblies, automated production and drone swarms.
  • Xenos — scavengers who salvage wrecks and reverse-engineer whatever they
    find into their own technology.
  • Voidborn — hardened shields and void weapons that strip protection off
    anything they touch.
Missions branch. Your choices change which map you see next, and briefings arrive
as transmissions from the officers who have to live with those decisions.

Build the war machine

Start with a command core and a handful of miners. Dock modules onto your
headquarters, plant forward bases across the map, feed refineries with ore and
salvage, and push a research tree that unlocks new hulls, weapons and abilities.
Everything you field has to be paid for first.

Design your own ships

Hulls are frames with slots. Fit weapons, shields, armour, reactors, utility and
hangar modules by slot size, from fighters to dreadnoughts and capital-class
super-capitals. Heavier ships hit harder and turn worse — mass is a real cost.

A frontier that fights back

Damaging nebulae, drifting ion storms, stealth minefields, shattered planets and
paired jump gates that move fleets across the map in a single move. Terrain is
not decoration.

Survival

Hold a position against escalating waves. Every run offers mutators and upgrades
that stack into a different build, with score multipliers that reward taking the
harder path.

Skirmish and multiplayer

Fight the AI on procedurally generated or handcrafted maps at the difficulty you
choose, or take it online. Team play with shared vision, in-game chat, map pings,
and reconnection if your connection drops mid-match.

Also included

  • Named save slots, achievements, and a full in-game encyclopedia.
  • Interface and text in English, German, Spanish, French and Hungarian.

store_data.about_the_game:
Carry the lantern. Build the warband. Outlast the road.


Starwood: Lantern is an asynchronous, day-based fantasy autobattler. Choose a hero, recruit minions and spells at Camp, arrange a seven-slot formation, and send your warband into automatic combat against rival runs. Every day asks a new question: spend now, upgrade your Camp, chase a synergy, or preserve the formation that is keeping you alive?

Build around your hero


Choose from 45 heroes with distinct powers and starting plans. Recruit across seven cultures—Concord, Lunari, Meridian, Lantern, Antler, Ashen, and Null—or combine them with Neutral cards to create flexible, unexpected builds.

Make every position count


Your board has seven slots. Attack order, adjacency, Shields, summons, Requiem effects, and start- or end-of-combat triggers can turn the same collection of minions into very different outcomes. Rearrange freely during recruitment, then watch the battle resolve.

Adapt over a full run


The Camp offers 238 live minions and spells across six tiers. Refresh the market, improve your Camp, freeze a promising offer, Discover new cards, and strengthen your board with 33 Blessings that can change the direction of a run.

A persistent casual account


Your casual account tracks run history, statistics, hero collection, and the Crownweights you earn in play. The optional Meridian Exchange lets players collect and trade hero variants using this valueless in-game currency. Export your Account key if you want to continue the same casual account on another device or in the web edition.

Current features


  • Asynchronous, day-based autobattler runs
  • 45 heroes and distinct hero powers
  • 178 minions and 60 recruit-phase spells
  • Seven-slot tactical formations and animated automatic combat
  • Seven cultures, Neutral cards, and six spell schools
  • 33 run-shaping Blessings
  • Persistent run archive, statistics, card collection, and hero collection
  • Manual Account key export/import for cross-device continuity

Starwood: Lantern requires a broadband internet connection. The Steam edition contains the casual game mode only.

store_data.about_the_game:
[Synopsis]

Living in an isolated freezing village, you are a hated woodcutter whose only emotional support is your wife and son. One day, during a "Werewolf Trial," you are framed for all crimes by a malicious conspiracy.

Execution is set for tomorrow morning.

If you do nothing, your beloved family will be slaughtered as accomplices. To let them escape, you choose to become the scapegoat, burning at the stake as the unloved "Werewolf". —But after death, a horrific scene unfolds before your spirit. You witness your surviving family become toys for the mastermind, hopelessly broken.

"I... I have to save them...!" Your overwhelming regret warps time itself, and you wake up again in the prison on the eve of execution. Beside you, the ghost of a medium watches and sneers. The ultimate choice.

A blood-stained loop. Can you find the true path to let your loved ones escape safely, even if it means sacrificing yourself?

[Features]

🔪 Cruel Multiple Endings through "Death Loops" Your choices branch the story into pure despair. Distance your family by dying hated, or plead the truth only to drive your son to massacre the village. Every choice matters.

🐺 A Death Game of "Self-Sacrifice" This is not a game about reasoning out the culprit. It's a new type of despair visual novel where you must figure out how to be correctly executed as the "culprit" while letting your family escape.

🩸 The "Truth" Beyond Despair Through repeated loops, the village's madness and the terrifying truth hidden within "yourself" will be revealed. What decision will you make for love?

"Even if the whole world hates you, as long as your beloved family is smiling"

Streaming & Video Policy

You are free to stream, record, and monetize this game.

No permission needed. No need to contact us. No restricted sections.

We ask for one thing only.

Please keep the truth route — and what it reveals — out of your thumbnails and titles.

Viewers choose what they watch. Nobody chooses what shows up in their feed.

This game was written for the moment a single fact turns over.

One line in a thumbnail is enough to end that moment for someone who hasn't played yet.

Inside the video, spoil as much as you like.

Official thumbnail assets are available for streamers.

About the translation

This is a one-person project, so every language other than Japanese was translated with the help of AI. I wrote a glossary and check consistency automatically, but no native speaker has proofread the text. If something reads wrong, tell me and I will fix it.

content_descriptors.notes:
This is a dark fantasy tragedy about a man condemned for a crime he did not commit.
The story deals with heavy subject matter throughout.

VIOLENCE
The game depicts execution by hanging, mob violence, stabbing, burning, poisoning, and
the killing of a child. One route includes combat with severe bodily injury. All of this
is conveyed through written prose and still character art. There is no animated gore.

SEXUAL CONTENT
There is no sexual imagery in this game. No nudity is depicted and no sexual act is ever
shown. Sexual content exists only as references in the text, and every instance is
presented as an act of harm:
- A past sexual assault (non-consensual sex) forms part of the story's background and is
  referred to in dialogue.
- A character is verbally degraded with sexual insults.
- A character works as a prostitute; coercion involving her is discussed.
- One route depicts sustained emotional abuse within a marriage.
None of this is presented approvingly or for titillation. The narrative consistently
frames these acts as cruelty, and the suffering they cause is the subject of the story.

OTHER SENSITIVE CONTENT
- Self-harm and a past suicide attempt are described by a character recalling his history.
- Alcohol is consumed on screen, mostly by characters abusing their authority.
- Wrongful conviction, false testimony, persecution by a mob, imprisonment, and child
  abuse are central themes.

The game does not glorify any of the above. Every act of violence and abuse is shown to
have consequences, and the story treats them as tragedy rather than spectacle.

store_data.about_the_game:
Backrooms: Insane is a first-person psychological horror and survival experience inspired by the unsettling universe of the Backrooms. Explore seemingly endless spaces, find a way to escape, and quickly discover that you are not alone.

Presented through a found footage aesthetic, the game is designed to make you feel as if you are watching recovered footage from someone who truly became trapped inside the Backrooms. The visuals, sound design, and environments are built to create a constant sense of isolation, vulnerability, and uncertainty.

Each level has its own rules, threats, and objectives. You will need to carefully explore your surroundings, find keys and important items, solve puzzles, activate mechanisms, and discover how to reach the next exit. But staying in one place for too long can have consequences.

AGAINST THE CLOCK

At different moments throughout the experience, timers and special events can completely change the behavior of a level. What begins as a seemingly calm exploration can suddenly turn into a race against time.

Countdowns may signal the beginning of a hunt, limit the amount of time you have to act, or warn you that something is about to change. When an entity begins chasing you, you will have to quickly decide whether to keep searching for your objective, hide, or run.

In certain situations, obtaining an important item or completing part of a level may cause the threat to stop being temporary. The entity will continue hunting you until you find the exit.

LEVEL CODES

Backrooms: Insane is designed to continue growing after release. Future updates will introduce new levels, each featuring its own mechanics, threats, objectives, and atmosphere.

To access certain additional levels, you will need to enter their corresponding number in the game's “Code” section.

At launch, Backrooms: Insane will include three additional levels accessible through codes:

Level 94 — Code “0094”

An unsettlingly familiar place that seems frozen in another era. Streets, houses, and seemingly peaceful environments hide a threat that becomes far more dangerous once night falls. Explore the area, find what you need to progress, and avoid drawing the attention of whatever inhabits this strange place.

Level 188 — Code “0188”

A massive, impossible-looking hotel filled with dark hallways, silent rooms, and spaces that seem to repeat endlessly. Exploration will be essential as you discover how to restore the hotel’s systems and find a way out, all while something roams its floors searching for you.

Level 931 — Code “0931”

An enigmatic and hostile level where the feeling of isolation becomes even stronger and the rules of the Backrooms seem increasingly unpredictable. Carefully observe your surroundings and search for an exit that changes its location every time the level is loaded. Understand the dangers around you and find your way out before it is too late.

These levels are part of a structure designed to expand over time. New codes and new levels will be added through future updates, gradually expanding the world of Backrooms: Insane.

EXPLORE. SURVIVE. ESCAPE.

Not every level works the same way. Each one introduces new environments, creatures, mechanics, and situations designed to keep you constantly uncertain about what might happen next.

Key Features

  • First-person psychological horror experience.

  • Cinematic found footage aesthetic.

  • Multiple levels inspired by the Backrooms.

  • Code system used to access additional levels.

  • New levels planned for future updates.

  • Hostile entities with different encounters and behaviors.

  • Temporary and permanent chase and hunt systems.

  • Timer and countdown mechanics that can alter the experience.

  • Exploration and the search for keys and essential items.

  • Puzzles and unique objectives required to escape each level.

  • Jumpscares and unexpected encounters.

  • Dark, oppressive environments designed to create constant tension.

  • Single-player experience.

In Backrooms: Insane, finding what you need is only part of the problem.

The real question is whether you will make it back alive.

store_data.about_the_game:
Battleships: FleetForge

A Roguelite reimagining of the classic game of Battleship. Command a fleet, hunt in the fog, and fight for one more level.

Escalating, Endless, Unforgiving

There's no fixed ending, only how far you can push. Every few levels, the enemy tier rises: bigger fleets, better-equipped ships, tougher fights. The grid grows to match. Your fleet grows too, if you can afford it, but every currency decision between rounds is a bet on what kind of fight is coming next.

Lose your whole fleet, or lose the ability to fight back entirely, and the run ends. Your reward, your fleet, your composition: it's all yours to build, level after level, for as long as you can hold the line.

Build a Fleet, Not Just a Ship

Every vessel in your fleet is a puzzle of its own. Bigger hulls carry more containers: more room to specialize, but a bigger target to hit. Every ship starts with the basics: an Engine to move, a Naval Gun to fire. What you equip beyond that is what turns a fleet of hulls into a fleet of specialists:

  • Engines & Naval Guns — stack them for more range, more reach, more firepower

  • Shields — absorb a set number of hits before breaking, protecting every system on board while they hold

  • Jammers — get struck without giving away your position, at the cost of the jammer's own strength

  • Sensors — pierce the fog and reveal what's lurking nearby before it's too late

... And MORE!

Drag, swap, and sell components between runs. Every choice in the shop is a trade-off between what you can afford and what your fleet actually needs to survive the next fight.

Features

  • Tactical grid combat — classic Battleship rules reforged into deep, turn-based tactics

  • Modular ship customization — Engines, Naval Guns, Shields, Jammers, and Sensors, mixed and matched across your fleet

  • True fog of war — nothing is revealed until you earn it

  • Endless, escalating progression — tiered difficulty that never stops climbing

  • A living battlefield — the grid itself degrades as fights stretch on

  • A build-your-run shop — buy ships, equip and swap components, gamble on a reroll

  • Captains — Unlock up to 5 different Captains with different passives for unique playstyle

  • Retro arcade presentation — CRT-inspired visual styling for a game built on a classic

How long can your fleet hold the line?

Demo vs Full Game

The demo gives you a taste of FleetForge’s core roguelite gameplay, while the full game expands on the experience with more content, progression, and components.

Demo

  • Limited Number of Levels

  • Limited Number of Components

  • No Rare Components

  • No Ability to Save Previous Run

  • Only 3 Captains 

Full Game

  • Unlimited Number of Levels

  • Up to 5 Levels of each Component

  • Rare Components

  • Ability to Save Previous Run

  • All 6 and future Captains

store_data.about_the_game:
You are unexpectedly transported to a cultivation world and become a regular disciple of the Immortal Spirit Sect.

One year later, an apocalyptic catastrophe descends, and all living beings under heaven and earth perish.

Yet death is not the end. Whenever the world is destroyed, you are sent back to the very moment you first arrived, starting a new cycle.

You attempt countless escapes. You travel to nearby cities, only to face annihilation once the time runs out. You try to cross the Monster‑infested Vast Ten‑Thousand Mountains, yet you fall in the wilderness before reaching distant lands.

Talk to sect senior brothers, gather secrets from NPCs, and unearth rare and precious treasures.

With clues gained from every cycle and accumulated power, you gradually uncover the truth behind this world‑ending calamity.

Game Features

• Real‑time combat cultivation gameplay: Built upon established wuxia‑cultivation action frameworks. Fight monsters and powerful foes in intense martial‑style battles.

• Time‑loop cycle mechanic: When the world ends, you return to the moment of your arrival. Your temporary combat power resets, but your cultivation aptitude improves and your inventory resources are preserved. Every failure becomes a chance to break fate.

• Multi‑path trial‑and‑error exploration: Different choices trigger distinct events. Talk with NPCs to unlock critical information and seek viable ways to survive the apocalypse.

Story Background

Transported into a cultivation realm, you strive to cultivate and pursue immortality — only for the end‑of‑world disaster to arrive.

You die again and again, only to wake back at your starting point.

Fleeing is not as simple as running away. Neither cities nor lofty mountains can shield you from total destruction.

Gather scattered fragments of knowledge across endless one‑year cycles, and search for the one single chance to survive.

store_data.about_the_game:
Hand Me The Splorch! is a fast-paced memory puzzle game based around getting your dad the tools he needs, and God help you if you're wrong.

Your Dad Needs Tools NOW! But Your Little Hands Can Only Carry So Much!

Remember tool locations and get them as fast as you can. Just remember that you have a very limited inventory (and you better put the tools back where you found them).

If You Think You Can Just Stand There And Watch Your Dad Do Everything, You Are Dead Wrong!

Fetching isn't enough. You're going to have to fix the electrics (rats keep getting into the damn thing), fill out paperwork (that lawyer just keeps calling), keep the slider centered (I don't even know what it does, but if it isn't perfect there'll be a problem), and more!

Be Quick on Your Feet!

Nobody ever organized this place, so the tools are scattered across many different locations in the garage. I hope your little legs carry you well.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Bots Want Your Gold! is a VR roguelite shooter in which you must defend your home base against a robotic horde intent on stealing all your valuable resources!

Mine ores and sell them to make quick cash. Use your hard-earned money to buy weapons, attachments, and equipment to help you defeat the bots! How long can you hold off the horde?

In The Bots Want Your Gold, equip 25+ different weapons that have access to their own unique pool of weapon mods. Build your weapons how you want, and for how you see fit. Want a sniper shotgun? Or a fully automatic sniper?
Go for it!

Use your weapons to take on waves and waves of robotic menaces, all desperate to take control of your property! Watch out though, as the bots have created specialised platforms designed to expose your weakness and force you to develop strategies on the fly.

How long can you survive? Can you defeat all threats, Land and Sky? When you hear the rumble of twin jet engines on the horizon... get ready...

store_data.about_the_game:
Wheat Awn: Line Zero is a single-player military-management game with turn-based card battles. A new campaign begins with two playable lessons. In battle, select a living enemy platoon, choose an officer and use one of that officer's available tactical cards; after your order resolves, the enemy takes its turn. In the Live-Fire Trial, move with WASD or the arrow keys and survive until the timer ends.

Go to the police station in Wheat Awn Town and speak to the Police Chief. Choose how long the trial will last, then dodge ricocheting boulders and machine-gun sweeps. Star Coins are added to the run every five seconds. Finish the timer to keep all of them. Death or early withdrawal erases only that run's earnings; coins owned before entering remain safe.

Use Star Coins in town to register each new group of 30 soldiers and form another platoon. Buy enough weapons for every soldier you deploy, together with medicine and special supplies. At the Academy, spend Star Coins to select officers. An officer can enter only courses matching their military attributes. Academy simulations provide both armies and their supplies, so they do not consume your inventory. Win a course and choose one of three tactical cards for that officer's field plan.

Return to the military compound, prepare your platoons and board the train. Every operation lists the required position, number of platoons and equipment before deployment. In battle, a tactical card works only when the deployed force contains the troops and equipment printed on it: infantry orders need armed infantry, armored orders need tanks, rocket orders need launchers, air orders need aircraft, and medical orders consume medicine. The Agent Radio reveals the enemy's next order and its effect, giving you a chance to prepare a counter.

The first nine warzones award promotions as your force grows from one 30-soldier platoon toward 729 platoons. Six final challenge warzones then test the army you built. Clear all 15 to finish the campaign; the ending records how many in-game days you needed.

store_data.about_the_game:
HYBRID LIFE-SIM RPG GAME

Dream City Psyche represents a unique approach to RPG game with pre-rendered 3D game world in top-down view perspective, open world city scale island, deep life-sim gameplay integration and tight integration of storyline. You can interact with the game world using point and click interface but there is option to use on screen direction pads or physical keyboard.

FOCUS ON SINGLE CHARACTER

You're playing as a single character throughout the game. You have the option to choose from 6 preset characters at the start of the game. Each character has their own unique abilities, skill bonuses and clothes.

MULTIPLE WAYS TO MAKE PROGRESS

The game doesn't use experience level to track progress like typical RPG game. Instead, progress in the game is tracked through several parameters - story (psychic control), career (work visa) and personality (determination and karma). You'll improve psychic control as you make progress throughout the game. If you care about career, improving work visa gives access to better job promotion.

Keep winning in combat to raise determination. Higher determination will allow you to earn HP bonus in combat. Do good deed to people such as donating will raise karma. Higher karma will allow you to earn bonus to roll chance in combat and many other things.

Despite of that, most of your time in the game will still be spent to improve skills. Performing action related to the skill or attending classes at schools will earn yourself experience points (XP). There are 20 skills which can be categorized into physical, tycoon, muse and analytical. Since improving skill points can take lots of time (you don't get XP from doing quests), focus on improving a few skills that's useful to you.

TIGHT STORYLINE INTEGRATION

There are a total of 20 quests in 4 separate acts (Prologue, Act 1, 2 and 3). Most quests revolves around investigation to uncover the mystery behind disappearances, murders and other things. The full story can be experienced in a single playthrough which can take around 8 to 10 hours to be completed.

The game starts with a long prologue to provide necessary background stories that could be helpful in later acts. When you arrived at Dream City, you have a mission to find your missing uncle. You'll meet a police detective to investigate murders. This will eventually leads to encounter with cultists. A guy managed to help you to reveal what really happened to your uncle - he is being kept at a place. You decided to join his group to be able to rescue your uncle.

The guy has a mission to storm the place where your uncle is being kept but he has a problem. A dangerous person has been guarding the entrance to the place. You'll volunteer to find his weakness. You'll meet many characters that either provide help or impede your progress. Your uncle left behind an important journal. You'll have to hunt several of the journal pages kept by a few people.

Eventually, you'll have to undertake an expedition to the underground city in order to find the last missing pages and unlock your last psychic ability. You'll discover the dangerous person's weakness. You'll use this information to bait him out and to beat him. With him out of the way, it is now possible to storm the place where your uncle is being kept. Will you be able to rescue your uncle?

In addition to talking to people, you'll discover stories by collecting up to 20 documents throughout the game. These documents provide lore and background details to help you make sense of why the events took place in the first place. It should be able to help you to connect lots of missing links between details.

OPEN WORLD CITY SCALE ISLAND

The game takes place in a city on a small island where you can have freedom to explore the whole island. The city is divided into 9 districts with more than 50 places to visit. Lots of effort have been made to create a living city.

Shopping district allows you to visit plenty of shops, cinema, art theatre and hypermarket. The hub of the city is city park where you can find night life entertainment (dance club or bar), plenty of schools and night market. Office district allows you to work at several office places such as ad agency, law firm, modelling agency or fashion firm or go to investment office to invest your cash. If you like nature, you can go to forest to forage or do some fishing.

The city changes dynamically every month in term of economy, crime and weather. Jewellery, house and company stock prices change based on economic condition. Because of the price changes, it is possible to make or lose money by taking advantage of the price changes. Crime will affect bad guys on the street. The crime can be so high that night curfew will be enforced throughout the month. Wet season means you'll see rain most of the time while going outside. When the city in plague, some places such as dance club or gym club are closed throughout the month.

There are 200+ generic characters you can talk to throughout the city. Their randomized response are based on their profile. Tourists will talk about tourist attraction, office workers will talk about office life, villagers will talk about forest and teenagers will talk about mischievous stuff. In addition to talk, it is possible to sell stuff to some of them to earn some money especially to characters on the street.

LIFE-SIM GAMEPLAY

You have to monitor energy, hunger, health, morale and hygiene bars at all time. Neglecting any of the bars could jeopardize your effectiveness in performing day to day life. Fortunately, these bars are easy to be taken care of due to close proximity of many places in the game.

There are a lot of job opportunities if you know where to look. You can take part-time jobs at the restaurants to earn side income. You have option to apply for a full-time job at several office places. You can dedicate a significant time to build the career. It is possible to get promoted all the way to the top as CEO.

There are plenty of ways to earn money without you working for people. You can buy a fishing rod from a guy and use it to fish at any 9 different fishing spots throughout the island. You can then sell the catch to the chef at sushi restaurant for some money. If you don't mind to get dirty, you can scavenge trash cans all over the island to look for scraps. You can then sell the scraps at the back of pawn shop for some money. You can walk around city park or forest to forage tree stumps for mushrooms. These mushrooms can be sold to villagers for some money.

You can rent to live at flat, apartment or condominium. You can buy 20 varieties of furniture or equipment and equip them at your home to unlock more activities such as sleeping, storing food, cooking and watching TV.

Even though you can buy meals from restaurants, cooking your own meals can save lots of money. You start with 22 recipes and can learn up to 66 recipes by taking part-time job at the restaurants or watching cooking show on TV. You can buy ingredients for the cooking from hypermarket, 24 hours shop, cake & pastry shop or night market stalls.

Even though the island is small, you can buy scooter and car to move faster between places. There are plenty of bus stops throughout the island to call for taxi or use bus service. Paying for taxi serves as fast travel to move between places. You can use free bus to move between districts.

If you have extra cash (more than $1,000), you can invest the money to buy jewellery and company stocks. The stuff will appreciate or depreciate in value at the start of month based on economic condition. The economic condition changes every month so it is possible to make money when the stuff appreciate in value. You can then sell the stuff to earn some profit.
store_data.detailed_description:
HYBRID LIFE-SIM RPG GAME

Dream City Psyche represents a unique approach to RPG game with pre-rendered 3D game world in top-down view perspective, open world city scale island, deep life-sim gameplay integration and tight integration of storyline. You can interact with the game world using point and click interface but there is option to use on screen direction pads or physical keyboard.

FOCUS ON SINGLE CHARACTER

You're playing as a single character throughout the game. You have the option to choose from 6 preset characters at the start of the game. Each character has their own unique abilities, skill bonuses and clothes.

MULTIPLE WAYS TO MAKE PROGRESS

The game doesn't use experience level to track progress like typical RPG game. Instead, progress in the game is tracked through several parameters - story (psychic control), career (work visa) and personality (determination and karma). You'll improve psychic control as you make progress throughout the game. If you care about career, improving work visa gives access to better job promotion.

Keep winning in combat to raise determination. Higher determination will allow you to earn HP bonus in combat. Do good deed to people such as donating will raise karma. Higher karma will allow you to earn bonus to roll chance in combat and many other things.

Despite of that, most of your time in the game will still be spent to improve skills. Performing action related to the skill or attending classes at schools will earn yourself experience points (XP). There are 20 skills which can be categorized into physical, tycoon, muse and analytical. Since improving skill points can take lots of time (you don't get XP from doing quests), focus on improving a few skills that's useful to you.

TIGHT STORYLINE INTEGRATION

There are a total of 20 quests in 4 separate acts (Prologue, Act 1, 2 and 3). Most quests revolves around investigation to uncover the mystery behind disappearances, murders and other things. The full story can be experienced in a single playthrough which can take around 8 to 10 hours to be completed.

The game starts with a long prologue to provide necessary background stories that could be helpful in later acts. When you arrived at Dream City, you have a mission to find your missing uncle. You'll meet a police detective to investigate murders. This will eventually leads to encounter with cultists. A guy managed to help you to reveal what really happened to your uncle - he is being kept at a place. You decided to join his group to be able to rescue your uncle.

The guy has a mission to storm the place where your uncle is being kept but he has a problem. A dangerous person has been guarding the entrance to the place. You'll volunteer to find his weakness. You'll meet many characters that either provide help or impede your progress. Your uncle left behind an important journal. You'll have to hunt several of the journal pages kept by a few people.

Eventually, you'll have to undertake an expedition to the underground city in order to find the last missing pages and unlock your last psychic ability. You'll discover the dangerous person's weakness. You'll use this information to bait him out and to beat him. With him out of the way, it is now possible to storm the place where your uncle is being kept. Will you be able to rescue your uncle?

In addition to talking to people, you'll discover stories by collecting up to 20 documents throughout the game. These documents provide lore and background details to help you make sense of why the events took place in the first place. It should be able to help you to connect lots of missing links between details.

The game takes place in a city on a small island where you can have freedom to explore the whole island. The city is divided into 9 districts with more than 50 places to visit. Lots of effort have been made to create a living city.

store_data.about_the_game:
EVOLUTION WITHOUT WAITING

That was SynTech's slogan. By 2053, seventy percent of humanity had bought it: neural interfaces, cognitive amplifiers, full-body Convergence systems, all held together by a SynTech bonding agent called NexuGel. Flesh and machine, seamlessly married. Progress you didn't have to wait a few million years for.

Dr. Eliza Chen was the first person to step inside the Genesis Chamber. Within forty-eight hours she could distribute her own consciousness through quantum entanglement and simulate the future with uncomfortable precision. What came out of her didn't spread blindly. It moved wirelessly, through the augmentation protocols themselves, and it waited - striking at the exact moment its models said would work best.

That was six months ago.

THREE KINDS OF SURVIVORS

PURISTS

Refused the technology back when there was no reason to. Being right about the largest question of the century has not made most of them pleasant company, and they have little patience for anyone who had to be cut clean.

DISCONNECTED

Augmented, until somebody took it out of them. Gutters worked out of abandoned buildings and makeshift labs with salvaged instruments, charging whatever the desperate could pay. Most patients survived. Most came out crippled. One man's implant had fused to his Broca's area; when they cut it free they took his speech with it, and he has understood every word spoken to him since without being able to answer one. He'll tell you it was worth it. No more Signal whispering in his skull.

IMMUNES

Rare, and alive by accident. A manufacturing defect, an illegal modification, an implant that never worked properly to begin with. The virus reached for them and found nothing to hold onto.

THE OPERATIVES

        Butchers hold the line.                             Hacksmiths keep the gear running.                         Mindrippers fix people.

BUTCHER: Ex-SynTech security, veteran of the Resource Wars, long since used to being torn apart and stitched back together. A laser fried his neural implant and melted part of his brain along with it. It's a wonder he can still do simple math. His shotgun doesn't require any.


HACKSMITH: An engineer who has spent his whole life inside other people's machines. He runs on gadgets, internal and external, and turns enemy systems against their owners. His problem was never competence. It's that he genuinely believes he's the smartest thing left alive.


MINDRIPPER: A therapist whose years in the field left her psychotic, and whose tumors, mercifully non-lethal, left her able to alter physical reality. She found out on a patient hiding a pirated implant, and the room was still raining blood when she caught herself laughing. Push it too far and her own head goes the same way.




THE GEAR

Over 30 weapons within 7 categories

Pistols, SMGs and assault rifles: the reliable spine of any loadout

Shotguns: close, loud, and the fastest way to remove a limb

Machine guns: including spin-up gatlings that demand you commit to a firing position before the barrels are even turning

Sniper rifles: up to an experimental antimatter platform

Energy weapons: the largest category in the game, salvaged from Quantum Arms Incorporated research: lasers, plasma, electrical, and a singularity cannon that folds space where it lands

Explosives and flamethrowers: for when the corridor matters more than the target

Friendly fire at 50% on Fleshbuilder, 100% on Apex difficulty. At the top, your own rounds are exactly as lethal as theirs. All NPCs can be killed at any time.

Penetration mechanics: rounds pierce multiple targets based on caliber and material, with damage falloff

100+ different armor pieces: Fitting in seven armor slots: backpacks, helmets, harnesses, chest, gloves, belts, boots, giving flat and percentage reduction applied against the body part actually hit while providing slot specific bonuses like increased ammo stack sizes, reload speeds, carry capacity, movement bonses and more.

NO TWO DROPS ARE THE SAME

Every weapon, armor piece and augmentation is generated randomly when it drops. Base item, rarity tier, then a randomized set of attributes pulled from deep stat pools, eighteen for weapons alone, more for armor, with no duplicates on a single item. Two rifles of the same model and the same rarity is near impossible to have the same stat rolled on them.



PUT IT BACK IN

The world ended because of augmentations. You'll be bolting them back in anyway. Endo implants integrated through NexuGel, Exo grafts fused to the frame, targeting optics, cortical accelerators, servo filaments woven through your tendons. More slots unlock through the skill trees. The best ones carry real drawbacks: sharper criticals for a narrower field of view, until you're lethal and half blind.

WHAT'S LEFT OF EVERYONE ELSE

Eleven enemy types, in the order the virus built them:
                   Zombies                                          Sprinters                                     Harvested                            Fleshdrones

                                                                                                                                                                                                             Apex Fleshgrinder
                                                                    Little is known about the Apex

                                                                    entities, for there is barely anyone

                                                                    left alive who met them and survived

                                                                                   to tell the tale

TAKE THEM APART

Damage is tracked per body part. Put enough trauma through a limb and it comes off, while the thing it belonged to is still alive and closing in on you. Headshots splatter. Explosions take several at once. Severed parts are thrown with real force and stay where they land, permanently.

THE DEMO

A tutorial and the first two mission areas, and the full combat, loot, augmentation and progression systems. Fleshgrinder is in active development with no release date yet.
