store_data.about_the_game:
Your shop. Your cauldron. Your cat.

Cozy Brew is a single screen potion shop where everything you need is one

click away. The cauldron simmers by the window, the alembic drips quietly on

the counter, and somewhere in the room Kevin the cat is asleep on something

important.

Buy ingredients through the crystal ball, toss them in the pot, and see what

comes out. Bottle your work, stock the chest, and fill orders for a village

that always needs one more tonic before sundown.

Three stations, one craft

  • The Cauldron brews raw ingredients into potions, from calming draughts to bottled storms.

  • The Alembic refines potions into stronger forms, and combines two into something new entirely.

  • The Mortar grinds ingredients down into dusts, oils, and sparks that unlock the deeper recipes.

Every recipe you learn is written into a book that actually feels like a

book, with parchment pages, ink, and a count of every batch you have ever

made.

Learn it your way

Choose how recipes come to you when you start a new brew, just click the mode title to switch when starting a new game:

  • Discovery is the intended way to play. Nothing is handed over. Experiment at your stations and earn every page in your book.

  • Extra Cozy keeps a recipe seller in the crystal ball for a gentler, spoiler friendly pace.

Grow the shop

Fill jobs for the village to earn gold and reputation across 50 shop levels.

New ingredient tiers unlock as word spreads, jobs grow richer, and upgrades

make the work smoother: a faster stir, a bigger chest, a vial station that

bottles finished brews on its own.

And when your craft finally reaches the palace, His Majesty has a request.

Four masterworks, fused into one. Finish it and you finish the story.

Meet Kevin

The shop comes with a cat. This is not negotiable. Kevin roams the room,

naps where he pleases, and can be dressed in hats and collars that he

tolerates with great dignity. Petting him is an achievement. Obviously.

A shop worth sitting in

  • 85 recipes across cauldron, alembic, and mortar

  • 66 potions and 50 ingredients across five tiers

  • 30 achievements, including one for the truly dedicated

  • 16 track original cozy soundtrack, played on an in game gramophone

  • Street life outside the windows, candlelight inside, and rain on the glass

  • Three save slots with play time tracking

  • A complete story you can finish in an evening, and a post game shop that stays open as long as you like

store_data.about_the_game:
Paint the arena. Tag the other team. Try not to face-plant.

Splatastrophe is a fast, funny third-person paint-combat game where blue and orange teams turn every arena into a spectacular mess. Sprint into trouble, slide under incoming paint, dolphin-dive through the chaos, and cover the battlefield before the other team does.

Three Ways to Make a Mess


  • Turf War — Cover more of the arena in your team's paint before time runs out.
  • Death Match — Tag the opposing team and race for the highest score.
  • Secure Zones — Paint and control key areas while the other team tries to steal them back.

Bring Your Paint Crew


Create a Steam party for up to five players, invite friends through the Steam overlay, or jump into a public online match. Bots keep the paint flying when the roster needs filling.

Move Like You Meant To Do That


Chain sprints, slides, jumps, and gloriously undignified dolphin dives to cross paint-covered arenas. Friendly paint helps you move; enemy paint makes every escape more awkward.

Pick Your Particular Kind of Chaos


Choose from distinct paint weapons, swap character styles, and take the fight across four arenas built for close calls, ridiculous dives, and last-second comebacks.

No blood. No grim battlefield speeches. Just two teams, too much paint, and a rapidly disappearing clean floor.

store_data.about_the_game:
You're a rabbit in a field full of rocks. The wolves are already moving.

Poggers can't fight. He can't outrun a wolf. What he can do is shove rocks — one at a time or

a whole row at once — and a wolf with a rock on every side isn't a wolf any more. It's a carrot.

That's the entire game, and it's the whole game: read the field, herd the pack, seal them in.

Clear the board and the next one is bigger, faster, and has more teeth in it.

Box them in

Wolves path straight at you every second or so. Rocks don't move on their own, and they never

move toward you. Every trap you build has to be built in the gaps the pack leaves you — and

they close those gaps fast. Catch two wolves in the same wall and the score doubles.

The carrots are bait for you, not them

A trapped wolf leaves a carrot. Carrots are pure bonus points — but the level ends the instant

the last wolf goes down, so anything you haven't eaten by then is gone. Grab it now with the

pack still loose, or play it safe and leave money on the field. Your call, every level.

The steak is bait for them

Shove thirty rocks and a packaged steak drops somewhere on the board. Wolves won't touch it

while it's wrapped. Pick it up and Poggers carries it, lit up in aqua — then hit SPACE to tear

it open and drop it. Every wolf close enough to smell it forgets about you and goes for the

meat, and a wolf with its head down eating is a wolf that isn't moving.

Drop it and run. If you're still standing on it when they arrive, they're not stopping for the

steak.

It gets worse on purpose

- More wolves, faster, as the levels climb — five breeds, each with its own pace

- Sinkholes from level five: shove a rock in and it's gone for good, so every wall you

build costs you material you might need later

- Endless levels — the board is generated fresh every time, so there's no memorizing a

solution, only getting better at reading one.

Built to sit on your desktop

Every standard resolution from 640×360 to 4K, windowed or full screen on a key press, separate

master / music / effects volume, and settings that remember themselves. It launches at about

half your monitor size and stays out of your way.

---

Feature bullets (for the short bullet block)

- Push rocks to box in the wolf pack — trap two at once to double the score

- Trapped wolves leave carrots: bonus points you have to earn before the level ends

- Steal a steak, drop it as bait, and watch the pack turn on the meat instead of you

- Sinkholes that eat your rocks and never give them back

- Endlessly generated levels — more wolves, faster wolves, every time you clear one

- Every standard resolution up to 4K, instant full screen, full volume control

A fast arcade puzzler in the spirit of old school casual commercial games, with endless levels that get meaner every time you clear one.

store_data.about_the_game:
Britain has fallen into chaos. Rule your kingdom, conquer rival lands, and make difficult decisions as you work to unite the realm. At the Round Table, knights, nobles, clergy, family members, and ordinary people will bring problems that demand your judgment.

Every decision affects four pillars of your kingdom: Faith, People, Army, and Wealth. Keep them in balance, or your kingdom will descend into chaos. Meanwhile, command your armies, expand your territory, and face rival kingdoms as each year brings new challenges.

Death is not the end. When your king falls, enter Avalon and face a trial for the chance to return. Discover legendary artifacts, strange events, changing weather, and unexpected challenges along the way.

Will you unite Britain and fulfill Arthur's destiny, or will your kingdom fall into chaos?

Features:

Rule the Kingdom

Balance Faith, People, Army, and Wealth as every decision shapes your kingdom.

Make Difficult Decisions

Face knights, nobles, clergy, family, and commoners at the Round Table. Every choice has consequences.

Conquer Britain

Train soldiers, command your armies, and conquer rival territories to unite the kingdom.

Survive Your Own Death

Enter Avalon after death and face a trial for the chance to return to your kingdom.

Discover Legendary Artifacts

Seek out Excalibur, the Holy Grail, and other magical artifacts with unique powers.

Face the Unexpected

Encounter changing weather, mini-games, strange events, and unexpected challenges.

Face Mordred

When Mordred rises against you, everything you have built will be put to the test.

store_data.about_the_game:
A 200 PLAYER WAR FOR ONE AMERICAN VALLEY

The Cold War ended the other way.

The United States did not lose a battle. It lost a bet. The men who owned its energy and its

appetite decided the future belonged to the other system, and by the time anyone noticed, the

country had been signed over from the inside. What stands now is a captured America: the

Soviet backed USSA, its federal stencil on every hood, against the Homegrowns, an internationally

supported resistance with no factory of its own and no intention of stopping.

Main Street has a propaganda billboard on it. The diner is still open. The war is two years old

and it is not going anywhere.

Internal Conflict is a large scale military simulation for 200 players on one persistent front.

It is a shooter first, a sandbox game second, and it means both of those completely.

WHAT YOU ACTUALLY DO

You spawn at a barracks that belongs to you, draw a weapon that a player physically delivered

there, get moved to a contested position by a driver who chose that job on purpose, and fight over

a strip of ground with a hundred other people on your side. Then you hold it, or you lose it, and

the line on the map moves for everyone in the war, including the people who log in after you leave.

Every system below exists to serve that one sentence.

ONE WAR, NOT A MATCH

There is no queue, no lobby, no countdown, no round timer. You join a war already in progress and

it keeps running after you log off. The front you left is the front you come back to.

A war can still be won. Push the other side three full levels of advance out of the region and that

war ends. It is deliberately built to resist snowballing, so the honest shape of a war is a

grinding stalemate that heaves back and forth for days, punctuated by pushes that cost something.

THE FRONT, AND HOW IT MOVES

The live battlespace is a band of ground twenty kilometers wide that slides north and south across

the valley as the fighting moves. Seven zones are contested inside it at any one time.

  • Three points per zone.[/b] Hold two of the three and the zone begins ticking over to you.

  • Thethird starts to flip once it goes uncontested. More bodies standing on a point takes it faster.

  • Five of seven shifts the war.

  • Hold five zones and the entire front steps one square in your favor, headquarters and all.

  • built on it. An advance hands you a raw position and the job of digging in all over again.

The commander of each faction designates which positions in a sector become that faction's zones,

so the map is a live planning surface rather than a scoreboard.

LOGISTICS WINS WARS

There are no tickets. Nothing is conjured.

Spawns, weapons, ammunition and equipment are physically delivered from headquarters and supply

nodes before anyone can spawn or draw gear at a position. Every category carries its own count, and

spawning burns from it. Starving a base is not a metaphor here. It is the actual way you choke a

faction out of a sector.

That makes the supply run a frontline job. Cutting a road matters as much as winning the firefight

on it. The truck driver wins wars too, and the game keeps the receipts.

COMMAND AND SQUADS

A full chain runs from Commander to Platoon Leader to Squad Leader to squad, named to each

faction's own doctrine. Squads carry the fight. Leadership is a job with actual authority over

where the faction's effort goes, not a cosmetic badge.

[h2]DIG IN[/h2]

Grab a hatchet. Drop trees. Build fortifications and dig trenches where you need them, not where

the map says you may. Experience earned from deliveries into a base buys builds and upgrades at

that base, so a position's shape is a record of the work players poured into it. Two weeks into a

war, the signature of a front is entirely what the players put there.

HOME IS A PLACE

Headquarters is a barracks with your bunk, your footlocker and your armory, per player, per squad

and per platoon. Spawning forward at a contested position is deliberately the opposite: fast,

functional, characterless. One is somewhere to come back to. The other is a foothold.

DEATH, RESCUE AND CAPTURE

Dying costs you something without ending your evening. Gear and cosmetic items degrade and drop,

and an item that dies twice is gone from the world permanently, so the good stuff genuinely

circulates and genuinely runs out.

Anyone can revive anyone, including enemies. You can restrain and capture a player instead of

killing them, which turns a losing firefight into a negotiation, a prisoner, and a story nobody

scripted.

PROGRESSION THAT NEVER BUYS A KILL

Your character persists and improves across every war you fight in: lockpicking, hotwiring,

crafting speed, stamina, and other quality of life skills that make you a more useful person on

the field.

Nothing you unlock, earn, grind or buy will ever give you a combat advantage. That is a design law

we wrote down before we wrote the game, not a launch window promise.

LOOT THE COLLAPSE

Late eighties American arsenals meet Soviet bloc steel. Your faction's patron decides your standard

kit, your uniforms, your vehicles and the look of every town it holds.

Then there is everything the country left lying around. Homes, hideouts and back rooms across the

valley hold rare and strange weapons from a place that stopped moving in 1989. Some are practical.

Some are legends. All of them can be taken off your body by whoever kills you.

THE JOURNALIST

A neutral third faction plays the war unarmed.

Journalists spawn at either faction's base, at neutral press locations and in towns, and they earn

from what they actually get on camera: a kill in frame, a capture in frame, a revive, an interview,

a surrender, a flag changing hands. That money can fund a squad to go take an objective so there is

something worth filming. Protection without invincibility, and a completely different game living

inside the same war.

ONE REAL VALLEY, 194 SQUARE MILES OF IT

A twenty by twenty four kilometer slice of the Tennessee River valley west of Chattanooga, built to

scale from real elevation data. Five million trees. Hundreds of miles of real roads. Appalachian

ridges, river flats, towns you fight through building by building, and one enormous bridge everyone

will learn to fear.

It is one map because it is one war. You will know this valley the way you know a neighborhood.

HOW LONG IS A SESSION

As long as you want it to be. Twenty minutes is a supply run that keeps a sector breathing. Two

hours is holding a zone through three assaults. A war runs for days across thousands of player

sessions, and it does not need you present to continue. Drop in, matter, log off, come back and

find the map changed.

FREE TO PLAY. PLAY FOR FREEDOM.

The entire game is free. Both factions, the journalist, every role, every weapon, every vehicle,

the whole valley and every system described on this page are included at no cost and stay that way.

Purchases are cosmetic only and never touch combat. No premium ammunition, no paid progression, no

paid access to a faction or a piece of ground, no fine print.

Come hold the line.

we wrote down before we wrote the game, not a launch window promise.

LOOT THE COLLAPSE

Late eighties American arsenals meet Soviet bloc steel. Your faction's patron decides your standard

kit, your uniforms, your vehicles and the look of every town it holds.

Then there is everything the country left lying around. Homes, hideouts and back rooms across the

valley hold rare and strange weapons from a place that stopped moving in 1989. Some are practical.

Some are legends. All of them can be taken off your body by whoever kills you.

THE JOURNALIST

A neutral third faction plays the war unarmed.

Journalists spawn at either faction's base, at neutral press locations and in towns, and they earn

from what they actually get on camera: a kill in frame, a capture in frame, a revive, an interview,

a surrender, a flag changing hands. That money can fund a squad to go take an objective so there is

something worth filming. Protection without invincibility, and a completely different game living

inside the same war.

ONE REAL VALLEY, 194 SQUARE MILES OF IT

A twenty by twenty four kilometer slice of the Tennessee River valley west of Chattanooga, built to

scale from real elevation data. Five million trees. Hundreds of miles of real roads. Appalachian

ridges, river flats, towns you fight through building by building, and one enormous bridge everyone

will learn to fear.

It is one map because it is one war. You will know this valley the way you know a neighborhood.

HOW LONG IS A SESSION

As long as you want it to be. Twenty minutes is a supply run that keeps a sector breathing. Two

hours is holding a zone through three assaults. A war runs for days across thousands of player

sessions, and it does not need you present to continue. Drop in, matter, log off, come back and

find the map changed.

FREE TO PLAY. PLAY FOR FREEDOM.

The entire game is free. Both factions, the journalist, every role, every weapon, every vehicle,

the whole valley and every system described on this page are included at no cost and stay that way.

Purchases are cosmetic only and never touch combat. No premium ammunition, no paid progression, no

paid access to a faction or a piece of ground, no fine print.

Come hold the line.
store_data.short_description: A 200-player war for one American valley. The Cold War ended the other way, and in 1999 the former USA is at war with itself. One persistent front across a real 20 x 24 km Tennessee river valley: dig trenches, haul supplies, hold the line. Free to play. Never pay to win.

store_data.about_the_game:
Spell Cards aren’t drawn from a deck—they’re ingredients you combine into new magic.

Discover powerful spells through different recipes, then wield your creations as you climb the Tower of Starlight.

Ray came to the tower for one reason to bring her missing mother home. But when she was caught in the tower’s magic, most of the power she carried was scattered. Now she must recover her lost magic as she climbs.

  • Recover Your Scattered Magic

Collect basic elemental Spell Cards as you climb the tower. Combine two cards through different

recipes to discover new magic, ranging from simple tactical tools to powerful spells.

Spell Cards are not a combat deck that gets shuffled before every battle. They are ingredients used

to create stronger magic. The first time you combine a spell, it is recorded in your Spell Library.

Review its recipe, gather the right materials during a future expedition, and craft the spell again

when you need it.

  • Fight with Four Elements

Build Burn with Ember and overwhelm your enemies. Recover and disrupt the enemy’s plans with Aqua.

Endure incoming attacks and strike back with Terra, or build Echo with Gust to unleash repeated

damage.

Combine elements, read enemy intents, and manage your Action Points, HP, and MP. With limited Action

Points each turn, decide whether to attack, defend, craft a spell, use a consumable, or meditate.

  • Find Your Own Way Up the Tower

Choose your next destination along paths filled with battles, elite encounters, events, shops, rest

sites, Card Sanctuaries, treasure chests, and bosses.

Collect relics and consumables, rearrange your active and reserve spells for the situation ahead,

and prepare for the next battle. Even the same path can demand a different solution depending on the

spells, relics, and choices you discover.

  • Growth That Remains Between Expeditions

When you complete an expedition, combine the Spell Cards you earn to discover spells that remain

recorded in your Spell Library. Use the Memory Shards gathered during your expeditions to strengthen

Ray, and work with Sally to expand the support and starting choices available on future attempts.

Return to the Wanderers’ Garden, meet the people gathered there, and prepare a new strategy before

entering the tower again.

  • Confront the Memories Left in the Tower

People say the Tower of Starlight reveals what has been lost.

In Ray’s memories, her mother was endlessly kind. Ray climbs with only the belief that her mother is

somewhere inside the tower. But the higher she goes, the traces she discovers begin to point toward

a truth that conflicts with her warm memories of childhood.

In Text Shelter, you can explore multiple regions, each with different resources and enemies. Start with easier areas and work your way up.

Use the materials you gather to build your shelter. Construct buildings with different functions, and expand your land to fit more structures.

In this world of words — stay alive, and keep going.

store_data.about_the_game:
Rain has not stopped for as long as anyone can remember. Four survivors, one shelter, thirty nights. Build it up during the day. Hold it together after dark.

The Gunner shoots. The Gunner cannot build a single wall.

The Engineer builds, mines, and repairs. The Engineer cannot fire a single shot.

A Gunner alone will run out of ground to stand on. An Engineer alone will watch their fortress get chewed through. You are not two players doing the same job faster. You are two halves of one survivor.

Chop wood. Break stone. Decide where the wall goes, how many turrets you can afford, and whether the campfire is worth the materials tonight. The day is on a timer, and it is never quite long enough. Every choice you make before sunset is a choice you will live with after it.

The light drains out of the world and they come from every direction. Twenty monster types, each one asking for a different answer. Some flood you with numbers. Some close the distance before you can react. Some ignore you entirely and go for your walls. On certain nights, something much larger arrives.

Every level up offers three cards. Piercing rounds, critical strikes, multishot, and more. Twenty three cards means no two runs play the same way.

Gold carries over into permanent upgrades. Records carry over into unlocks. Reach day seven, kill three hundred enemies, take down three bosses, clear all thirty nights. Each milestone widens the card pool itself, so your tenth run is a different game from your first.

Online co-op for up to 4 players through Steam. Drop in with friends in one click.

30 day campaign with a real ending, not an endless score chase.

20 monster types and multiple boss encounters.

23 run cards, permanent upgrades, and record based unlocks.

Hand made pixel art with dynamic day and night lighting.

Full support for English, Korean, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese.

store_data.about_the_game:
Lace Up Your Boots and Take to the Trail

Adventure called, and you answered! In your excitement, you arrive at the trailhead with no supplies beyond your backpack. Fortunately, with some perseverance and a bit of luck, you’ll be able to find everything you need along the way.

Discover the World Off Trail

As you wander alongside calm streams, shady forests, and peaceful meadows, you generate your world. No two walks are the same and each playthrough is unique. Will you discover a forgotten castle, weave through a slot canyon, or spot a rare bird? The only way to know what’s out there is to go and see it for yourself. Just keep an eye on your energy, so your hike doesn’t end before the trail does.

Wander Your Way

Where you explore and how you spend your time is up to you. Will you specialize in one area or become a jack-of-all-trades? Will you speed to the trail end or discover all the secrets the land offers? The choice is yours.
  • Rest at a campsite, searching for constellations as you roast a marshmallow over the fire.
  • Cast your line for fish to fuel your hike or dive into the water yourself.
  • Create paintings, sketches, and sculptures inspired by the nature you see.
  • Forage for fresh berries and herbs to eat as they change through the seasons.
  • Spot shapes in the clouds and patterns in the falling leaves.
  • Climb to the mountain peaks and treetops to get a greater view of the wonders around you.
Get ready to wander. Wishlist Wanderbound on Steam to stay updated!

Saber World League VR is a physics-based 1v1 melee combat game built exclusively for VR. Step into the arena and fight for real — every hit registers by the actual force and speed of your swing, not a canned animation, so victory comes down to your own timing, positioning, and power.

Choose your weapon — swords, sledgehammers, knives, and more, each with multiple models — then pick and save your robot avatar to bring into any game mode.

Features:

  • Ranked PvP — Get matched with online players in 1v1 physics-based duels and climb the leaderboards

  • Play with Friends — Generate a match code and share it with a friend to duel them directly, no matchmaking needed

  • Practice / Playground — A sandbox mode to test out weapons and get a feel for the physics before jumping into ranked matches

  • Multiple Weapon Types — Fight with swords, sledgehammers, knives, and more, each with its own weight and feel

  • Robot Avatars — Select and save your own robot avatar, used across every mode

  • Play room-scale or standing — built for tracked motion controllers with support for both play styles for maximum immersion and instant response

store_data.about_the_game:
Neverrest is a cozy, nostalgic idle RPG built around steady progression, deep character builds, and a world that keeps moving even while you are away.

Create a roster of heroes, send them into dangerous zones, and watch them battle automatically—or take control by activating skills, changing equipment, and choosing where they train. Your active hero and benched characters can continue earning experience, gold, materials, and equipment through background and offline progression.

BUILD YOUR ROSTER

Choose from five classic starting classes: Warrior, Archer, Mage, Acolyte, and Thief. Develop each hero through class skills, specialized talent trees, powerful equipment, and level-50 class promotions.

CREATE DEEP BUILDS

Hunt equipment with individual quality rolls, refine and enchant your favorite gear, collect socketable Monster Cards, unlock passive bonuses through the NeverDex, and combine skills and talents to create distinct builds.

EXPLORE AND GROW

Travel through a growing world of combat zones, monsters, quests, Elite enemies, and increasingly difficult challenges. Revisit cleared areas through Empowered Hunts or test your strongest build against Sir Splinters in the 60-second DPS Training Lab.

BUILD A LIFE IN NEVERREST

Return to town to cook lasting food buffs, craft and improve equipment at the Gearsmith, trade with the Merchant, manage shared storage, complete daily quests, raise pets, and prepare your roster for the next expedition.

PROGRESS YOUR WAY

Neverrest is designed for both active and idle play. Check in for a few minutes, optimize every detail, or let your heroes continue working while you are away. There is always another level, item, card, recipe, talent, or class upgrade waiting.

store_data.about_the_game:
Akos is a co-op open-world dark fantasy RPG built around a single relationship. You raise a dragon, and it does not turn out the same for everyone: a personality system reads how you actually treat it and shapes the creature you end up with. Once it is grown, you fly it. Play alone, or alongside a friend raising a dragon of their own.

THE DRAGON IS THE GAME

A creature you are responsible for, that grows over the course of the game, and that ends up different depending on what you did.

The personality system reads how you actually live: what you feed it, how you fight beside it, what you choose when it is watching. Two players can play the same number of hours and end up with genuinely different creatures.

A WORLD WITH NO ROOM FOR YOU

Both of the gods who made this world are dead, and neither of the races they left behind has forgiven the other for it. The empire that inherited the mortal plane now burns its own villages over a strip of forest and calls it faith.

You begin with nothing. No name, no family, no house to answer to. Nobody is coming.

Dragons cannot be replaced. The god who shaped them died before it occurred to him they might need to reproduce, so every one still breathing is one of the last there will ever be.

AN OPEN WORLD THAT BITES BACK

Explore, hunt, and survive in a kingdom tearing itself apart, with progression for you and for the dragon. The empire's provinces are at each other's throats and the war does not care that you are in it. Encounters are built around fighting as a pair, so the creature beside you has to be part of how you win.

BETTER WITH A FRIEND

Full co-op throughout. Your friend's dragon is their own, with a temperament their choices caused rather than yours. Two riders, two creatures that should not exist, and eventually a kingdom that wants them both dead.

KEY FEATURES

  • A dragon that becomes its own creature. A personality system driven by how you treat it, not by a loyalty meter you fill.

  • Wingbeat-driven flight. Flap, glide, dive, and flare, with mounted flight and aerial combat.

  • Full co-op. Every system replicates. Your friend raises their own dragon with its own temperament.

  • Growth you can see. The dragon changes in size and capability over the course of the game, and how you play changes with it.

  • Survive and explore. Hunt, gather, and feed in an open world that does not hand you anything.

  • RPG progression for both of you. You get stronger. You never get stronger than the dragon.

  • A world with real history. Warring provinces, a cursed empire, and a race of dragons that cannot replace its dead.

Akos is in active development by two people. Wishlist to follow along!

store_data.about_the_game:
A QUIET PUZZLE AMONG THE STARS

Under A Turning Sky is a meditative celestial puzzle game about finding harmony in alignment.

Rotate planets along their orbit rings, bring their positions and seasons into balance to create a path that carries a lone signal across the systems, and across the stars.

FIND HARMONY IN ALIGNMENT

Every movement changes the relationship between the planets. As planets move so too do they turn on their own axis. Observe the entire system, consider each orbit, and discover the sequence that brings everything into harmony.

The rules are simple to understand, but each new constellation introduces fresh ideas, mechanics, restrictions and puzzeling possibilities.

CARRY THE SIGNAL FORWARD

Guide a single signal from its origin planet, awakening each planet as a relay until the signal unites the system in a unified loop. Every completed connection becomes part of a larger celestial journey, revealing new constellations and new ways of seeing the sky.

A JOURNEY THROUGH THE ZODIAC

Travel through 12 distinctive zodiac worlds, each introducing its own atmosphere, visual identity, calm meditative soundtrack and evolving puzzle ideas. Across more than 150 handcrafted puzzles, the challenge develops gradually from peaceful introductions into intricate celestial systems.

MOVE AT YOUR OWN PACE

There are no timers, no enemies, and no pressure. Take your time, experiment freely, settle into the rhythm of the stars. A colourful, atmospheric universe and transporting soundtrack create a contemplative experience designed for quiet moments of discovery.

FEATURES

  • More than 150 handcrafted celestial puzzles

  • 12 colourful worlds inspired by the zodiac

  • Intuitive orbit and planet-alignment mechanics

  • Gradually evolving spatial and pattern-based challenges

  • No timers, combat or fail states

  • An atmospheric, relaxing original soundtrack

  • A peaceful single-player journey through the cosmos

store_data.about_the_game:
Overview

The black plague has swept across a neo-feudalistic world, relentlessly killing almost half the human population. The plague still lingers, and many human minds have been twisted by the horrors they’ve seen and the corruption of the land. It is the Age of Intolerance, and a global inquisition is underway to eradicate all heretics and nonbelievers. The enforcers of this inquisition believe that a lack of faith is the reason the world has become ill, when in truth it was their sinister leadership who engineered a viral pathogen that infected all of humanity. Superstition and paranoid whispers are commonplace, and few folks emerge during the day out of fear of sickness and death. An evil, vile darkness now blankets the land and humanity is on the brink of extinction. The dormant virus, called the blood curse by the common folk, must be cured to prevent all humans from going mad again and killing each other off. It is up to a small party of mercenaries to quest forward and destroy the very heart of darkness to save the world from madness and eternal damnation.

Setting

The game takes place on our world roughly two thousand years from now. Several world wars have reduced a once glorious globe-spanning empire to rubble. Most of the planet has become irradiated and inhospitable, known as the Cursed Lands. In the last war with the machines, all of humanity was infected by an insidious blood virus that remained dormant until every last human had contracted it. Then, on a day that came to be known as the Culling of Madness, everyone simultaneously was overcome with delirium as the virus activated. In one day, half of humanity killed itself off in a fit of madness and unchecked insanity. This is a dark future alternate universe set in a techno-medieval time period where the world has been ravaged by an ongoing inquisition, a maddening blood virus, and a looming, all-consuming plague. 

Narrative

A party of mercenaries must quest to seek and destroy the source of a vile evil spreading across the world that is corrupting humanity. The last remnants of humanity fight on for some semblance of a civilization and hope to find a cure to the madness caused by the blood virus. The few remaining forces of good have unified under a common belief that the Stygian Empire is responsible in some way for the blood virus, and that if the Dark Citadel can be breached, a cure to the virus and the madness consuming humanity can be found. The Stygian Empire is on the march, seeking to conquer the shattered kingdom of Elyria. In one last ditch effort, a call to arms is sent out to any hero who would stand against the darkness and fight to find a cure to the virus. Will you answer the call to save humanity?

Release Date
2027

Players

1-4 players co-op campaign.


Character Progression

  • Play as one of eight heroes: Barbarian, Mage, Rogue, Cleric, Fighter, Ranger, Necromancer, or Monk.

  • Heroes gain experience levels 0-10 by completing quests in the Prologue, Acts I, II, and III.

  • 24+ unique ability cards per hero.

Goals

  • The party must journey forth from their home base to complete quests to cleanse the land and gain hordes of treasure and loot.

  • The party must journey to a lair to defeat the act boss in order to complete an act.

  • The party must complete all acts in order to journey to the final lair, the Dark Citadel, in search of a cure to the blood virus.

Challenges

  • The party will encounter numerous enemies, hazards, circumstances, and bosses they must work together to defeat and overcome.

  • There are three acts to the game, each with their unique biomes, difficulty, and challenges.

  • Challenge is presented by enemies and their combat abilities, party members can die, bleed over time, and gain negative traits the players must figure out how to remedy or work around.

  • Bleeding over time attracts more monsters over time. If the party doesn’t remedy bleeding characters, the scent of blood is picked up by nearby enemies. Eventually, these enemies will hunt down the party and ambush the party or join an existing battle.

Game Mechanics
2.5D Dungeon & Open World Map Exploration, Turn-based Combat, Deckbuilding, Resource Management.

Genre
Card Battler, Dungeon Crawler, Roguelite.

Soundtrack
Original heavy metal & dark synth soundtrack.

Additional Game Modes
Hardcore Mode: greater risks and greater rewards with hero permadeath.

movies.name: THE CUP - Official Trailer | a free card battler where everyone watches the die

store_data.about_the_game:
The Cup is a free 1v1 creature card battler. Field a survivor and a line of three creatures, play cards, roll dice, and hold the center. Every contestant is a mutated version of a real North American animal, entered under its true natural history, and every natural-history fact on a card is checkable.

Variance is a choice. Every creature is tagged Safe, Swingy, or Jackpot, so the gamble is always one you opted into, and everyone watches the die land. There is no skip button, because the animations are the interface.

The booth calls your match live. BroadcASH calls the play. BOBcast adds the color. The action waits while the booth talks, and the feed is recorded.

TONIGHT'S CARD

  • 59 contestants and 9 survivors from the US, Canada and Mexico delegations, every one a real animal

  • Live 1v1 by invite link, single-elimination gauntlets with medals, or the House

  • Draft mode: build your line from the pool, nobody gets the same night twice

  • Seeded dice: same seed, same game - every match is written to tape, and every highlight links its replay

  • Streaks, medals, the dice ledger, and a shelf of mugs with your name on it

  • An owned score, composed in-house - no rented songs anywhere on the broadcast

THE STATE OF THE BROADCAST

Early access, and honestly labeled: the rules, the dice, the booth and the natural history are all real. The card art is mostly emoji placeholder while we commission real illustrations of every creature, three are completed! The animals earned more than a picker glyph, and they are getting it in style.

Free. No account required - play first, sign up after, and your record follows you.

Card art by @chioart08 and @prayogaardip - A broadcast of the Galactic Athletics Commission. The feed is recorded.

store_data.about_the_game:
Neon Frontline is a single-player roguelike deckbuilder built around tactical battles across three contested battlefields.

The old civilization has collapsed, but its tactical terminals, corporate protocols, autonomous machines, and weapon systems are still running among the ruins. Choose a combat squad, cross increasingly unstable sectors, build your deck, and fight for control of three battlefields at once.

CONTROL THREE BATTLEFIELDS

Every battle is fought across the left, center, and right battlefields. At the end of each turn, power is compared separately on all three. Win a battlefield to deal damage to the enemy.

Limited deployment slots force every Unit card to find the right position. Deploy Units, issue Commands, adjust their Power, and grant Barrier to gain the advantage this turn while preserving enough resources for what comes next.

Different enemies can also alter battlefield rules. A safe battlefield may suddenly become a trap, and a single misplaced deployment can disrupt your entire plan.

CHOOSE YOUR SQUAD

Choose from multiple squads, each with different starting attributes, a starting Relic, and a starting deck.

The Command Squad excels at establishing a stable frontline. The Allied Squad relies on the individual strength of its members. The Tactical Squad creates opportunities through deliberate discards and deck cycling.

Your squad defines the beginning of a run, while every choice you make during the expedition determines the tactical system it eventually becomes.

BUILD MORE THAN A DECK

Acquire new Unit and Command cards after battle, then gradually refine your deck's cost curve, power distribution, and tactical synergies.

Collect Relics that reshape the rules of combat and exploration, and use Modifications to permanently alter a card's cost, Power, or effects. The right Modification can become the core of an entire build, while a powerful choice with a drawback may force you to rethink your route.

CROSS THE UNSTABLE ZONES

Advance through randomized routes across three Acts and choose your next destination.

Fight regular enemies and Elites, encounter unusual events in the ruins, buy supplies at shops, recover Relics from chests, or rest, modify, and duplicate cards at campfires. Manage your health, gold, and deck as you prepare for the Boss waiting at the end of each Act.

A BROKEN WORLD THAT REFUSES TO SHUT DOWN

The old civilization is gone, but its systems refuse to stop.

Unattended settlement networks continue to collect old debts. Abandoned corporate facilities still enforce protocols that have long since lost their purpose. Survivors and armed factions fight over scarce resources using whatever technology they can recover. Push deeper into the ruins, make use of everything that still works, and find a way forward before the remaining systems spiral completely out of control.

FEATURES

• Turn-based card battles fought across three simultaneous battlefields

• 100+ Unit and Command cards supporting a wide variety of tactical builds

• Multiple playable squads with distinct starting decks and Relics

• 20+ Modifications that alter energy costs, Power, and card effects

• 90+ Relics that continuously reshape combat and route decisions

• Randomized routes filled with battles, Elites, events, shops, gifts, and campfires

• 40+ different enemies, three Acts that delve progressively deeper into dangerous zones, and a varied roster of Boss encounters

store_data.about_the_game:
[h1]A cozy autumn to call your own[/h1]

Leaves & Lanterns is a gentle first-person game about the simple joy of tidying up. Sweep and blow drifting autumn leaves into big, satisfying piles, scoop them away, and slowly bring three beautiful places back to life — your suburban home, a walled cottage garden, and a lantern-lit park.

Gather the leaves

Blow glowing maple, oak, birch and ginkgo leaves across the yard, watch heaps form where they gather, and press every new species you find into your Leaf Album.

Light the lanterns

Paper lanterns wait in the dusk of every area. Spend what you've gathered to light them one by one, and watch each place glow warm and gold.

Make it your own

Sell what you gather, upgrade your leaf blowers, and decorate with pumpkins, a scarecrow, a hammock, flower pots and more. Craft cozy autumn keepsakes — garlands, wreaths and pressed-leaf frames — at your own garden workbench.

No pressure, ever

  • No timers, no fail states, no enemies — stop any time and leave it tidy.
  • Three distinct, hand-built places to wander and tend.
  • A warm autumn soundtrack and gentle ambience.
  • Set the mood: bright day, golden afternoon, warm dusk, or moonlit night.

Pull up the hammock, light a lantern, and let the afternoon drift by.

store_data.about_the_game:
Two Hands. One Summit.


A monk who has lost his legs sets out to reach the summit of a massive mountain.

Move each arm independently, grip the rocks, and pull your body upward.
Your only tools are two hands—and your own skill.

Control Each Arm Independently


Control the left arm with WASD and the right arm with IJKL.
Hold the corresponding grip keys to grab a rock, then press both keys together to bend the arm and pull yourself upward.

Hang from one hand, swing your body, and reach for the next hold.
The order and timing of every movement create many possible ways to climb.

Falling Is Part of the Training


There are no mid-run saves.

Let go, run out of grip strength, or miss the next rock, and a single mistake may send you falling a long way down.

But every fall teaches you something.
A rock that once seemed impossible may be within reach on your next attempt.

One Massive, Continuous Mountain


The stage is a single handcrafted mountain that remains the same on every attempt.

Begin among the greenery of the foothills, climb beyond the forest limit, pass through the clouds, and overcome snow-covered and frozen heights on your way to the summit.

As the altitude increases, the gaps between holds become wider, and icy rocks begin to drain your grip strength more quickly.

Traces of Those Who Climbed Before


Wooden resting places left behind by previous monks can be found along the route.

Scattered throughout the mountain are 108 objects representing worldly desires and attachments.
Witness the changing landscape and the monk's journey toward the summit.

Key Features


  • Independent controls for the left and right arms
  • Climbing built around grip-strength management
  • Multiple approaches using momentum and gravity
  • A huge stage that changes from green foothills to clouds, snow, and ice
  • A fixed handcrafted map that rewards practice and mastery
  • No mid-run saves
  • 108 representations of worldly desires scattered across the mountain

Can you overcome every attachment and reach the summit?

store_data.about_the_game:
Medieval Embers of War 2 is a top-down co-op RPG that mixes action, strategy, and battlefield control in a colorful low-poly medieval world.

Take control of a hero and fight alongside your allies in battles where you don't fight alone. Call in units to support you, capture strategic points across the battlefield, and push back an enemy force that has access to the same tools and abilities you do.

⚔️ Fight Together

Team up with up to 4 players in local co-op and take on the battlefield together. Each player controls their own hero while managing their units and working with the rest of the team.

🛡️ RPG Meets Strategy

You are more than just a hero running into battle. Your decisions on the battlefield matter.

Call in the right units, capture and hold strategic points, choose where to fight, and use your forces to create an advantage. The enemy isn't just waiting to be defeated — the AI can use the same battlefield mechanics and capabilities available to you.

🗺️ Campaign

An introductory, objective-based campaign takes you through a series of battles designed to teach you the game's mechanics while gradually introducing new gameplay elements.

⚔️ Skirmish Battles

Skirmish mode is free-form battle. Capture battlefield points, build your forces, disrupt the enemy, and push toward their camp. The outcome comes down to how well you play your strategy and control the battlefield.

🔥 Your Battlefield, Your Strategy

Medieval Embers of War 2 is built around simple ideas: fight together, make smart decisions, and take control of the battlefield.

Whether you're working with friends in co-op or testing your strategy against the AI, every battle gives you the freedom to decide where to fight, which forces to bring, and how to turn the tide in your favor.

Gather your allies. Take control of the battlefield. Make your stand.

store_data.about_the_game:
One question, every turn

You don't play a card — you build a chain. Every technique has an opening and an ending, and

each one only links to the technique it fits. You lay them down face down, and when both duelists are

done, the two chains meet position by position.

The longer the chain, the more damage it carries. But every position is a clash, and a technique that

loses its clash adds nothing. You build the chain. Your opponent decides how much of it lands.

The edge, the feint and the guard

Attack beats Maneuver. Maneuver beats Defense. Defense beats Attack. When two techniques of the same

type meet, no number saves you: the position goes to whoever holds the initiative — and if

nobody holds it, both cancel out. Win a position and the initiative is yours, shielding you on the

next one. The duel has momentum, and taking it from your opponent is half the craft.

Two schools, two stretches of the wheel

  • Kurenai River — water. Its techniques live in the low values, and they link into each otherreadily: the river doesn't strike, it drags.

  • Mount Okuribi — ember. Its techniques live in the high values and open harder: fire doesn'tflow, it catches.

The two schools overlap on only a couple of values, so mixing them means fewer techniques that link —

and a deck built to bridge the gap on purpose.

The Dojo Path

A campaign across regions where you choose your opponent at each stage, and a forge where the pieces you

combine matter for what they share — their element, their region, their era. Like matching affinities, but

with steel.

And when the campaign is done

  • Free Duel — your decks against any rival.

  • Daily Challenge — a fixed duel, the same one for everybody, every day.

What it is, and what it isn't

  • A single-player game, paid and complete. You buy it once.

  • No microtransactions, no passes, no energy. Not now, not later.

  • No always-online requirement.

The two schools overlap on only a couple of values, so mixing them means fewer techniques that link —

and a deck built to bridge the gap on purpose.

The Dojo Path

A campaign across regions where you choose your opponent at each stage, and a forge where the pieces you

combine matter for what they share — their element, their region, their era. Like matching affinities, but

with steel.

And when the campaign is done

  • Free Duel — your decks against any rival.

  • Daily Challenge — a fixed duel, the same one for everybody, every day.

What it is, and what it isn't

  • A single-player game, paid and complete. You buy it once.

  • No microtransactions, no passes, no energy. Not now, not later.

  • No always-online requirement.

Your opponent's blades decide how much of it survives. Two schools, hidden paths, one campaign of duels.

Monster Collector is a single-player collection RPG focused on discovery and collecting.

Across 20 distinct regions, you'll encounter 1,020 monsters, including standard monsters, color variants, rare monsters, and ultra-rare creatures.

Battle them, record your discoveries, recruit them to your party, and keep searching for the ones you haven't found yet.

Rather than focusing only on becoming stronger, Monster Collector is about the satisfaction of discovering, collecting, and completing your catalogs.

Collect 1,020 Monsters

Travel through 20 distinct regions, including grasslands, forests, rivers, snowy fields, volcanoes, the deep sea, and otherworldly realms.

Your encounters, victories, recruits, drops, and other discoveries are recorded in the Monster Catalog. Search for monsters you haven't encountered yet, hunt down rare variants, and gradually work toward completing your collection.

Plan Your Next Hunt

There are many things to collect, including standard materials, rare materials, emblems, color variants, and recruitable monsters.

Choose the regions and equipment that best suit your goal, decide what you want to collect next, and plan your runs accordingly.

Recruit and Raise Your Monsters

Build a party of up to four monsters from the creatures you've recruited.

Manage your collection at the Ranch, where you can sort, search, and compare stats to find your favorites among the many monsters you've collected.

Complete Five Catalogs

Monsters aren't the only things to collect.

  • Monster Catalog

  • Item Catalog

  • Emblem Catalog

  • Accessory Catalog

  • Furniture Catalog

Discover collections scattered throughout the world and aim for 100% completion.

Reliable Save System for Long-Term Collecting

Monster Collector supports autosaving, three manual save slots, checksums, three generations of backups, and automatic recovery from corrupted save data. A dedicated save file for Steam Auto-Cloud is also included.

Main Features

  • Single-player

  • English and Japanese

  • Keyboard and mouse controls

  • Fullscreen display

store_data.about_the_game:
02:00. The log will not stop scrolling.

One of those lines is an attack.

SEC//SIM is a detection-and-response roguelite in which you work one night as an analyst in a security operations centre. It is not a game about breaking in. It is a game about reading an attack, and cutting it.

■ Hunt. Deduce. Contain.

A shift is three motions.

Hunt Click a suspicious line in the flood to flag it. Follow it by eye, or press / and narrow the river with grep — regular expressions supported.

Deduce Dive into focus mode. The world slows down and you get time to think. Inter-arrival variance (a z-score), entry path, cause, business impact. "Variance near zero = machine, not human." The C2 beacon gives itself away.

Contain Choose your response. Cut surgically, firewall the C2 address only, or take down the whole /24. The choice changes the outcome: the wider you block, the safer you are — and the more uptime and trust you burn.

Every shift is scored on MTTR, SLA uptime, and detection F1. The metrics you are graded on are the metrics a real SOC is graded on.

■ The attacker adapts to you

Ten attacks — reconnaissance scanning, credential stuffing, SQL injection, XSS, L7 DDoS, phishing, valid-account abuse and lateral movement, C2 beaconing, exfiltration, ransomware — all mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, OWASP, and NIST.

And the attacker learns. Block it with a signature and it returns obfuscated the next night. Fix the root cause and it does not return at all. The difference between a patch and a cure shows up tomorrow.

At the top of the map waits the APT campaign "Silent Intruder": a loud diversion and a quiet real objective, running at the same time.

■ A low floor and a very high ceiling

A newcomer can solve a shift by picking from the suggested responses.

A practitioner can read the structure of the log directly and solve it far faster, far cheaper, and far more cleanly. Both are driving the same simulation underneath — the only difference is the score and the clock. Improvement is one continuous slope, not two games.

Techniques you have mastered get automated away (SOAR starts handling them unattended), so the board in front of you never settles into busywork.

■ One night ends. There is always another.

Campaign Climb night by night toward the APT. Draft a different loadout every run.

Endless The threats never stop, and they start arriving together. How long do you hold?

Daily Everyone gets the same seed. Same flood — whoever handles it cleanest wins.

Lab Study one technique with no clock and no consequences.

Every technique you beat is registered in the ATT&CK codex along with your own response record. There is a skill tree, a shop, and a career ladder (Intern → L1 → L2 → Responder → Hunter → Lead → CISO). Every reason to come back is inside the board.

■ How it feels to play

· Fully playable from the keyboard alone. Key rebinding included.

· Severity is distinguished by shape (▲▲ / ▲ / ●) as well as colour, with a colour-blind-safe pattern mode.

· Focus mode's slowdown is adjustable in settings, for players who do not want the rush.

· Japanese and English, switchable instantly.

· Entirely offline. No account, no connection, no server.

There is no stamina. Nothing refills on a timer.

There are no loot boxes, no gacha, and no in-app purchases.

What you get instead is the feeling of getting better at it.

■ Yes, this is practice

The mechanics are modelled on real blue-team work: log analysis, SIEM triage, finding IOCs, reconstructing a kill chain, making a containment call, detection engineering. Playing well and working well were designed to point in the same direction.

That said, this is a game, not a certification and not courseware. "Because it is fun" is a perfectly good reason to get good at it.

Cardrooms is a fast-paced card-based roguelite shooter where every round can change the way you fight. Jump into intense arena battles, outplay your opponents, and use powerful cards to create a build that fits your playstyle.

Lose a round? That's when things get interesting. The losing player gets to choose a powerful card, gaining a new advantage that can turn the next round in their favor. Stack upgrades, experiment with different combinations, and find new ways to take down your opponent.

As the battle continues, both players become stronger and the fights become more chaotic. A small advantage can quickly turn into a devastating build, so adapt to your opponent and make every card count.

- Build & Combine — Experiment with different cards to create powerful combinations.

- Unique Battle Arenas — Fight across a variety of maps, including a Backrooms-inspired arena.

- Multiplayer — Battle your friends and opponents in intense arena combat.

store_data.about_the_game:
Driving through to the edge of town, you pull into a small gas station that's seen better days. The pumps are rusted, the shelves are bare, and the register swallowed its last coin weeks ago. This is your business now.

From a humble roadside stall, build a thriving fuel station and convenience store. Every shift is yours to run by hand.

A genuine first-person workday

Unload deliveries, haul crates into the warehouse, and set each product out on the shelves by hand. Ring up customers at the register — scan every item, take the cash, and give the right change. Refuel the cars that roll in, and keep the store open from the first morning light to the last evening customer.

Run the numbers, grow the business

Set your own prices and restock wisely. Manage your inventory and daily expenses, turn a profit, and reinvest it to unlock franchise licenses and upgrade your shop — new shelving, better pumps, a bigger warehouse. Every upgrade draws more customers through the door.

A living, busy shop

Customers come and go, browse the shelves, and leave things behind. Pick up what they drop, tidy the aisles, and keep the place running. The little details add up — from pumping a stranger's last tank of gas to watching a full shelf of goods finally sell out.

Whether you dream of a quiet corner shop or a busy highway stop, this is your station. Build it your way.

store_data.about_the_game:
I made this game for my friends.

Not for them to have fun.

For them to suffer.

Rocket is a 2.5D rage-inducing obstacle game where you take control of a rocket and attempt to navigate through increasingly difficult levels without crashing, introducing new mechanics every couple levels. 

The controls are simple. The levels are not. 

Featuring

  • 🚀 Easy to Learn. Hard to Master

    • Learn the controls in a matter of seconds, then spend wasted hours trying to master them.

  • 🌍 Two Worlds. Thirty Levels. And a Boss Fight?

    • Take on 2 worlds (currently), each containing 15 levels filled with different obstacles and mechanics.

    • Oh and at the very end, there's a boss fight. Because why not.

  • 🎵 Music

    • My friend was force- I mean.. gladly agreed, to make the soundtrack, specifically for the game

    • So, if you hate the game, at least listen to the music. SHOUTOUT haydn juliff

  • 🛍️ Customisation

    • Unlock and equip a variety of different rocket skins, particle effects and hats as you progress.

  • 📈 Leaderboards

    • Speedrun the game and climb the rankings on the leaderboards and see how your times stack up.

    • Every second counts. Can you get to the top?

  • 🏆 Steam Achievements

    • Think you have mastered Rocket? (no you haven't)

    • Prove it by unlocking all of the game's Steam Achievements, including challenges that will test how far you can actually get.

Oh, did I forget to mention that you have to do it all in one run?

store_data.about_the_game:
Once You Understand Magic, Everything Becomes an Ingredient.

Welcome to Scroll Shop, where villagers, merchants, nobles and adventurers send you problems they believe magic can solve.

A farm is crawling with rats.
A monster is blocking the road.
A merchant needs a rusted gate restored.
Someone desperately wants to be loved.

Read the request. Figure out what they actually need. Then craft the scroll you believe will solve it.

And eventually, find out what your magic really did.

Magic Has Rules. You Have to Discover Them.

You do not begin with a spellbook full of answers.

Experiment with magical elements, strange ingredients and scrolls you have already discovered to uncover new spells.

Fire burns.
Water cleans and corrodes.
Light reveals.
Time accelerates.

Those meanings do not disappear when elements are combined. They build on one another.

A simple spell you discover today may become an ingredient in something far more powerful tomorrow. What begins as a way to remove rust might eventually teach you how to tear an iron construct apart.

The deeper you understand the logic of magic, the more possibilities you begin to see.

Solving the Problem Is Only the First Test.

There is rarely just one spell that works.

A firestorm will get rid of the rats.

It may also burn the crops, the barn and the family's winter stock.

The customer matters too. A ruthless soldier may appreciate a lethal solution that horrifies a pacifist farmer. A frugal merchant may admire an elegant low-tier spell while a showy noble expects something spectacular.

Think about the problem, its scale, the surroundings and the person asking for your help.

A spell can work perfectly and still be completely wrong.

Your Magic Leaves the Shop Without You.

Once a scroll is delivered, the decision is out of your hands.

Later, you discover what happened.

Perhaps the problem vanished exactly as intended. Perhaps your solution worked with an unfortunate side effect. Perhaps you misunderstood the request entirely.

Or perhaps the new problem is now much worse than the old one.

Customers remember what you gave them. Good judgment can earn better rewards, rare ingredients, reputation and future opportunities. Reckless magic has consequences of its own.

In Scroll Shop, success is not simply about whether a spell worked.

It is about what happened because it did.

Every Mistake Teaches You Something.

Your greatest progression does not come from a level bar.

It comes from understanding the world.

Discovered recipes fill your Spell Book. Encounters with unfamiliar creatures reveal weaknesses and resistances in your Beast Book. Returning customers become less mysterious as you learn their preferences, values and history.

Knowledge gathered from one problem can become the missing piece of another.

The creature that nearly ruined your day yesterday might be the one you know exactly how to handle tomorrow.

The Kingdom Keeps Sending Problems.

Each day brings a new batch of letters, changing ingredient stocks and events that alter what people need from you.

Your time is limited.

Choose which requests deserve your attention. Buy and earn ingredients. Improve your tools. Research unfamiliar magic. Experiment with combinations that might lead somewhere new.

Some letters promise easy coin.

Some hide rare discoveries.

Some ask for magic you do not yet understand.

And some may be better left unanswered.

You Are Not Collecting Spells. You Are Learning Magic.

The more of its logic you uncover, the larger your vocabulary becomes.

The more you learn about the people and creatures beyond your shop, the better your decisions become.

And sooner or later, you may look at a problem, look at everything you have learned and realize that the answer was sitting in front of you all along.

store_data.about_the_game:
You are the Red Queen. The road goes through their country.

Seven rival Queens hold seven realms, and the only way to any of them is the long way across their fields, through their villages, past the people who live there. At the far end of every road there is a Queen, a table, and a reckoning.

THE MARCH

Travel through tiles of villages, magicians, tithe barns, until you reach the standard of rival Queen.
Everything is open information. There are no hidden statistics, no invisible timers, no rolls the game makes behind your back.

THE CHOICE

Every tile is a card and every card asks something. Feed the starving and your column grows and eats more. Seize the grain and you'll be fed and remembered. The peasantry, the clergy and the merchants each keep their own count of you, and when a count crosses a line, a door opens or closes: a back gate offered, a road picketed, a convoy gone.

THE RECKONING

The choices that matter don't pay out on the spot. They become deeds: Oaths and Intrigues that will shape the rest of your march and decide your destiny.

THE DUEL

Three hits and a Queen is finished. Your army is the people still marching behind you, and it is the only thing between her and you. Play from a hand of five — mercenaries, peasants, reinforcements, sacrifice, assault — roll the clash die, and hope the crown comes up on your side of the table.

FEATURES

  • Seven rival Queens, each with her own realm, her own voice, her own way of fighting, and her own deck of schemes.

  • Over a hundred authored decision cards and more than a hundred deeds. No procedural text, no filler, every card written.

  • A moral ledger that persists across the whole run. Reputations, counters and consequences carry from march to march.

  • Four difficulty tiers, from a road you can walk to one that expects you to have learned something.

Sanguinity, given to us by the mirthful Goddess Gwyn, allows those who study it to command blood itself. Weak to intense and angry emotions, casters of the Sanguine arts practice good health and the healing of others, and are optimistic that a brighter future awaits us all. 

Melancholy, bestowed upon us by the withdrawn Deity Ela, supplies more than just despair to the folk who live and breath that blackest of bile. Choleric masters too are weak to that nihilistic instinct to give up on it all. 

Phlegmaticism, somehow gained from the lethargic and "never-present" Deity Peggy, is oft ignored by the wider world. While applications of said power come with a strong devotion and sensitivity, the feelings of passivity and disgust usually overwhelm the user, and lead to a life of decay and inert inactivity. That same sensitivity is however their weakness too, as most can still be moved to action by devastating sadness.

Explore the Temples of each of these Deities, gain the power to fight back against the monsters that stand in your way, and discover reasons behind the plot to vitrify the entire world at the whims of a broken heart.

store_data.about_the_game:
I never wanted to be the dad who says "go study."


You're an office worker in your forties. You live in Tokyo, went to a decent university, work at a decent company.
You never took entrance exams as a kid yourself. You wanted your daughter to grow up free.

...Right up until you noticed the part of you that quietly hopes she gets into a top school.

Happy Project 12 is a life-sim in which you become the father of Hinata, a fourth-grader,
and live out the three years leading to her junior high entrance exams in February of sixth grade.

Three years, 69 turns. Every weekly choice decides everything


Each turn, you decide how your daughter spends her time.

  • Have her study — Japanese, math, science, social studies. Her stats grow, her stamina drains
  • Let her play — stamina and drive come back. But that week's studying is gone

Six stats grow: STEM Knowledge, Humanities, Reading, Calculation, Reasoning and Drive.
But— a daughter whose Drive has bottomed out will not do what you tell her.
"I don't feel like it today." One sentence, and the week you planned disappears.

Mock exams: reality with nowhere to hide


Six of them in three years. National mock exams score your parenting without mercy.
Depending on her results, she moves between Class α and Class β at cram school.
Move up and she gains confidence; drop down and— dinner that week gets a little quiet.

Grades aren't the only thing that matters


In this game there is something you have to watch besides her academic ability.

It's the trust between parent and child.

What you answered when your daughter asked for help.
The face you made on the day her grades fell.
All of it adds up, never once shown to you as a number, and quietly decides how it all ends.

Because you can't see it, all you can do is believe in your own three years.

A family isn't a battle you fight alone


Your wife Naomi checks the exam forums and social media every single night.
She rides every high and low of your daughter's grades, second-guesses your decisions, and is slowly worn down.

Leave her alone and your family breaks before the exams do.
...Entrance exams are not the child's problem alone.

Over 50 story events, and 11 endings


Afternoons with friends, cram school meetings, Christmas, the walk home from a mock exam, and exam day itself.
All kinds of events unfold one after another across the three years.

And waiting beyond the final results are 11 different endings.

Getting into her first-choice school doesn't guarantee happiness.
Failing every school doesn't rule out redemption.
...What decides it isn't only her deviation score, but how you faced your daughter over three years.

Endings you reach are recorded in the ending gallery, and you can play again and again until you've filled it.

Contents


  • Three years, roughly 70 turns of main story (about one hour per playthrough)
  • 50+ story events / 11 endings (with a gallery feature)
  • Skip for already-read events, dialogue log, 10 save slots
  • Fully localized in 10 languages (Japanese / English / Simplified Chinese / Traditional Chinese / Spanish / Portuguese (Brazil) / German / French / Korean / Russian)

February, three years from now. What will your face look like as you send her off?

store_data.about_the_game:
AN ACTIVE INCREMENTAL TOWER DEFENSE

How to Turn Zombie combines incremental progression, tower defense pressure, and direct cursor-based combat.

  • Attack cells directly with your cursor

  • Defend your central Viral Core

  • Harvest Biomass and unlock permanent mutations

  • Build powerful upgrade synergies

  • Adapt to new mechanics across different organs

  • Face increasingly dangerous immune defenses and bosses

BECOME THE VIRUS

You are not fighting the infection. You are the infection.

Take control of a living virus and invade the human body from within. Destroy cells, harvest Biomass, evolve new mutations, and protect your Viral Core as the immune system becomes increasingly desperate to stop you.

DESTROY. HARVEST. INFECT.

Your cursor is not just a pointer — it is your weapon.

Strike cells directly, break through biological defenses, and collect the Biomass they leave behind. But spreading the infection is only half the battle. As the body reacts, antibodies and specialized immune cells begin attacking your Viral Core.

Push the infection forward while defending the very thing keeping it alive.

EVOLVE YOUR VIRUS

Biomass is more than a resource. It fuels a permanent Evolution Tree filled with mutations that can dramatically change the way you play.

Increase your damage, improve Biomass generation, trigger critical effects, create viral constructs, unleash electrical chain reactions, manipulate the battlefield, and combine mutations into increasingly powerful synergies. Choose how your virus evolves.

THE BODY ADAPTS

The deeper the infection spreads, the harder the body fights back. New cells, immune defenses, hazards, and biological mechanics constantly change the battlefield, forcing you to adapt your strategy and evolution.

What works in one stage may not be enough for the next.

INFECT THE BODY, ORGAN BY ORGAN

Each organ is its own battlefield. Progress through different parts of the human body, each introducing its own environment, enemies, mechanics, and biological threats.

The bloodstream is only the beginning.

FACE THE BODY'S STRONGEST DEFENSES

At the end of each organ, the infection faces a powerful biological boss. These encounters combine the mechanics introduced throughout the organ and push your build to its limits.

Your mutations will determine whether the infection survives... or gets eradicated.

store_data.about_the_game:
Build with your hands. Travel with your creations.

House Craft Voyage is a single-player adventure sandbox built around freeform construction and physics interaction. Along the journey, craft structures, vehicles, and devices from geometric blocks, turn ideas into reality, and keep moving forward with what you’ve made.

Create your own solutions
Facing terrain, mechanisms, and all kinds of challenges, there is no single right answer. Spawn blocks, reshape them, snap and weld parts together, combine drive components, and clear the way—explore, or simply play—on your own terms.

Physics-driven building
Welded structures respond to gravity, collisions, and power for real. Build cleverly and you may run steady or fly far; build freely and you may still get surprising results. Creating and experimenting are the core of the fun.

A journey rooted in the feeling of home
Explore, collect, and try things out in lived-in, everyday scenes. Building can clear a level—or express who you are. Dress a space the way you like, then take your work on the next stretch of the road.

Key Features

  • Freeform geometric building: spawn and combine many basic shapes

  • Snap & weld: join parts into stable structures or vehicles

  • Appearance painting: color your creations and make them yours

  • Physics interaction: real feedback from power, collisions, and structural stability

  • Exploration & puzzles: solve journey challenges through building

  • Single-player sandbox: create and adventure at your own pace

Start building—then set out.

store_data.about_the_game:
A roguelite siege defense. The horde marches at your wall in lanes, and

anything that reaches it takes health you cannot fully get back.

Spin, place, transmute

Every turn the reel deals you alchemical symbols. You place them on the

table, then transmute: the board resolves and becomes damage. Where you

put them is the whole decision.

The board grows

Symbols react to their neighbours. Fire beside Fire hits harder. A Seed

grows every turn it survives. Leave a symbol alone long enough and it

promotes into a stronger form that was never in your deck. Symbols come

in elemental families and enemies have weaknesses, so the kind of damage

matters as much as the amount.

Relics, Tools and Rituals

Relics change a rule for the rest of the run. Tools have limited charges

and few slots, so you spend them carefully. Rituals pay out when their

condition is met, which means building toward them turns in advance.

Between sieges

A shop with a short stock. A scavenger running a shell game you can walk

away from. A mason who grants a single favour: open a locked cell, move

a symbol, or destroy one.

Between runs

Losing ends the run but not the progress. Essence carries into a tree of

permanent unlocks, so the next attempt starts with something the last

one did not have.

matters as much as the amount.

Relics, Tools and Rituals

Relics change a rule for the rest of the run. Tools have limited charges

and few slots, so you spend them carefully. Rituals pay out when their

condition is met, which means building toward them turns in advance.

Between sieges

A shop with a short stock. A scavenger running a shell game you can walk

away from. A mason who grants a single favour: open a locked cell, move

a symbol, or destroy one.

Between runs

Losing ends the run but not the progress. Essence carries into a tree of

permanent unlocks, so the next attempt starts with something the last

one did not have.

store_data.about_the_game:
Our planet went dark

SOMETHING caught our little world and pulled it into permanent night. There is no sun, only the heat bleeding up from the planet's core, and whatever light you can carry. You, a miner orc, alone on the surface of the dark, with a candle lantern on your back and a whole crust of ore beneath your feet.

Fight darkness with light

Your lantern is your eyes, your weapon, and your clock. Its glow is the only thing that reveals the world, and any creature caught in it burns. But the flame is finite, venture out and it drains, and as it dies your circle of light shrinks, step by step, until you're standing in the pitch black with nothing left. Every dive is a held breath: how deep do you dare go before you have to run back to refuel the flame?

The dark fights back

The night is not empty. Pools of living oil well up out of the black and slide toward you, invisible until your light touches them. Spitters wait for a distraction to destroy you with their balls of dark matter. Hold them at the edge of your glow where they burn but can't reach you, and clear a room with an orc rage whirlwind when they swarm.

Unlock new weapons, use new minerals to fuel them. 

Mine coal to boost your flame and slow your enemies with your blinding light. Charge your mace for a powerful sweep that destroys both rock and enemies... Every edge of advantage means another chance to free yourself and the planet

Greed has a price

Your bag starts small on purpose. Upgrade it back at camp and it grows, tier after tier. But the mine doesn't get safer while you're in it, and an unlimited bag is still tethered to a very limited flame. The only cap that ever really mattered was your trusty friend... your lamp's light.

A camp that grows into something stranger

Home base starts as a scrappy mining camp with a torch that never goes out, the one patch of this planet that's always safe. Sell your haul here, spend it on gear, and watch the camp grow with you. A trading post first, and then, once enough sinistervein has come up out of the dark, a base anchored by a portal woven from the vein's own magic. How did you learn to open a door between worlds?

Short sessions, real tension

There's no cutscene standing between you and the mine. Load in, watch your candle catch, and go. A run is as long as your nerve holds out, and the loop resets clean every time you come back for another.

store_data.about_the_game:
Heat is your HP, your fuel, and your timer.
You are a dying star drifting through an infinite procedurally generated galaxy. Every second you cool. The only way to survive is to slam into other stars and steal their heat.

There is no attack button. Collision is everything — it damages, it heals, it propels, it feeds your growth.

  • Mass growth — Absorb stars to gain mass. The heavier you are, the bigger the prey you can swallow. But mass makes you cool faster and drags you into the gravity of giants.
  • Elemental decay — Your composition shifts as your heat drains: Hydrogen → Helium → Carbon → Silicon → Iron. You can literally read your remaining lifespan off your own body, and each element changes your stats.
  • The heat death front — A cooling front expands from the origin and never stops. Standing still is death. Keep moving outward.
  • 34 celestial bodies — Gas giants you can hide inside, ice grains that trade heat for mass, pulsars, white dwarfs, and black holes whose event horizon means instant death.
  • Roguelite builds — 10 in-run upgrades, plus a permanent research lab between runs.
  • Everything is procedural — Every pixel of art and every sound effect is generated in code. No external image or audio assets.
