store_data.about_the_game:
Take control of a powerful drill vehicle and descend beneath the surface of a distant planet in search of valuable minerals. Explore unfamiliar terrain, manage your fuel, and decide how deep you are willing to go before making the journey back to base.

Drill Into the Unknown

Break through layers of alien rock to uncover hidden riches. Every expedition takes you farther beneath the planet’s surface, where valuable deposits and greater risks await.

Manage Your Fuel

Fuel is limited, and every trip is a race against the gauge. Mine as much as you can, then turn back when you run dry. Return to base to refuel, and prepare for the next expedition.

Upgrade Your Drill Rover.

Use the resources you bring home to improve your equipment. Upgrade your drill to break through tougher rock, expand your fuel capacity to stay underground longer, and strengthen other systems to make each run more productive.

Go Deeper through sectors.

Each expedition helps you push beyond your previous limits.

Strike It Rich

Search the alien underground for gold, gems, and other valuable finds. Build your fortune one expedition at a time and turn a humble mining vehicle into a high-powered machine built for the deepest reaches of the planet.

How Far Will You Go?

Step on the gas, watch your fuel, and make every trip count. The planet is waiting beneath your wheels.

store_data.about_the_game:
A 2.5D tower defense game where your primitive tribe fights to protect its campfire against endless waves of creatures and beasts.

FEATURES

  • 2.5D pixel-art tower defense gameplay.

  • Many unique tribe members and creatures.

  • Resources including sticks and stones.

  • A storyline with hand-crafted levels.

  • An endless mode with exponential difficulty.

DEFEND YOUR CAMPFIRE

  • Defend your campfire from endless waves of wild creatures using primitive tribe members with different attack patterns and status effects. 

  • Kill creatures with your tribe members to gather sticks used to grow your tribe to kill more creatures.

  • The less damage delt to your campfire the more stones you are awarded at the end of the level.

GATHER RESOURCES

  • Killing enemies awards your tribe sticks, sticks can be used to place more tribe members.

  • Beating levels or reaching milestones in endless awards you stones, stones are used to unlock tribal compositions that can be used in any future level or endless run.

STORY LEVELS AND ENDLESS

  • In story mode you can play through levels with unique maps, enemy waves, and progression to the storyline.

  • In endless mode, fight against endlessly spawning creatures that grow exponentially stronger until your tribe is overwhelmed into defeat.

SYNERGIZING COMPOSITIONS

  • Use powerful tribal compositions to give massive buffs to your tribe members to more easily defeat the creatures.

  • Tribal compositions are unlocked using stones.

  • Compositions are activated automatically once the correct tribe members are fighting together.

  • Experiment with different tribal compositions that stack together to create the strongest possible tribe.

ART STYLE

  • Tribe members and creatures use 2D pixel-art sprites.

  • The maps are made up of simple 3D objects with pixel textures and when mixed with the 2D tribe member and creature sprites lead to a clean 2.5D look.

store_data.about_the_game:
Packpunk is an asynchronous PvP auto-battler. You pack a grid of gear onto your rig and watch the run play out on its own.

Nobody is waiting on the other end, so there's no queue and no session to sit through. Opponents are real players' rigs, read off a Steam leaderboard and rebuilt on your machine; when there's no rig to pull, one is composed to match yours instead. Every item on the shelf is rolled fresh, so a run starts whenever you want one.

A run takes about a minute and you don't drive it. Items fire on their own timers, heat builds while they do, statuses stack, and items sitting next to each other work better than they would apart. Partway through, a flux window changes one rule of the run for a stretch, and every build has a window that's good to it.

KEY FEATURES

  • Asynchronous PvP. Your rig goes on the leaderboard, other people's rigs come back, and neither of you has to be online at the same time.

  • Tile bags together to shape your socket space, then pack it with the gear you've got.

  • Items are rolled, not authored. A base object plus affixes like Rot, Glitch, Freeze and Mend.

  • Where an item sits matters. Neighbours work on each other, so packing isn't just filling empty sockets.

store_data.about_the_game:
Typesmith is a typing roguelike where your keyboard is the weapon.

Words spawn at the edge of the arena and close in on your core. Type a word to destroy it. Miss a key and you lose ground on it. Let a word touch the core and the run is over. That is the entire combat system, and everything else in the game exists to make it faster, louder, and more satisfying with every round.

Build a run out of upgrades

Hit the score target, clear the round, and step into the shop. Spend what you earned on relics that bend the rules, upgrades to individual keys so your most-used letters hit harder, and synergies that stack until a build snowballs. In the first rounds you read every word. By the end of a good run you are clearing the screen on reflex.

Some words fight back

Gilded words pay triple. Shielded words have to be typed twice. Volatile words burn on a fuse instead of waiting to arrive. And every round, one word carries a bounty worth hunting ahead of everything else. Reading the board is half the skill. Choosing which word deserves your hands next is the other half.

The shop is typing too

Buying, selling, rerolling, continuing: all of it is typed. You never reach for the mouse. A run in Typesmith is one continuous typing flow from the first word to the last.

Win the round the moment you win it

Every round demands a score. Hit it and the round ends on the spot, with the clock you did not need paid out as coins. Fast hands finish early. Careful hands use the whole clock. Nobody waits around.

Roguelike bones

  • Runs of twelve rounds, with boss rounds waiting at the milestones
  • Score targets that climb every round, so your build has to keep up
  • Streaks that reward accuracy, with a knockback (not a full reset) when you miss
  • Every keystroke plays a note, and a clean word resolves like a short melody

Get faster without noticing

Typesmith is a roguelike first. But it rewards speed and accuracy above everything else, and it builds every round against your measured typing speed, so every run is also practice. Whether you type at 40 words per minute or 120, you will feel yourself getting faster without ever opening a typing tutor.

store_data.about_the_game:
Bring a seaside town back to life

Tidewell is a cozy town-management game about rebuilding a neglected coastal village, one thoughtful decision at a time.

When you arrive, only a handful of residents remain. The harbor is weathered, old plots lie abandoned, and the younger villagers have left for bigger towns. As the newly elected mayor—and a former fisher—it is up to you to give people a reason to come home.

Listen to the people who live there

Villagers bring you petitions asking for homes, shops, decorations, and improvements. Approve them, set them aside, or turn them down—but choose carefully. Space is limited, the town’s vault is not bottomless, and every decision changes the lives of named villagers.

Requests also naturally introduce new parts of the game. There is no checklist of disconnected objectives: the town tells you what it needs through the people who call it home.

Decide what belongs where

Placement matters in Tidewell. Reclaim neglected land, arrange buildings, shape districts, and make the most of a compact coastline.

A busy workshop might provide jobs while annoying its neighbors. A well-placed bench, flower bed, or lantern can lift an entire corner of town. Decorating is not just cosmetic—it helps determine how each district feels.

Balance prosperity and happiness

Set taxes, fund improvements, and keep an eye on the town’s mood. Higher taxes fill the vault more quickly but may push struggling households too far. Lower them, and people will be happier, but ambitious projects will have to wait.

There is no sudden game over. A town can decline, but it can always recover through patient decisions, careful spending, and a little honest work.

Make the cove your own

Customize your mayor, restore the harbor, and watch the village develop through changing days, weather, tides, and seasons. Meet residents with their own names, routines, and wishes. Welcome, cats, prepare for festivals and capture postcard views of the place you created.

As Tidewell grows, fishing and voyages beyond the cove will bring back income, materials, discoveries and new neighbours—opening the way to a thriving harbour community.

Features

  • Restore a declining town rather than starting with an empty map

  • Answer petitions from named villagers whose needs shape the town

  • Place buildings and decorations across a handcrafted seaside cove

  • Manage taxes, happiness, population, and limited space

  • Create districts where nearby buildings affect one another

  • Customize your mayor and name your village

  • Watch villagers work, wander, gather, and return home

  • Experience changing weather, tides, seasons, and festivals

  • Fish, explore, and bring new opportunities back to the harbor

  • Play at your own pace with no combat, quick-time events, or hard game-over

  • Photograph and share your village in Postcard Mode

5081940.name: Das Hexencafé am Zürichsee: Der letzte Eintrag

store_data.about_the_game:
At the Hexencafé on Lake Zurich, there are rules for things that cannot be explained. But when a final entry appears in the archive that should not exist, this fragile balance begins to unravel.

Das Hexencafé am Zürichsee: Der letzte Eintrag is a standalone fantasy visual novel about choices, memories, and the question of what should be recorded – and what might have been better left unwritten.

Follow Liva Kern through a story filled with unusual encounters, mysterious records, and impossible events. Aurelia, Momo, Mary Kanzi, and other characters become part of a mystery whose outcome depends on your decisions.

YOUR CHOICES MATTER

Conversations and decisions shape the course of the story. What you believe, whom you trust, and how you deal with the final entry can have far-reaching consequences.

MULTIPLE ENDINGS

Your decisions lead to different outcomes. Not every path ends the same way – and some consequences only reveal themselves much later.

A STANDALONE STORY

No prior knowledge is required. The story was designed as a standalone experience and takes you directly into the world of the Hexencafé on Lake Zurich.

ATMOSPHERIC FANTASY

Explore a quiet and mysterious world blending the atmosphere of Lake Zurich with magic and things that probably should never appear in an official record.

FEATURES

• Story-driven visual novel

• Meaningful choices

• Multiple endings

• Atmospheric fantasy story

• Full German and English text

• Three selectable text sizes: Normal, Large and Very Large

• Fully playable with a mouse

• No timed inputs or Quick Time Events

WHO CAN YOU TRUST WHEN EVERYONE'S GOT AN AK-47?

Play as an Innocent and protect the Leader as a team or play as the Impostor, blend in, and eliminate everyone one by one. No voting, no meeting. Every player has the power to execute anyone at any moment.

ROLES

  • Innocent: Complete tasks, clear enemy robots, and protect the Leader at all costs.

  • Leader: Stay alive. Lead your team, make critical decisions, and complete the mission.

  • Impostor: Sabotage systems, create chaos, and execute the Innocents, especially the Leader without being caught.

WEAPONS & ABILITIES

  • Fire Mode: Fire standard rounds. (Standard bullets won't damage aliens.)

  • Lasso Mode: Move quickly across the map or pull players into traps.

  • Tornado Mode: Create a tornado that hurls your targets directly into environmental traps.

TASKS & THREATS

While keeping the base operational (or quietly sabotaging it), watch out for hostile robots and map traps lurking at every turn. At any moment, everything can go sideways.

5082020.name: 深夜閲覧 Midnight Reading：Showa Echoes

store_data.about_the_game:
■ Overview

Midnight Reading is a short horror adventure set in a Japanese school during the Showa era.

You play as a member of the school library committee. After school, the librarian asks you to retrieve several overdue books, sending you through the school to find them.

However, when midnight arrives, the school begins to take on a different appearance from the one you knew during the day.

And when you open one of the books you find—

Something happens without the protagonist realizing it.

■ Story

Autumn, 1981 — A Japanese School

After school.

The protagonist, a member of the school library committee, is asked by the librarian to retrieve books that have not been returned by their due dates.

To find the overdue books, the protagonist heads to the places where they were last checked out.

A silent school.

Classrooms that should be empty.

Books left behind in the school at night.

And strange stories written inside them.

The protagonist searches for the books, reads them, and returns them one by one.

■ Gameplay

· A choice-based horror adventure centered around the school library

· Choose one of three overdue books at the beginning of each chapter

· Explore the school to search for the missing books

· Something happens as you search for the books

· Choose one of three actions during supernatural events

· Your story changes based on both your choice of book and your actions

· Hidden internal parameters change according to your choices, leading to different endings

· Three main routes: Truth, Supernatural, and Records

· A True Route unlocked after completing all three routes

· A compact structure consisting of multiple short horror scenarios

■ Features

· An eerie atmosphere set in a Showa-era Japanese school and library

· Retro horror presentation

· Horror built around the act of reading a book itself

· Psychological horror where strange events gradually spread through a silent school

· A slow-burning horror experience built on unease and mystery rather than relying solely on sudden scares

· Multiple endings determined by your book and action choices

· A gameplay system where the seemingly ordinary act of returning a book becomes a key part of the story

· A world inspired by the atmosphere of Japanese schools during the Showa era, based on the creator's own experience of attending a Japanese school during the later Showa period

■ Controls

· Confirm / Select

Simple controls make the game easy for anyone to play.

■ Playtime

Approximately 30–45 minutes per playthrough

Approximately 2 hours to complete all routes

Includes multiple endings.

Playtime may vary depending on play style.

■ Genre

Horror / Adventure / Short Story / Choice-Based Novel

■ Content Warning

This game contains psychological horror, supernatural elements, and scenes designed to create a sense of unease.

Players who are sensitive to quiet horror or unsettling atmospheres are advised to take care when playing.

You have been brought here to be evaluated.

A machine examiner will present you with a series of questions, situations and visual tests. Every response you provide will be recorded and evaluated individually.

But there is something deeper beneath the surface. It is trying to reach you, tell you something and reveal layers hidden within the system.
What is the Examiner testing you for? Whose memories are these records you unlock? It seems that this time, answers may finally be given.

Sokolov Test is a short psychological science-fiction visual novel centered around choice, perception, identity and the ways a person responds when there may be no objectively correct answer.

Sokolov Test is also a standalone story connected to the wider world of N.U.E. No prior knowledge is required. Some names, records, and memories may prove more significant than they first appear.

store_data.about_the_game:
A LEGEND FORGED BY CHOICE

Britain is divided, its kingdoms consumed by war, and its ancient magic is disappearing. At the heart of the conflict stands a sword embedded in black stone—an artifact that has rejected kings, champions, and conquerors for generations.

Arthur never intended to claim a crown. He only needed a sword.

When the Oathblade answers his hand, a forgotten Camelot begins to rise and an ancient enemy awakens from the promises broken by those who ruled before him. To save Britain, Arthur must decide what kind of king he will become and whether the future written for him deserves to survive.



REIMAGINE THE LEGEND OF CAMELOT

King Arthur: Crown of Avalon is a mature, story-driven visual novel inspired by Arthurian mythology. Follow Arthur across three chapters as he faces fractured kingdoms, forbidden magic, ancient prophecies, dragons, Avalon, and the Hollow King.

Your dialogue choices shape Arthur's personality and responses. Lead with honor, authority, intelligence, honesty, or passion as the story develops toward a new interpretation of Camelot and its legendary king.

THREE SACRED BONDS

Arthur's journey is shaped by three powerful women, each with her own ambitions, responsibilities, and relationship with the future of Britain.

Guinevere represents the Crown—a brilliant commander and political leader determined to build a kingdom founded on accountability rather than blind obedience.

Morgan represents the Flame—a fiercely independent sorceress fighting to protect magical beings from royal ownership and control.

Nimue represents the Lake—the immortal guardian of Avalon, burdened by centuries of prophecy and the countless futures she has already witnessed.

Each relationship develops through its own narrative arc, combining romance, character development, intimate encounters, and mature animated scenes.

MATURE CONTENT AND ANIMATED SCENES

The game includes three consensual adult relationship sequences featuring nine animated NSFW scene loops.

Players who prefer a less explicit presentation can select romantic fade-to-black alternatives without changing the central story, relationships, or ending.

Animated scenes viewed during the story are permanently unlocked in the main-menu gallery, allowing them to be replayed whenever you wish. Scenes that have not yet been reached remain hidden until they are discovered naturally.

GAME FEATURES

Experience a complete three-chapter Arthurian fantasy story with three mature relationship arcs, nine animated adult scenes, character-shaping dialogue choices, full-screen cinematic event artwork, atmospheric music, event sound effects, Steam achievements, and a persistent unlockable gallery.

Encounter dragons, forbidden sorcery, political conflict, ancient kingdoms, broken prophecies, and a seductive new vision of Camelot.

Draw the sword. Question the prophecy. Build a kingdom capable of surviving its king.

5082210.name: Six Feet Under: The Mortician’s Last Stand

movies.name: Six Feet Under: The Mortician’s Last Stand

store_data.about_the_game:
Perdition Flats, Arizona Territory, 1889. You buried them all. You know every name, because you wrote them down. They are not staying buried.

SIX CHAMBERS, AND THEY FIRE IN ORDER

Every level you engrave one chamber. Chamber three bursts, chamber five ricochets, chamber one drinks the blood back. The order never changes, so the cylinder becomes a sequence you read as it turns — and the reload is where you live or die.

There is no screen-clearing light show at minute fifteen. The ceiling is low on purpose. You aim every shot from the first night to the last.

CLOSE IT WITH A FLICK

The cylinder turns as a ring around you, in the middle of the picture where your eyes already are. A bright notch comes round once. Snap it shut with a flick of the mouse, a click, or the spacebar — hit the notch and it closes early, miss it and you are standing in the open with an empty gun.

MARKS THAT TOUCH PAY LIKE A HAND

Put the same mark on neighbouring chambers and they pay out like a poker hand — a pair, three of a kind, a flush across all six. And the cylinder wraps, so chamber six touches chamber one. The bench draws a bracket under exactly the chambers making each hand, so you can see what you are holding and what you would be holding before you spend the level.

The real decision is deepen or widen. The same mark again can go deeper on a chamber it already occupies, feeding a two-chamber fusion, or take a second chamber and pay you a hand. One card, two directions, and you cannot have both.

HIRE WHAT YOU CAN AFFORD

A peddler's wagon rolls onto the field. The silver you pick off the ground buys laudanum, a full cylinder, a blessed nail — or a hand for hire. The Gambler fires fast and hits light. The Widow takes two seconds a shot and rarely misses. The Sawbones stitches you up where he stands. The Preacher reads over them until they give ground.

They walk where you walk, they do one thing each, and anything that touches them is killing them. They do not come back.

FIVE GROUNDS, AND EACH ONE BREAKS A HABIT

  • Boot Hill — the burying ground, and what is under it.
  • Perdition Flats — main street, and nobody on it.
  • The Railyard — you cannot back away at speed over ballast and sleepers.
  • The Salt Flats — no cover for nine miles, and a crosswind pulls every shot.
  • The Deep Mine — you see forty metres, the muzzle flash is your lamp, and the roof comes down: dust first, then the stone.

SIX WHO CAN WALK OUT THERE

The steady Mortician, the three-chamber Sawbones, the twelve-chamber Preacher, the charm-laden Widow, the ever-shuffling Gambler, and the Revenant who cannot be healed but takes another life off every boss.

THIRTEEN NIGHTS, AND SOMETHING AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SHAFT

A story campaign across three acts. Walk a funeral wagon home while the road ahead is held against you. Empty grave-pits that wake when you step into them. Run the town's ledger to the far fence with everything between you and it. Put down the Hanging Judge, cut down the Hanging Tree, and meet the Pale Rider on open ground with four waves of his own dead between you.

The mortician grows between the nights, in the Undertaker's Book — so a night is always six chambers and a steady hand. Finish all thirteen and ride them again at a harder tier; beating a night above your best pays its pages over.

AND THEN THE ENDLESS NIGHTS

Three survivor modes underneath the story: the fixed fifteen-minute night, the Long Night that never ends, and a daily grave on a seed everyone shares.

WOODCUT AND LAMPLIGHT

Every mark in the game is drawn, not painted — hatched ink on aged paper, one colour of brass, and a lot of dark.

WHAT IS IN IT

  • 13 authored nights across three acts, with 114 scripted scenes and a 19-beat epilogue
  • 5 grounds, each with a rule that changes how you play rather than how it looks
  • 6 characters whose chamber counts and core rules rewrite the run
  • 12 engravings and 10 two-chamber fusions, plus 10 gunsmith upgrades and 14 charms
  • 6 named bosses, 15 kinds of dead, and a 21-entry bestiary that fills as you meet them
  • 4 difficulty tiers, in the story as well as the survivor modes
  • 24 contracts and 10 stackable wagers that break a mechanic on purpose for better pay
  • 42 collection entries and 22 achievements
  • Adjustable gore, screen shake, flick sensitivity, and independent master, music and effects volume

You buried them once. Do the job properly this time.

The real decision is deepen or widen. The same mark again can go deeper on a chamber it already occupies, feeding a two-chamber fusion, or take a second chamber and pay you a hand. One card, two directions, and you cannot have both.

HIRE WHAT YOU CAN AFFORD

A peddler's wagon rolls onto the field. The silver you pick off the ground buys laudanum, a full cylinder, a blessed nail — or a hand for hire. The Gambler fires fast and hits light. The Widow takes two seconds a shot and rarely misses. The Sawbones stitches you up where he stands. The Preacher reads over them until they give ground.

They walk where you walk, they do one thing each, and anything that touches them is killing them. They do not come back.

FIVE GROUNDS, AND EACH ONE BREAKS A HABIT

  • Boot Hill — the burying ground, and what is under it.
  • Perdition Flats — main street, and nobody on it.
  • The Railyard — you cannot back away at speed over ballast and sleepers.
  • The Salt Flats — no cover for nine miles, and a crosswind pulls every shot.
  • The Deep Mine — you see forty metres, the muzzle flash is your lamp, and the roof comes down: dust first, then the stone.

SIX WHO CAN WALK OUT THERE

The steady Mortician, the three-chamber Sawbones, the twelve-chamber Preacher, the charm-laden Widow, the ever-shuffling Gambler, and the Revenant who cannot be healed but takes another life off every boss.

THIRTEEN NIGHTS, AND SOMETHING AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SHAFT

A story campaign across three acts. Walk a funeral wagon home while the road ahead is held against you. Empty grave-pits that wake when you step into them. Run the town's ledger to the far fence with everything between you and it. Put down the Hanging Judge, cut down the Hanging Tree, and meet the Pale Rider on open ground with four waves of his own dead between you.

The mortician grows between the nights, in the Undertaker's Book — so a night is always six chambers and a steady hand. Finish all thirteen and ride them again at a harder tier; beating a night above your best pays its pages over.

AND THEN THE ENDLESS NIGHTS

Three survivor modes underneath the story: the fixed fifteen-minute night, the Long Night that never ends, and a daily grave on a seed everyone shares.

WOODCUT AND LAMPLIGHT

Every mark in the game is drawn, not painted — hatched ink on aged paper, one colour of brass, and a lot of dark.

WHAT IS IN IT

  • 13 authored nights across three acts, with 114 scripted scenes and a 19-beat epilogue
  • 5 grounds, each with a rule that changes how you play rather than how it looks
  • 6 characters whose chamber counts and core rules rewrite the run
  • 12 engravings and 10 two-chamber fusions, plus 10 gunsmith upgrades and 14 charms
  • 6 named bosses, 15 kinds of dead, and a 21-entry bestiary that fills as you meet them
  • 4 difficulty tiers, in the story as well as the survivor modes
  • 24 contracts and 10 stackable wagers that break a mechanic on purpose for better pay
  • 42 collection entries and 22 achievements
  • Adjustable gore, screen shake, flick sensitivity, and independent master, music and effects volume

You buried them once. Do the job properly this time.
store_data.short_description: Six chambers. They fire in order. You decide what each one does. Engrave the cylinder one chamber at a time, close it with a flick of the wrist, and learn the sequence before it learns you — a hand-drawn Western horde shooter where everything you buried is walking back up the hill.

direction. Leave the safe border, draw a trail through the arena, and reconnect it to capture territory.

  • Combos, ranks and high-score competition

  • A multi-phase final boss

  • Unlockable character gallery

store_data.about_the_game:
WELCOME TO GROUND ZERO

After the great Gradixian invasion, the Shimigu Mining Corporation has never been the same. Neither has Mikey Minerals, one of the heroes of that war, who was recently found to owe the company TRILLIONS in college debt.

His repayment plan: the remote planet Dirt. Rich in minerals. Deeply infested. Extremely far from anyone who might help.

Strap into a mech-themed roguelike mining tower defense survivor. Battle hordes of aliens. Mine and make money for the COMPANY.

BUILD. MINE. SURVIVE.

Your base is power pylons, mining facilities, power plants and deadly turrets. Defend the HQ, push out into dangerous caverns, and dig up the precious artifacts and minerals buried down there.

Stay alert. Aliens, pirates and whatever else lives in the abyss all want the same rock you do. Live to mine another day.

FEATURES

  • Fourteen different mechs, from bullet hoses to a guy with a very large hammer

  • Survival mode: endless hordes, no quota, no end

  • Epic campaign mode spanning 4 planets of corporate-sponsored missions

  • Bullet hell in all its glory. Colors and explosions

  • A goofy story and silly voice acting

  • A full original soundtrack

  • Mining and base building, all for the bottom line

  • Local split-screen co-op for up to 4 pilots

  • Many different turret types for all your bug-squashing needs

  • Epic boss fights

MEET THE QUOTA

Upgrade and unlock powerful new mechs, exotic technologies, and better ways to move dirt. Spend your hard-earned cash at the company store. Clear levels to research your way across a vast tech tree.

And do not slack off on the mining, or you will fall behind the quota. The company notices.

GLORIOUS CO-OP

Fourteen mechs, every one a different job. Combine them with up to three friends alongside you in local split-screen.

  • The Uber Mech - ALL THE GUNS!

  • The Crusader - Make the aliens see the light!

  • The Sweeper - Scorched earth!

  • Bastion - Buff nearby turrets and stiffen the whole line!

  • Mech Donald's - You're gonna love this!

Or role-play as a Mining, Repair or Construction specialist and stay in your lane.

An officially licensed product of the Tom Lander universe by Heavy Photon.🐱‍🚀

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to Thrift Store Treasure, a relaxing hidden object game set in a cozy, cluttered secondhand shop overflowing with forgotten finds. This charming thrift store invites you to slow down, dig through the racks, and enjoy the simple satisfaction of turning clutter into treasure.

Browse through 10 charming chapters, each featuring hand-crafted hidden object scenes inspired by overstuffed thrift shops, dusty back rooms, donation bins, and vintage display shelves. Every location is designed to be cozy and inviting-perfect for players seeking a calm and satisfying experience.

Along your journey, enjoy a variety of laid-back mini-games that add playful variety without pressure. Assemble relaxing jigsaw puzzles, guide items through arrow escape mazes, unscrew layered planks, fix up broken finds, untangle knotted ropes, and serve customers by finding the exact hidden items they're shopping for.

With its gentle progression and diverse puzzle mechanics, Thrift Store Treasure is the perfect escape for fans fun puzzles and hidden object adventures. Whether you play for a few minutes or settle in for a longer session, the shop is always waiting and full of small treasures to discover.

Key Game Features:

- Cozy hidden object scenes set across a cluttered, charming thrift store

- 10 relaxing chapters to explore at your own pace

- Jigsaw, Arrow Escape, Screw Planks, Fix It, and Untangle mini-games

- Customer-serving hidden object scenes where you find exactly what shoppers need

- Warm, inviting secondhand-shop visuals and calming atmosphere

- Stress-free gameplay designed for relaxation and comfort

store_data.about_the_game:
Moonhollow is a top-down action-adventure where exploration, magical combat and discovery shape your journey through a mysterious world trapped beneath an endless night.

Play as Noctus, a small raven wielding lunar magic, and venture through a dark and enchanted land inhabited by corrupted creatures and wandering souls.

Explore beyond the obvious path, uncover the secrets of Moonhollow and gradually gain new ways to interact with a world that changes as your powers grow.

Bring Light Back to Moonhollow

Light your way and find the lost souls of those who once called Moonhollow home. Restore them and watch a forgotten village in the forest slowly come back to life.

Among those who return are former adventurers, craftspeople and wanderers, each bringing something of their own back with them. As the village is restored, new possibilities emerge for Noctus, and together, its inhabitants may hold the key to pushing back the darkness that consumed their world.

Explore a World That Opens With You

Discover abilities that let you reach places that once seemed inaccessible and find new foes along the way.

Master Lunar Combat

Combine close-range attacks, lunar magic and movement against creatures with distinct behaviors and weaknesses. Learn when to strike, evade and turn Noctus' growing arsenal of abilities to your advantage.

Tools Are More Than Weapons

What you learn in combat follows you into the world. Pull, reach, activate and manipulate your surroundings with abilities designed to serve multiple purposes, from defeating enemies to solving environmental puzzles and opening new routes.

store_data.about_the_game:
YOU ARE DEAD. THE DEPARTMENT DOES NOT CONSIDER THIS THE RELEVANT FACT.

The relevant fact is staffing.

Your admission has been deferred pending completion of temporary service. A binder has been issued. A window has been assigned.

The queue outside it has never been empty and did not form for you.

Report to the desk.

THE FILE STATES WHAT OCCURRED. THE APPLICANT STATES WHY.

Everyone arrives with a verified record. Everyone also arrives with a reason the record does not tell the whole story.

You get two questions a file. There are six.

PRESS them on the serious matter. Ask what they are SORRY for, and notice who they are sorry for. CROSS their account against the record and see whether it holds in the same order twice. Pull the administrative RECORDS and find out whether this file was lived or assembled. Ask the WITNESS queue, because somebody standing in it may have known them. Put an item from the drawer to the Division and ask them to IDENTIFY it.

Spend them on the wrong question and you have spent them.

Then bring down the stamp.

ASCEND. HOLD. DESCEND. REFER UPSTAIRS.

Simple. Official. Frequently catastrophic.

THE BINDER IS AUTHORITATIVE. THE BINDER IS ALSO WRONG.

Standing orders arrive while you work. Addenda correct instructions you have already followed. Rules are struck out after they have already cost somebody.

Management records whether you followed procedure.

The Kingdom records whom you allowed inside.

These are not the same measure. They will not agree.

Follow the binder without judgment and the Department may approve of your work. The Kingdom may not survive it.

EVERY STAMP CHANGES THE KINGDOM.

Your decisions do not disappear when the applicant leaves your window.

Reports arrive describing what has changed. Not as numbers, but as small disturbances in a place that should have been perfect.

Admit too freely and perfection begins to curdle.

There is a queue inside. There has never been a queue inside.

Refuse too freely and the reports grow shorter.

A place was set at the table this evening and not taken.

There is no morality meter explaining what you have done. There is only the Kingdom you created, and the one condition above ETERNAL COMFORT that the Department prints on every form and has never once claimed to have reached.

HOLD IS NOT MERCY. IT IS A LENGTH.

Some souls are assigned service and sent away. You decide how long. The ledger says what the term should be and nobody says it out loud.

Later they return, carrying a record of what they did with the time you gave them. A term that was too short did not finish its work, and the paperwork will say so in the flattest language available.

You will judge them again.

They will remember who sent them there.

NOT EVERY APPLICANT IS A SOUL.

Some are lying. Some are wearing another person's name. Some should never have reached your window at all.

Their paperwork is usually excellent.

That is the difficulty. The rules examine paperwork, and the paperwork passes.

Staff catch them, or nobody does.

THE TRAY FILLS WHETHER YOU READ IT OR NOT.

The Department writes to you. Distribution lists to be confirmed by response. Controlled copies to be acknowledged by their holder. A ruling on whether the kitchens may describe a soup as hearty without a substantiating ingredient.

Answer and it is filed. Every available answer is filed identically.

Other things arrive that are not the Department.

Some are merely tireless, and will keep arriving until you mark them.

Some are from the Damned, and are dressed as office mail. They want a reply, or they want you to open something. Everything wrong with them is on the page you are already reading. Information Technology will stop the first one. Information Technology has one interception per window.

THE DESK IS YOURS, WITHIN REASON.

Facilities permits the loose items to be arranged. It permits nothing else.

There is a set bolted under the monitor with a dial on it. Five stations and a position for off. No memo has ever mentioned it.

There is a telephone the Department did not issue and does not acknowledge. It blinks when the people you admitted yesterday have said something to each other. You may read it. You may press the praying hands. The queue continues to form while you do, and the clock does not care what you are looking at.

There are dice. There is a notebook nobody will ever read. There is a noticeboard in the break room with a motivational mop on it.

None of it is required. All of it costs the same nine minutes.

YOUR OWN FILE IS STILL OPEN.

Every rule you follow, every exception you make, and every soul you judge becomes part of your own record.

Complete your service and face a final review assembled from everything you allowed through the gate.

The Department thanks you for your service and reminds you that it has not yet been assessed.

store_data.about_the_game:
Kronon Era is a co-op horde survivor, made by one person, in Godot. It is in playtest on Steam and runs on its own dedicated server. Right now the game has one town, one 10-minute run and one boss. That is not much, and it is on purpose: first the foundation has to hold up with real people, then the content comes.

What you can play right now (v0.97)

  • Shared town: you arrive in a square with whoever else is online. Chat, friends, block, party. The square's portal takes the whole party into a run.

  • One run: Grey Plain, 10 minutes: the horde grows in five tiers, with swarms, charges, marches and elites in between. At the end, the Skeleton King: he falls apart, rebuilds himself from the bones and comes back for a second phase.

  • Three heroes + the Recruit: Bulwark holds and pulls the horde. Oracle is the only healing in the game. Blade kills fast and dies easy.

  • Seven weapons with seven levels each and a final evolution. 22 cards with rarity. Nine enemy types with elite traits.

  • Party level up: everyone sees everyone else's hand and can suggest a card to an ally.

  • Server-side collection: heroes drop as pieces from elites and bosses, each piece with its own grimoire. Forge (reroll, fusion, preservation, ascension), progression path, quests and a Codex that reveals itself as you play.

  • Market with no currency: you say what you want and a ceiling in materials; the system matches you with the cheapest offer. Nobody picks a seller.

  • The server has the final say: damage, kills, drops, purchases and even your character's movement speed are measured on the server side.

  • Challenge modes: straight to the King, with and without cards in the draw.

  • Automatic update with every version.

What is still rough

  • Only one run and one boss. The other five runs are designed in the code, but switched off.

  • Part of the art is placeholder. Some heroes and creatures already have their own sprite, others do not.

  • Forge and market run with no fee, on purpose, to measure the economy.

  • Translation only in the menus (30 languages).

  • The playtest is small. Each run opens a process on the server, so the number of players is limited while we measure the cost.

  • The economy resets at launch. Everything gathered during the playtest (pieces, materials, collection) goes away. The notice goes out at least one week in advance.

Join the Discord

The game changes because of the people who play it. The elite explosion was rejected by a player ("there is no time to get out") and fixed the same day. The Codex exists because someone lost 26 minutes trying to figure out what a weapon turned into.

If you want to test, complain, suggest or just follow along: . That is where the playtest keys, the version announcements and the polls on what comes first go out.

Roadmap

No dates. The order is the order of priority, and it changes with feedback.

Now (playtest)

  • Steam login instead of the provisional per-install identity.

  • Calibrate drops, forge and market with real data from the people playing.

  • Finish the art for the heroes and enemies that are still placeholder.

  • Translation of the rest of the game (cards, weapons, Codex).

Next

  • 20 and 30-minute runs, in chapters. Each chapter closes with a gate boss and switches the arena (pit, hall, corridors). Harder, faster, more dangerous, not just more numerous.

  • A more complete Skeleton King

Later

  • Biomes where the floor is the rule: Howling Glacier (ice with inertia), Spectral Current (currents that push you), Heart of the Volcano (lava that flashes before it burns). The floor physics is already in the code; the stages are not.

  • New bosses, each one asking for something beyond damage.

  • More heroes and grimoires.

Launch

  • "Coming soon" page on Steam, wishlist, playtest closed and paid launch.

  • Economy reset, with the Codex possibly preserved.

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to a Paradise That No Longer Exists

In the distant future, virtual sensory reconstruction has advanced far enough to deceive human perception itself.People can enter digitally reconstructed worlds, touch objects that do not exist, hear sounds that never occurred, and give forgotten memories a tangible form once again.

Your wife, Ephoros, a neural science engineer, died in an accident two years ago.You only intended to sort through the files she left behind in the virtual world.But an unexpected incident leads you somewhere you were never meant to reach—a beautiful, silent, and fractured [LOST] Paradise.

Search for the Truth Between Two Worlds

404Rander combines two interconnected forms of exploration: a simulated 2D desktop system and 3D semi-open environments.

Explore a Computer from the Future,Navigate a simulated desktop environment. Browse files, launch programs, examine archived data, and search for anomalies hidden deep within the system.Some files contain nothing more than ordinary information.Others... may not want to be found.

As your investigation continues, the computer will gradually become more than a safe window through which you observe another world.

Step Beyond the Screen

Leave the desktop behind and enter 3D spaces constructed from data, memories, and fragmented sensations.

Explore semi-open environments filled with abandoned facilities and anomalous landscapes. Search for key objects, environmental clues, and hidden information as you piece together what happened.

Something discovered on the desktop may become the key to navigating the world beyond it.

And something you encounter in that world may change what awaits you on the other side of the screen.

A Sci-Fi Story About Memory, Death, and the Self

404Rander is built around an original science-fiction setting exploring virtual reality, consciousness, perception, and digital existence.

As you venture deeper, you will encounter remnants of corporations, experimental facilities, technological archives, and people who have long since disappeared—all fragments of a larger story surrounding Ephoros' death.

There is no omniscient narrator to tell you what really happened.Files, programs, environments, images, sounds—even the system itself—can become part of the narrative.And discovering the truth does not necessarily mean finding an answer.When you finally reach the end, the choice remains yours:

Face it. Understand it.

Or—reject it, and bury it with your own hands.

An Experimental Work of Interactive Art

404Rander is also an experimental visual work created through the medium of video games.

Blending avant-garde graphic design, science-fiction interfaces, surreal spaces, environmental storytelling, and meticulously crafted cinematics, the game explores how UI, imagery, environments, and interaction itself can become part of the narrative.

Rather than focusing on combat or mechanically intensive gameplay, 404Rander places greater emphasis on:

An immersive science-fiction narrative and psychological horror atmosphere

Exploration across both a simulated 2D desktop and 3D environments

A richly developed world told through archives and environmental storytelling

Experimental concept art and visual design

Carefully crafted cinematics and narrative sequences

Discovering the story through observation, reading, exploration, and puzzle-solving

If you enjoy slowly losing yourself in an unfamiliar world, reading files you were never meant to find, and piecing together a story that has already fallen apart—

Welcome to 404Rander.

Please remember: everything you see is only perception.

store_data.about_the_game:
You never lose the shores you leave.

Keepshore is a calm 3D town-builder that spans nine ages of human ingenuity — from one thatched hut on a wild coast to a gas-lit city of iron, glass and electric light.

Raise buildings. Staff them with people who have names. Wire raw goods into production chains, sell into a market that actually moves, and grow a settlement you're proud to look at.

No combat. No failure state. No timers you have to pay to skip. Just the town you're building — and the next good idea you have for it.

  • Build from a catalog of 600+ hand-made buildings across nine ages

  • Grow a living town of villagers with names, moods, jobs and opinions

  • Leave — settling a new island is the only way to advance the age, and every island you leave keeps paying you forever

Start with a hut. End with a city.

Every game begins the same humble way: an empty, procedurally generated island and one place to put your first home. People move in. Producers staff themselves. Goods start landing in the storehouse without a single click of harvesting.

Then the questions get interesting. Where should the watermill go? Which producers want to sit shoulder-to-shoulder? What is this whole quarter waiting on?

  • Terrain matters. Every producer has ground it loves — a quarry on rocky hill, a saltern on sand. The Build menu tells you the bonus before you place it.

  • Placement is a puzzle. Workshop districts, supply chains, comfort venues, roads, rail and the electric grid all reward the shape of your town, not just its size.

  • Bottlenecks glow. A producer that's starving floats a red ember; one with no worker glows amber. Click it and the panel names the exact good it's short of.

  • Buildings improve by working. Mastery stars accrue on their own; paid upgrades stack on top; a perfected building picks a permanent Mastery Path.

Ore into ingots into tools. Grain into flour into bread. Over a hundred and fifty goods, wired together into chains you can read at a glance.

Nine ages — and you leave every one behind

Ages don't unlock from a menu. An island is locked forever to the age you settled it in. To reach the next age you must earn your Settlement Charter, load the boats, and sail for a brand-new island.

When you go, the old island freezes exactly as you left it — you can never return to it. You carry a quarter of its stockpile as a launch grant, and from that day it sends a daily tribute home to your treasury. Forever.

Nine islands, nine ages, one kingdom. Stone. Bronze. Iron. Classical. Medieval. Renaissance. Enlightenment. Steam. Electric.

Each age is its own world of buildings, goods and problems — bronze smelters and salt pans, guild halls and windmills, printing houses and observatories, foundries and railway stations, telephone exchanges and power stations. Nothing past 1899. No magic, no future tech.

Night is not just darker. Forges throw sparks, cathedral glass burns, salon lanterns drift, marquees chase around the picture-house, and searchlights rake the sky over the aerodrome.

No two islands. No two runs.

Every island is generated fresh — a wandering coastline of coves, bays and lagoons, with rivers, lakes, headlands and highlands, drawn across six climates from tropical to subarctic to arid. Your town looks completely different depending on where you land.

A town full of people who notice you

Your villagers aren't a population counter. They have names, vocations, dispositions and moods. They wander, they talk, they comment on what you just built. You can rename them, favourite them, and follow one across the island.

Name your island. Name your neighbourhoods. Raise a Heraldry Hall and your realm becomes a noble House with a name and a motto — and from then on your own household rides at the head of the age's great spectacles, and its words ring out over the field when it wins.

Something is always happening

Travellers turn up at the quay with a choice to make. Market days spike. A gambler offers you a pot and a chance to press your luck. A rainbow pays out. The chronicle records a small kindness by name. Sometimes the world just goes strange for a week.

And every age has its own signature spectacle, gated behind a building you chose to raise:

  • The Great Hunt — Stone. The hunters come home with a rotating quarry, and roughly one in five is legendary.

  • The Great Moot — Bronze. The kindreds gather, and one of them takes the honour.

  • The Oenach — Iron. The clans muster at the standing stones for the great assembly.

  • The Games — Classical. Chariots, athletes and the olive crown, with a rotating victor faction.

  • The Grand Tourney — Medieval. Jousts and craft contests, and a champion guild crowned.

  • The Carnevale — Renaissance. Masques and cloth-of-gold over the playhouse.

  • The Balloon Ascent & the Salon — Enlightenment. Montgolfier marvels and the brightest evening in town.

  • The Grand Exposition — Steam. A World's Fair whose grandeur scales with the city you raised.

  • The Air Show — Electric. Pylon races and barnstormers, and a flying team crowned.

Each one crowns a winner, throws a real festival over your town, and records the victor in your Chronicle. Collecting all of them is a chase that lasts a whole age.

Always something to chase — almost none of it mandatory

Eight daily quests. Weekly projects that pay a Perk Point. Ventures. Landmarks hidden out on the terrain waiting to be found. Daily find-hunts tucked into the scenery. Runaway critters to catch. A Research Cabinet to fund. Wonders to commission.

The critical path stays light and always doable. The hard stuff is a destination you choose to walk to — never a toll gate.

Over five hundred lifetime achievements, a building collection, an almanac of recipes and a chronicle of your town's own history — a compendium you will not finish in a hurry.

A market with a memory

Prices move with supply. Selling floods a good and drops its price; buying drains it and lifts it. One commodity is hot each day and pays a premium. Read the rise, hold the dip, land a Perfect Sale, run a caravan, work the exchange — or ignore all of it and just fill orders.

Specialize. You can never take it all.

Perk Points come from every level, and there is a firm rule behind the tree: no player ever reaches more than half of it. Your Specialist Focus is a fixed budget. Kingdom Doctrines lock each other out permanently and can't be un-picked.

So the question is never "what do I unlock next?" It's who is this kingdom? The layout optimizer, the market shark, the comfort-blanket city painter, the collector — each has a real lane, and none of them can walk all of them.

Play for five minutes. Or five hours.

  • The town works while you're gone. The Nightwatch keeps your storehouses filling overnight — you come back to a full report, not a stalled town.

  • Daily content follows the real calendar. Quests, login streaks and weekly projects roll over once a real day.

  • Missing days is fine. Skipped days pay a Rest Bonus and streaks have a catch-up window. Nothing punishes you for having a life.

  • Nothing is on a leash. No energy bars, no ads, no progression sold in a shop.

In short

  • A peaceful 3D island town-builder across nine ages, Stone to Electric — hard-capped at 1899

  • 600+ buildings with real production chains, terrain bonuses, upgrades and mastery

  • Procedural islands in six climates — every run a new coastline, every town a new shape

  • A living town: named villagers, moods, wandering visitors, districts, your own noble House

  • A market that moves, orders, contracts, caravans and a commodity exchange

  • A perk tree you can never finish — permanent specialization, real trade-offs

  • Age-signature spectacles, festivals, landmarks, find-hunts and a chronicle of your own history

  • Offline-first — the whole game plays with no connection

  • No combat, no losing, no pay-to-win

Keep the shore. It keeps sending.

Travellers turn up at the quay with a choice to make. Market days spike. A gambler offers you a pot and a chance to press your luck. A rainbow pays out. The chronicle records a small kindness by name. Sometimes the world just goes strange for a week.

And every age has its own signature spectacle, gated behind a building you chose to raise:

  • The Great Hunt — Stone. The hunters come home with a rotating quarry, and roughly one in five is legendary.

  • The Great Moot — Bronze. The kindreds gather, and one of them takes the honour.

  • The Oenach — Iron. The clans muster at the standing stones for the great assembly.

  • The Games — Classical. Chariots, athletes and the olive crown, with a rotating victor faction.

  • The Grand Tourney — Medieval. Jousts and craft contests, and a champion guild crowned.

  • The Carnevale — Renaissance. Masques and cloth-of-gold over the playhouse.

  • The Balloon Ascent & the Salon — Enlightenment. Montgolfier marvels and the brightest evening in town.

  • The Grand Exposition — Steam. A World's Fair whose grandeur scales with the city you raised.

  • The Air Show — Electric. Pylon races and barnstormers, and a flying team crowned.

Each one crowns a winner, throws a real festival over your town, and records the victor in your Chronicle. Collecting all of them is a chase that lasts a whole age.

Always something to chase — almost none of it mandatory

Eight daily quests. Weekly projects that pay a Perk Point. Ventures. Landmarks hidden out on the terrain waiting to be found. Daily find-hunts tucked into the scenery. Runaway critters to catch. A Research Cabinet to fund. Wonders to commission.

The critical path stays light and always doable. The hard stuff is a destination you choose to walk to — never a toll gate.

Over five hundred lifetime achievements, a building collection, an almanac of recipes and a chronicle of your town's own history — a compendium you will not finish in a hurry.

A market with a memory

Prices move with supply. Selling floods a good and drops its price; buying drains it and lifts it. One commodity is hot each day and pays a premium. Read the rise, hold the dip, land a Perfect Sale, run a caravan, work the exchange — or ignore all of it and just fill orders.

Specialize. You can never take it all.

Perk Points come from every level, and there is a firm rule behind the tree: no player ever reaches more than half of it. Your Specialist Focus is a fixed budget. Kingdom Doctrines lock each other out permanently and can't be un-picked.

So the question is never "what do I unlock next?" It's who is this kingdom? The layout optimizer, the market shark, the comfort-blanket city painter, the collector — each has a real lane, and none of them can walk all of them.

Play for five minutes. Or five hours.

  • The town works while you're gone. The Nightwatch keeps your storehouses filling overnight — you come back to a full report, not a stalled town.

  • Daily content follows the real calendar. Quests, login streaks and weekly projects roll over once a real day.

  • Missing days is fine. Skipped days pay a Rest Bonus and streaks have a catch-up window. Nothing punishes you for having a life.

  • Nothing is on a leash. No energy bars, no ads, no progression sold in a shop.

In short

  • A peaceful 3D island town-builder across nine ages, Stone to Electric — hard-capped at 1899

  • 600+ buildings with real production chains, terrain bonuses, upgrades and mastery

  • Procedural islands in six climates — every run a new coastline, every town a new shape

  • A living town: named villagers, moods, wandering visitors, districts, your own noble House

  • A market that moves, orders, contracts, caravans and a commodity exchange

  • A perk tree you can never finish — permanent specialization, real trade-offs

  • Age-signature spectacles, festivals, landmarks, find-hunts and a chronicle of your own history

  • Offline-first — the whole game plays with no connection

  • No combat, no losing, no pay-to-win

Keep the shore. It keeps sending.
store_data.short_description: A calm 3D island town-builder spanning nine ages, from stone huts to electric streets. Raise workshops, wire production chains, work a living market, and grow a town that keeps producing while you're away. Settle a new island to advance the age — every shore you leave sends tribute home forever.

store_data.about_the_game:
Lights. Camera. YOU do the voices.

Dub Rumble is a party game about dubbing scenes live on the mic. Pick a scene, cast your friends into roles, and when the video rolls, you improvise the dialogue. Watch the takes back, cry laughing, and vote for the best performance.

How a round works

  • Pick a Dub Pack and a scene
  • Cast the roles — everyone gets a part
  • The scene plays and the mic is live: improvise your dub
  • Watch every take back and vote for the winner

Play your way

  • Couch party — pass the mic around one machine
  • Online — host a room over Steam: invite friends, join by code, or use the room browser. Peer-to-peer, no servers needed
  • Solo — practice takes and export your best performances

Make it yours

  • Steam Workshop — build your own Dub Packs from your videos and images, share them, and subscribe to packs made by others with one-tap import. Only upload content you have the rights to
  • Recordings — export finished dubs straight to your PC
  • Steam achievements, cloud saves, friend invites, and rich presence
  • Compatible with Choicer Voicer packs

A microphone is required. An internet connection is required for online play.

store_data.about_the_game:
Can you resolve your bizarre, recurring dream?

The Zoo is a short, hand-painted interactive story about a recurring dream. Well, maybe it's more like a nightmare. Spoiler alert, the dream always ends with an animal attacking you. So yes, let's call it a nightmare. But aside from the deadly animals, the Zoo is mostly benign. 

Back to the point. You're having a recurring dream about a zoo. The question is, can you work within the constraints of the dream to force a different ending? A non-lethal ending, perhaps?

Wander the Welcome Pavilion, African Savanna, Arctic Experience, Monkey Island, and the RainForest. Talk to what and who you find there. Every choice is yours, but the dream keeps its own time, and if you linger too long, something awful is always waiting.

Features

  • A complete, hand-painted narrative

  • Explore a dream-logic zoo across distinct, storybook exhibits

  • A recurring-nightmare loop that rewards curiosity over caution

  • Multiple endings, and more than one way to finally escape the zoo

  • An original score that drifts between dream, dread, and the flat hum of waking life

  • A sit-down-and-finish experience, meant for a single quiet evening

The Zoo is proudly built with Godot and Ink, and all scenes are painted in Procreate.

store_data.about_the_game:
Coindrop Dungeon is a Pachinko inspired dungeon crawler. Your coins and pegs from the board are your inventory. Explore builds, create synergies and break the curse that keeps you in the ever changing dungeon.

The heroes are cursed to roam this dungeon in order to discover and face the dark secret that is keeping them hostage.

Defeat the sins of your past to restore your soul!

Game mechanics

The game relies on a deck-building of both pegs for the board and the coins you drop on a Pachinko inspired board. You can acquire new ones as you progress, place them cleverly in order to maximize their potential and combine coins into more powerful ones to become even more powerful.

Each coin and peg have powerful effects, and by combining them you create combos and synergies to defeat your enemies.

Each level in the dungeon is unique and offers you opportunities to discover new gear while trying to stay alive by slaying enemies.

store_data.about_the_game:
Grand Snow Rider is an open-world action-adventure simulator about fighting your way through an extreme snowstorm.

Take on the role of Lucy and set out to recover abandoned vehicles scattered across snow-covered locations. Clear blocked roads, locate missing cars and their keys, fight off troublemakers, and bring every recovered vehicle back to safety.

But there’s a catch: the more progress you make, the worse the weather gets.

CLEAR YOUR OWN PATH

Snow isn't just scenery — it's part of the gameplay.

Deep snow can slow Lucy down, block roads, and leave vehicles completely stuck. Take control of snow-clearing machinery and carve your own routes through buried roads and paths to reach abandoned vehicles.

FIND THE CAR. FIND THE KEY. BRING IT BACK.

Finding a vehicle is only the beginning.

Mark its location on your GPS, track down the hidden key, and be ready to fight for it. Local troublemakers aren't going to stand by and let you take their prize without a snowball fight.

Win, and you can return to the vehicle and drive it back to the parking area.

Lose? Well... you'll have to go get that key again.

SNOWBALLS ARE WEAPONS

Nobody needs real bullets here.

Fight groups of troublemakers in snowball battles and use your equipment to gain the upper hand. They can knock Lucy down, steal the key, and send you right back to where you started.

Get back up, return to the fight, and finish the job.

FOUR GADGETS. FOUR DIFFERENT TOOLS.

Lucy has access to four unusual gadgets, each designed for a different problem.

Fight enemies, melt snow, free frozen vehicles, and manipulate cars when brute force isn't enough. Choosing the right tool can make recovering the next vehicle considerably easier.

EVERY CAR HAS A STORY

The vehicles you recover aren't just numbers on a checklist.

Throughout each mission, Jay stays in contact with Lucy over the radio, sharing stories about the cars you discover and the people who owned them.

What begins as another recovery job gradually becomes a journey through the lives of people caught in the storm.

FROM A PARK TO AN ENTIRE STATE

Your journey takes place across three increasingly large locations:

Park → City → State

Start small in the park, move on to the city, and eventually face the storm across a much larger region.

As the search area grows, you'll need to change your approach — and find new ways to locate vehicles buried somewhere in the snow-covered world.

THE STORM KEEPS GETTING WORSE

Every vehicle you recover and register brings you one step closer to completing the job.

At the same time, the snowfall intensifies.

Visibility gets worse. Snow gets deeper. Roads become harder to navigate, and both Lucy and her vehicles become increasingly vulnerable to getting stuck.

Find the cars. Recover the keys. Clear the roads. Bring them home — before the storm takes over.

store_data.about_the_game:
Death was meant to be an ending. In Fractunum, it became a wound.

Project: Fractunum is a 2D dark fantasy pixel-art Metroidvania built around atmospheric exploration, precise combat, and a fragmented narrative. Awakened between life and death, you must cross a world broken by a forbidden pursuit of immortality and discover the truth behind your own fractured existence.

THE WORLD THAT REFUSED DEATH

Long ago, the rulers of three realms attempted to break the boundary of death. Their ritual failed, corrupting the natural order and leaving the world scarred. You awaken without a name or memory—neither fully alive nor truly dead. To learn what you have become, you must follow the remnants of their legacy.

EXPLORE A FRACTURED WORLD

Journey through interconnected regions filled with forgotten ruins, hidden paths, deadly creatures, and buried secrets. Gain new abilities, revisit earlier locations, and open routes that were once beyond your reach.

MASTER PRECISE, PUNISHING COMBAT

Study enemy patterns, choose your moment to strike, and survive unforgiving encounters where timing, positioning, and restraint matter as much as aggression.

CONFRONT ANCIENT HORRORS

Face grotesque enemies and formidable bosses shaped by a failed quest for immortality. Each victory draws you deeper into the mystery of the fracture and the powers that created it.

RECLAIM YOUR IDENTITY

Recover fragments of memory and uncover a dark story about mortality, ambition, and the price of refusing death.

A DARK FANTASY IN PIXEL ART

Enter a bleak world brought to life through detailed pixel art, haunting environments, and a brooding atmosphere.

store_data.about_the_game:
Jack and Sylvia are a couple.

Life put debt in the way of each of them, and each faced the same choice: a long term of servitude, or prison and forced labor. Both chose service. They met serving their previous master — he as a guard, she as a cook — and they chose to become a couple. A love under hard circumstances.

Now they stand before the doors of the mansion of their new, eccentric mistress: Talia Godroy.

What life is waiting for them here? Will she be strict? What will their work be like? Will their love flourish, or wither along the way?

A story about a conservative couple meeting a very open eccentric mistress and her friend. Whether you focus on your lovely girlfriend Sylvia or fall deep into lust is entirely your own choice.

WHAT'S INSIDE

  • 15+ hours per playthrough — considerably more to see everything

  • No season 1, no part1, no early access. A fully finished game with endings. 

  • 16 endings across branching routes

  • 60,000+ lines of dialogue and narration

  • 12,000+ rendered images and 1000+ high quality animations

  • 100+ sex scenes

  • Choice and consequence of those choices.

  • In-game event flowchart for tracking routes across replays

EVERY PATH IS A DIFFERENT STORY

In Her Service is not one story with optional scenes bolted on. Your choices decide who Jack and Sylvia become to each other.

Hold the line — and it stays a slow-burn story about a couple keeping their footing in someone else's house.
Let go together — and it becomes something shared, with Talia, with Henry, with each other watching.
Let go separately — and it becomes something else entirely. Secrets. Jealousy. Cheating.

Sixteen endings. None of them is the "true" one. An in-game event flowchart tracks what you've found and what you've missed, so replays are targeted instead of blind.

HIGH QUALITY ANIMATIONS

THE HOUSE

Sylvia — Jack's girlfriend. She loves (you) deeply, and for that love she is willing to endure a great deal. You met two years ago, serving a different master together, and you have been together ever since. She is a conservative woman. Beyond you, she loves her daughter just as much.

Talia — Talia Godroy of House Godroy. An eccentric noblewoman of high status, she always seems to be in control. For some reason, until your arrival she lived alone in her mansion. Why alone? What is her past? And is the face she shows the world only a façade...?

Fiona — Talia's Best Friend. A noblewoman of high status. Behind a face that could captivate entire realms hides an intellect capable of outmaneuvering anyone. She always comes out on top, and her motives are rarely legible.

content_descriptors.notes:
This game is intended for adults only. It contains frequent, explicit depictions of sexual acts and full nudity. All characters depicted are adults aged 18 or over.

The story centers on themes of romance, infidelity, cheating, partner swapping. Depending on the choices the player makes, this can include the protagonist's girlfriend having sex with other characters, the protagonist being unfaithful, and both partners doing so together or separately. All sexual activity depicted is between consenting adults and never forced. The game contains no depictions of sexual assault or non-consensual sex, and no BDSM content.

The premise involves the two main characters under indentured servitude to repay a debt. This arrangement is contractual and there are rules where both nobles and commoners have to obey by. The game does not depict physical abuse, sexual abuse or violence of any kind, it contains no drug abuse, no self-harm and no graphic violence.

Other themes some players may be sensitive to include jealousy, emotional distress, and the breakdown of a romantic relationship. Several story paths end unhappily. The game contains occasional depictions of alcohol use and tabacco use.

store_data.about_the_game:
You don't choose your spirit animal. It watches first, quietly testing who you are, then it chooses you back: a bear, a wolf, or a capybara that is somehow always chill. Once matched, it moves right onto your screen.

It settles on a small patch of land at the edge of your display. It wanders around, gathers berries, catches fish, and rests under trees. You can leave it alone or interact directly: drag food over, point out the lake, or let it explore on its own.

It lives its own life on your screen, mostly content on its own. But not entirely: sometimes it needs your hand to reach a stone, catch a fish, or get through a hard season. Your daily work fuels its world. The more you type and click, the more it eats, grows, and prepares for winter. It isn't a rigid productivity app, just a quiet companion you help become its best self, one that thrives whenever you get things done.

Watch the seasons change, discover beehives, and unlock new skins from ancient stones. It already knows which spirit is yours. All that's left is to meet it.

store_data.about_the_game:
From 18 to retirement — build your wealth


Capitalize is a financial life sim: job, budget, housing, broker, business… and time working for you (or against you).

Learn the long game by playing — compound interest, diversification, the 4% rule, DCA, company treasury, going public — no boring lectures, with a real life to steer.

What you manage

  • Budget & bank — income, expenses, priorities, safety net
  • Career & training — apply, skill up, change trajectory
  • Housing — rent or buy, costs, real-estate wealth
  • Broker — ETFs, stocks, bonds, gold & commodities, scheduled DCA (multi-plan)
  • Business — launch ventures, cash flow, dividends, treasury, company health; in realistic mode, IPOs and employee equity
  • Vehicles & daily life — transport, breakdowns, theft, surprises, constant trade-offs

Local game modes

Four ways to play outside online rankings:
  • Guided tutorial — tour the apps and one year-end report, learn without pressure
  • Year by year — broader pace, ideal for the big picture
  • Month by month (normal run) — every month counts: budget, markets, decisions
  • Realistic (month by month) — the same pace with more hazards (breakdowns, life events, health, tougher markets…)

Online Career

A mode separate from local runs: permanent profile, runs to retirement, dedicated leaderboards.
  • Normal run (month by month) — net worth & financial independence (FI) age boards
  • Realistic (month by month) — dedicated board, harsher conditions
  • Seasons (S1, then S2…) and live tops

End of run & sharing

  • Retirement bilan: net worth, compounding, 4% rule, wealth curve
  • Capture and share your bilan (image clipboard, Steam, Discord…)
  • Local scoreboard + online career

Built to teach

  • Educational simulation — not personalised financial advice
  • In-game documentation (ETFs, DCA, 4%, diversification, business, IPO, company health…)
  • Guided tutorial to learn the apps
  • Life events and choices that hit mood, health and cash (especially in realistic mode)

Who is it for?

  • Anyone curious about budget, markets and wealth
  • Fans of chill-but-deep management / life sims
  • Streamers & players who love optimising a life over decades

Capitalize — JL Games Studio (Switzerland). Build your financial empire… one month (or one year) at a time.

Slaughter hordes of enemies, gain experience, and level up. Create your own build, upgrade your weapons, and unlock new magical abilities. Combine guns and magic however you like

store_data.about_the_game:
"It starts with the soil!" ー Did you know? Building and maintaining a proper soil ecosystem is one of the secrets behind growing a successful, organized, and delicious farm that can last for generations. In Dokimon: The Living Soil, you've completed your journey as a powerful Dokimon Ranger and are ready to build a peaceful new life in a small town in countryside Japan.

Plan, build, and decorate your new home and growing farm as you learn about this cute little town, raise helpful Dokimon, and discover real-world applicable farming knowledge and techniques through an easy-to-follow, gamified farming RPG experience.

Game Features

  • Decorate your home and build your dream farm in a small town in countryside Japan

  • Capture, befriend, and raise monsters to help you on the farm, explore caves, and battle alongside you

  • Learn real-world applicable farming, gardening, soil, and home-farm knowledge and techniques (optional)

  • Visit shrines and discover new monsters, magic, and skills to use on the farm or in battle

  • Unlock new skills, techniques, and knowledge through a skill tree as you grow and level up

  • Dive into a roguelike cave system and battle monsters in search of treasure, experience, and rare items

The Haruna Region

Famous for its beautiful natural scenery, shrines, mountains, farms, and hot springs, Haruna is a treasured region of Gunma, Japan, far away from the busy bustle of Tokyo. In Dokimon: The Living Soil, you'll explore the Japanese countryside, fish, farm, scavenge, dive for rare items, raise Dokimon, and simply live life to its fullest!

Go on adventures, stay home, rest and decorate, tend to your farm, or dive into the cave system when you need some excitement! A living, breathing world combining a cozy farming life sim, monster-taming RPG, and exploration adventure is waiting for you. Kick back, relax, and enjoy your peaceful new life in Haruna.

store_data.about_the_game:
Pixel Nightshift: The Vesta Protocol

A pixel art psychological horror short story.

Step into the shoes of a night shift operator at Vesta Robotics. Dressed in isolation, your job is simple: process shipments, manage terminal requests, and clear daily quotas. However, as the nights progress, subtle anomalies begin to breach your routine.

The Night Shift

Distant echoes fill the empty facility. Inside, it is just you, the terminal, and endless shipping crates waiting to be dispatched.

A Rigid Routine

Read orders at the terminal, collect parts from the dark warehouse, pack the cargo, and load the delivery truck. A structured routine that slowly begins to fracture.

System Verification

Before starting each shift, you must complete security verifications at the terminal. Nine unique protocol mini games designed to test your focus, though the system grows increasingly erratic.

The Unraveling

Shifted boxes, flickering lights, and figures appearing in the dark. As the facility glitches, small choices ripple forward toward one of two distinct endings.

Key Features

  • Ten atmospheric night shifts with escalating psychological tension

  • Nine distinct verification mini games with unique mechanics

  • Handcrafted 320x180 pixel art with classic CRT terminal aesthetics

  • Two separate endings shaped by your choices

  • A focused 30 to 45 minute narrative experience

store_data.about_the_game:
Pull a string down, feel the tension build under your finger, and let go. The physics does the rest, flinging you up toward the next string. Land, take aim, pull again.

Pull too far and the string snaps. It does not come back, and the gap it leaves will still be there on the way down.

Every string you touch rings out a note, so your climb writes its own music as you go. The whole register lifts an octave for every 1500 meters you gain, which means the higher you get, the brighter the whole thing sounds.

You get one life per run. That sounds harsher than it feels: a climb takes a few minutes, and the next one is a single button away.

Sound you can feel

Every note is made the moment you pluck it, thick strings speak low, thin ones ring high, and the register climbs with you. Chain your launches and it answers with a rising run.

Some strings have plans of their own

A violet string is a rocket, as long as you give it clean air underneath. An ember sets you alight, and the next string will not be able to hold you. A balloon slows the whole world to a drift. A rainbow throws you much further than you meant to go. Strings wear out and tear, too, so the ones you have already spent will not be waiting for you on the way back down.

The drifters are a long way from home, and the only road back is up. None of them can make that climb alone that is what you are for.

Zap, Twang, Chime, Ping, Thump, Cackle, Hush and Fizz. Each one is trying to reach a different planet. Each one is sure this is the run that finally does it.

Features

  • One pointer, and that is the whole control scheme. Press, drag, release.

  • Procedurally generated, so no two climbs are ever the same.

  • A combo system with a real ceiling. Three flawless links in a single flight and you ignite.

  • Eight drifters to unlock, each earned a different way.

  • Step away mid-climb and come back to your altitude whenever you like.

  • Runs last minutes. Restarting takes a second.

  • Fully offline. No launcher, no login, no account.
