store_data.about_the_game:
A tiny survival story in a drawer

You are a button lost in a drawer. You have no weapon to swing. Instead the small things around you fight for you — a paperclip orbiting your body, a thumbtack firing off, a coin ricocheting, a button battery arcing. All you decide is where to stand.

The boss ends the run, not a timer

A chapter is the run. Its length, its intensity, and the boss waiting at the end are all fixed — replay a chapter and you get the same fight, so skill is the only thing that changes the result. You do not win by outlasting a clock. You win by putting down the Padlock, the Paper Shredder, the Drafting Compass.

  • Drawer — the boss arrives around 14 minutes in. Open from the start.
  • Desk Top — about 18 minutes. 1.7x enemy power, 1.6x rewards.
  • Pencil Case — about 22 minutes. 2.4x enemy power, 2.2x rewards. Unlocked by clearing Desk Top, or with 500 buttons.
  • Challenge — it never ends. A fixed seed means every player fights the same layout, and every three minutes a chapter boss comes calling: the Stapler, the Padlock, the Paper Shredder, the Drafting Compass, then around again. Killing one does not end the run. Whatever you score before you fall goes to a Steam leaderboard.

Everything arrives on a clock

Each kind of trash has its own entry time and ramp, and for elites the period is the tier — one every 3 minutes, one every 8, one every 14. A short run never even meets the 14-minute tier.

Bosses and elites each push you around in their own way.
  • Scatter — flings nearby trash outward. The burst itself is harmless, but the bodies land in the lanes you were kiting through.
  • Sweep — telegraphs a corridor for 0.7 seconds, then shoves everything inside it one way. One lane empties; the horde piles up at the far end.
  • Spin — grabs everything near it and orbits it for 1.6 seconds before releasing along the tangent. You can read where each body will land while it is still going around.
  • Ram — throws you along its charge line and cuts your input for 0.6 seconds. Not a slow. No control at all.

Eraser blocks, bottle caps and batteries sit on the floor, so there is no straight line across the arena. Supply chests, candy and magnets drop every 24-36 seconds — and going to fetch one is exactly the moment your safe orbit breaks.

Your build caps at 6 + 4

14 weapons, 8 supplies. A run holds 6 weapons and 4 supplies, and once a category is full new items stop appearing in your level-up choices entirely. The question is never what to take. It is what to give up.

  • Evolutions — every weapon has one. Max a weapon (Lv.6) while holding its paired supply and the EVO card appears on your next level-up. Thumbtack + magnifier shard = Meteor Tack.
  • Six synergies — carry the thumbtack and the button battery together and hits arc to a nearby enemy. Coin + magnet shard, paperclip + magnet shard, rubber band + thread, pencil lead + eraser, and safety pin + glass marble each earn their own name too.
  • The button is the character — the skin you equip decides your starting weapon. Thumbtack, needle, pencil lead, coin, glass marble: five different openings.

Between runs there are 6 gear slots — thimble, stamp, badge, wrapper, bread tag, dice. They are tuned to make you slightly better off, not to become a wall you cannot pass without them.

What's included

  • 3 chapters plus an endless fixed-seed challenge
  • 28 enemy types, from dust and crumbs up to scissors and a paper shredder
  • 14 weapons (every one has an evolution), 8 supplies, 6 synergies
  • 16 achievements
  • A Steam leaderboard for the endless challenge
  • 14 interface languages
  • Controller support — runs and menus alike; anything the mouse can do, the pad can do
  • Steam Cloud saves
  • No ads. No in-app purchases. No connection required.

store_data.about_the_game:
It was supposed to be funny.

THE PRANK — Four friends. Three nights. One forest the internet calls cursed. On the second night, while Sam slept, the other three packed up the camp in silence and vanished into the trees — wearing the cheap souvenir masks they'd bought at the last gas station. The plan: scare him, film it, go viral.

THE MASKS — Sam wakes up thirsty at 3 A.M. to a dead fire, an empty clearing, and a walkie-talkie that answers with two soft clicks and no voice. Somewhere between the trunks, pale masked figures are starting their game. He knows it's a prank. He's almost sure it's a prank. But everyone buys the same mask at that gas station — and not everyone wearing one tonight is a friend.

YOU DECIDE WHO SURVIVES — The Fifth Mask is a fully filmed, first-person interactive horror. Read every situation: call out or stay silent, run or hide, press the talk button or let the static breathe. Your choices shape who trusts you, who stands beside you at dawn — and who never leaves the forest. Failure doesn't mean game over. It means the night gets worse.

FEATURES

  • A complete cinematic horror story (~2.5 hours) told entirely in first-person filmed sequences

  • Choices that carry: bonds, betrayals and small decisions echo all the way to the finale

  • Silence is always an option — and sometimes it's the cruelest one

  • Tension-first interaction: pressure decisions, held-breath moments, in-scene observation. No button-mashing filler.

  • One ending scene, shaped by everything you did: who lives, who forgives, who wears the mask at dawn

  • No supernatural excuses. Everything in Hollow Pines is human. That's the frightening part.

The demo contains the complete Prologue. Your choices and saves carry into the full game.

store_data.about_the_game:
Running a pizza shop seemed easier from the outside

The sauce is burning. There’s a pizza in the oven. Someone is waiting at the counter, the phone is ringing, and your friend has disappeared with the scooter.

Welcome to Ciao Pizza.

Run a pizza shop alone or with up to three friends, where every order starts as a ball of dough and ends — hopefully — in the hands of the right customer.

Make every pizza yourself

Press the dough. Ladle the sauce. Grate the cheese. Add every topping by hand, then slide the pizza into the oven.

Pepperoni, mushrooms, olives, pineapple, if it’s on the ticket, somebody has to put it there.

Every order goes through your hands from start to finish.

Just don’t forget what you left in the oven.

Something always needs your attention

Customers are lining up. The sauce is still on the burner. The soda fountain is almost empty. A phone order just came in. And somewhere behind you, a pizza is becoming charcoal. You only have two hands.

Good luck.

Bring friends. Blame them later.

Play alone or with up to three friends in drop-in co-op.

Split the work. One cooks, one handles customers, two takes deliveries.

Or all four of you can crowd around the same pizza while everything else falls apart.

That works too.

Take the pizza across town

Some customers won’t come to you.

Grab the scooter and deliver their order yourself, weaving across the city while the pizza gets colder with every wrong turn. Or send the delivery robot down the road while you stay behind and deal with the next disaster.

Take too long and the food gets cold.

Keep the customers happy

Customers queue to order, pay, and collect their food.

Keep them waiting too long and their patience starts to disappear. Forget their drink, or hand over something cold and your reputation takes the hit.

You can also pick them up and carry them outside.

This is rarely good for business.

Try not to run out of everything

Ingredients empty. Drinks run dry. Supplies disappear faster than you expect.

Keep the shop stocked, keep the orders moving, and unlock more of the menu as your business grows.

More menu means more options.

It also means more things to forget.

Keep the shop alive

Good orders build your popularity.

Cold food, missing items, failed deliveries, and angry customers create complaints and damage your reputation.

And sooner or later, rent is due.

Apparently chaos is not an accepted form of payment.

If you can pick it up, you can probably throw it

Ingredients. Boxes. Tools. Trays. Crates.

Carry them. Stack them. Drop them. Throw them across the kitchen.

Throw a pineapple at whoever is complaining.

Throw the supplies by accident.

Carry a customer out the door.

Running a restaurant is about making decisions.

store_data.about_the_game:
Classic Element TD Meets Roguelite

Build a new tower arsenal from elements, runes, and divine gifts in every run. Your towers are more than weapons: they are the walls of your maze – you decide the path your enemies must take. Journey TD combines the depth of classic element tower defense games with modern roguelite progression: every run is different – but your progress endures.

Draft Your Arsenal

Over the course of each run, you draft elements and unlock their towers. Each element follows a clear identity – from raw direct damage to poison and burn effects, crowd control, and support. It's the combination that makes the build: towers empower one another through element combos, and if you play damage types and armor types wisely, you'll break even the toughest waves. Five elements are open to you from your very first run – the sixth must be earned.

Prove Yourself in the DPS Arena

After every Lord, a DPS check awaits: the run pauses, your towers enter the arena as one and unleash everything they have in two 20-second fights — first against a single target, then against an entire group. The higher your damage, the better the reward: from Bronze to Diamond, with increasingly rare items to choose from. An honest test of whether your build truly holds up.

Under the Eyes of the Gods

Six gods shape the world of Journey TD. Their unique god towers, gifts, and trials give every run its own direction – build around their powers.

Progress That Endures

Between runs, your power grows permanently: collect materials across 6 quality tiers, hunt 27 extremely rare Power Runes across 5 ranks, and work your way through the Transcendence Tree with its 98 nodes. And if you want to go even further, ascend to the Astral Tree – a starry sky of long-term progression with endless Paragon levels.

Your Builder Gets His Hands Dirty

No anonymous build cursor: your Builder walks the map in plain sight, finds his own way across the terrain, and raises every tower hammer in hand. And between runs, you make him YOUR Builder – with equipment, titles, and over 25 unlockable skins.

Features

  • 168 towers across 6 elements – each with its own identity – plus 6 unique god towers

  • Draft system: a new arsenal every run

  • Element combos, damage types, and an armor system for true buildcrafting

  • 27 Power Runes, a skill tree, the Transcendence Tree with 98 nodes, and the Astral Tree with endless Paragon levels

  • Procedurally generated maps with mazing: your towers shape the enemies' path

  • 3 game modes (150 waves, 300 waves, Endless) × 6 difficulty levels

  • 341 achievements, 133 titles, and over 25 unlockable skins

  • Race the ghost of your best run – with a live wave-by-wave comparison

  • Fully playable offline, single-player

store_data.about_the_game:
YOUR DECK IS YOUR DEFENSE

A midnight mob is marching on the Grand Flicker Theatre. Build a deck of cartoon contraptions, spend Ink to play your hand, and drag tower cards onto the street. The card does not merely trigger an effect. It jumps off the table and takes its place on the battlefield.

CARDS BECOME TOWERS

Every tower starts in your deck. Draw it, pay its Ink cost, choose a position, and bring it to life.

  • Popgun Pup peppers single targets with rapid cork fire.

  • Boiler Bell lobs hot ink bombs into packed crowds.

  • Buzzer Beacon shocks every enemy caught inside its reach.

Your deck cycles from draw pile to hand to discard, then shuffles back together. Ink arrives when a wave is cleared, not while enemies are moving. Every breather becomes a tactical choice. Build now, save for a stronger card, or hold a support for the moment your defense starts to crack.

TURN A HAND INTO A KILLING MACHINE

Tower cards establish the board. Support cards transform it for the rest of the fight. Throw a Spotlight on a cramped position for extra range, give a tower Top Billing for a burst of damage, or start a Chorus Line that arcs attacks into more enemies.

Placement matters. Range matters. Timing matters. A cheap answer now can leave the perfect card stranded in your hand when the next wave arrives.

CHOOSE THE NEXT REEL

Plot a route across eight floors toward Big Boss Baffo. Combat nodes grow your deck. Elite fights offer extra rewards and sigils. Workshops permanently stamp new powers onto cards. Ticker Crow sells tempting contraptions, deck surgery, and the repairs that may keep your theatre standing.

Your theatre's health carries through the run. Damage is not erased when the fight ends, so the safest route is not always the route you can afford.

STAMP THE CARD. CHANGE THE RUN.

At the Workshop, press permanent sigils into the cards you plan to build around. Add a second shot with Twin Barrel. Slow the street with Sticky Ink. Trade speed for raw force with Heavy Frame. Cut an Ink cost with Budget Build.

Each card can hold up to two sigils. The right pair can turn a familiar tower into the centerpiece of a completely different defense.

MAKE EVERY COIN HURT

Ticker Crow always has an answer. The problem is the price. Buy a new card, reroll the stock, remove dead weight from the deck, invest in a sigil, or repair the Grand Flicker Theatre before the next fight. You will rarely have enough coin for everything.

SURVIVE THE MIDNIGHT REEL

Flicker Alley sends swarms of Ink Imps, armored brutes, splitting slimes, umbrella wielding hustlers, and screen filling bosses down a winding filmstrip road. Learn what each enemy does, build the right answer, and call each wave when you are ready.

  • Roguelike deckbuilding fused directly with tower defense placement

  • Branching routes with combat, elite fights, merchants, and workshops

  • Permanent card sigils and temporary in-fight support combinations

  • Persistent theatre health that makes every leak matter

  • Player controlled wave starts, pause, auto play, and double speed controls

  • Original 1930s inspired cartoon art with film grain, scratches, line boil, and procedural audio

  • A compact indie run built around readable decisions, fast experimentation, and one more try

Build the deck. Raise the towers. Keep the final reel running.

Your deck cycles from draw pile to hand to discard, then shuffles back together. Ink arrives when a wave is cleared, not while enemies are moving. Every breather becomes a tactical choice. Build now, save for a stronger card, or hold a support for the moment your defense starts to crack.

TURN A HAND INTO A KILLING MACHINE

Tower cards establish the board. Support cards transform it for the rest of the fight. Throw a Spotlight on a cramped position for extra range, give a tower Top Billing for a burst of damage, or start a Chorus Line that arcs attacks into more enemies.

Placement matters. Range matters. Timing matters. A cheap answer now can leave the perfect card stranded in your hand when the next wave arrives.

CHOOSE THE NEXT REEL

Plot a route across eight floors toward Big Boss Baffo. Combat nodes grow your deck. Elite fights offer extra rewards and sigils. Workshops permanently stamp new powers onto cards. Ticker Crow sells tempting contraptions, deck surgery, and the repairs that may keep your theatre standing.

Your theatre's health carries through the run. Damage is not erased when the fight ends, so the safest route is not always the route you can afford.

STAMP THE CARD. CHANGE THE RUN.

At the Workshop, press permanent sigils into the cards you plan to build around. Add a second shot with Twin Barrel. Slow the street with Sticky Ink. Trade speed for raw force with Heavy Frame. Cut an Ink cost with Budget Build.

Each card can hold up to two sigils. The right pair can turn a familiar tower into the centerpiece of a completely different defense.

MAKE EVERY COIN HURT

Ticker Crow always has an answer. The problem is the price. Buy a new card, reroll the stock, remove dead weight from the deck, invest in a sigil, or repair the Grand Flicker Theatre before the next fight. You will rarely have enough coin for everything.

SURVIVE THE MIDNIGHT REEL

Flicker Alley sends swarms of Ink Imps, armored brutes, splitting slimes, umbrella wielding hustlers, and screen filling bosses down a winding filmstrip road. Learn what each enemy does, build the right answer, and call each wave when you are ready.

  • Roguelike deckbuilding fused directly with tower defense placement

  • Branching routes with combat, elite fights, merchants, and workshops

  • Permanent card sigils and temporary in-fight support combinations

  • Persistent theatre health that makes every leak matter

  • Player controlled wave starts, pause, auto play, and double speed controls

  • Original 1930s inspired cartoon art with film grain, scratches, line boil, and procedural audio

  • A compact indie run built around readable decisions, fast experimentation, and one more try

Build the deck. Raise the towers. Keep the final reel running.

Take Command in a Blockaded Strait

You are Archer Rusk, master of the product tanker Meridian, held at anchor in the Strait of Hormuz with twenty-six lives under your authority and flammable cargo beneath your feet. War closes the route while supplies thin and the office repeats one order: hold. Protect your crew, judge corporate orders, and decide what command means when insurance calculations conflict with the lives aboard.

War Risk is an adult romance visual novel built around three single-choice romance routes and multiple endings. Choose Vesna, Yvette, or Phaedra, and face the consequences of your decisions aboard the ship. Each romance route includes explicit adult scenes.

Meet the Cast


Yvette Sorel — The Survey
A war-risk surveyor and Archer's unresolved love from fifteen years ago, Yvette boards with the power to declare the Meridian seaworthy or a write-off. Her route forces Archer to confront the past and decide whether he will choose an accurate appraisal over a safer corporate lie.


Phaedra Lekas — The Survivor
Pulled from the sea after a nearby strike, Phaedra comes aboard carrying survivor's guilt and the duty of getting her dead master home. She and Archer share grief for the same man while trying to endure the blockade and determine what comes next.


Vesna Kral — The Mate
Archer's blunt, capable chief officer challenges his obedience to the office and his judgment as master. Her route follows a forbidden attraction within the chain of command as pressure builds across the ship.

Key Features

  • Three single-choice romance routes: Forbidden Attraction, Second Chance, and Widow's Confidant.
  • A sealed maritime setting aboard a working product tanker in a war zone.
  • Decisions that balance corporate orders, crew welfare, and command responsibility.
  • Multiple endings shaped by the route and choices you pursue.
  • Explicit adult scenes in each romance route.

store_data.about_the_game:
PUCKVPUCK is a fast 2D arcade sports game for up to 8 players, local or online. You play as a puck: you boost across the arena, you slam into people, and you charge up shots. Three game types — SOCCER, DODGEBALL and SHOOTER — with more on the way.

SOCCER

Boost across the arena, slam into whoever is in your way, and hold to charge a shot that actually hurts. Eight arenas that change the game rather than just the scenery: a donut with a hole through the middle, a pinball table full of bumpers, a wormhole pitch, and an S-shaped one where the goal is not where you expect it.

DODGEBALL

No goals here. Knock the other team out with thrown balls, and remember that every throw explodes three seconds after it leaves your hand. Catch a throw cleanly and the ball powers up: green, then yellow, then BLACK. Each tier flies faster and hits harder, and BLACK cannot be caught or blocked at all. Five arenas, including rotating stages and portals that swallow balls and players alike.

SHOOTER

Weapons instead of a ball. Twelve guns sit on pads that keep moving around the arena, the pistol is the floor you always have, and recoil is movement: a shotgun blast is a dash backwards, a railgun shot a kick. Every kill in one life climbs your streak — three earns an AIRSTRIKE, five a MISSILE you steer yourself, seven a GUNSHIP that makes half the arena illegal for ten seconds — and six more rewards are waiting to be unlocked. Four arenas, plus three ways to twist it: KING (hold the crown, score the seconds), INFECTION (one stab and you turn) and SOCCER WITH GUNS (the ball only moves when it is shot).

SOLO, ON THE COUCH, OR ONLINE

All three play the same either way. Play solo against bots at a difficulty you choose, fill a couch with up to 8 players on controllers, or send your friends a code and play online. Bots also take any empty seat in a team game, so a match never waits for the last person to show up.

ORIGINAL SOUNDTRACK

Ten original tracks, written and played by us — funk, surf and synthwave, no stock library. Every menu and every match runs on our own record.

EASY TO PLAY, HARD TO MASTER

Moving takes a minute to learn. Reading a charged shot, timing a slam into a moving puck, catching a black ball on purpose, and knowing when to cash a kill streak — those take a while. A six-step tutorial covers the basics in about two minutes, and it runs the first time you launch the game.

MORE TO COME

More modes, more arenas, and more skins are on the way.

store_data.about_the_game:
A single-player tank combat action game featuring military vehicles of World War II.
Fight enemy forces across a variety of battlefields rendered with retro-style visuals, making use of your tank's performance and the surrounding terrain.

Armor and Penetration

This game does not use a hit point system. A single penetrating shot can destroy a tank.
Armor thickness varies by vehicle and by armor section.
Penetration is affected by impact angle and distance, so targeting weak points and using your own armor effectively are key to survival.

Battlefields

The game currently includes suburban, urban, forest, mountain, and open plain maps.
Additional battlefields are planned for future updates.

Missions

Missions include close-range combat in cover-rich environments, long-range interception battles, encounters in dense fog, and escort operations.
Additional missions are planned for future updates.

Included Vehicles

BT-7, T-34/76, T-34/85, KV-1, KV-2, IS-2
Panzer III, StuG III, Panzer IV, Panther G, Jagdpanther, Tiger I, Tiger II, Hetzer, Sd.Kfz.251/22 Pakwagen, Sd.Kfz.251 Half-track
Additional vehicles are planned for future updates.

Game Systems

  • Earn points by completing missions, then purchase tanks to expand your vehicle roster.

  • In most missions, you can change both friendly and enemy vehicles before deployment.
    Combine vehicles to create a variety of battle situations and playstyles.

  • Vehicle performance can be upgraded for each mission.
    Increase movement speed for close-range combat, improve reload speed for interception battles, and adjust other performance parameters to customize the difficulty to your preferred playstyle.

store_data.about_the_game:
The wilderness was supposed to be a place to disappear.

Instead, it became a place where daylight can kill you.

Forgotten Grounds is a top-down pixel-art survival game about enduring an isolated wilderness while living with a lethal sun allergy. Clear daylight is not safety - it is a threat that can drain your strength, push your body toward lasting damage, and turn a simple journey into a desperate search for shelter.

Plan your days around shadows, abandoned buildings, changing weather, limited supplies, and the dangers waiting outside after dark.

► Reverse the Usual Survival Routine: Daytime is dangerous. Night, bad weather, shadows, and indoor shelter become strategic resources rather than simple atmosphere.

► Explore a Living Wilderness: Search forests, roads, abandoned buildings, and hidden locations for resources. Different regions offer their own risks, rewards, weather conditions, and reasons to keep moving.

► Survive With What You Find: Scavenge resources, craft essential tools, light fires, find food, collect water, and manage hunger, thirst, fatigue, stamina, sanity, and carrying capacity.

Repair damaged equipment, harvest items for useful materials, and decide whether a valuable tool is worth wearing down further.

► Face Wildlife and Isolation: The sun is not your only problem. Predators, limited resources, exhaustion, illness, and the long-term pressure of isolation can all threaten a run.

► Weather Changes the Rules: Weather affects visibility, sound, exploration, and sunlight exposure. Rain can offer relief from the sun, while fog and wind can make the world feel less predictable and more dangerous.

► Death is Permanent: Every decision carries weight when there is no second chance. If you die, your journey ends - and the save is gone with it.

Cook up as many takoyaki as you can, fill orders, and aim for a high score!

Make takoyaki using a takoyaki maker!

Make as many as you can before time runs out!

Compete with up to 4 players to see who's the ultimate takoyaki chef!

You can also challenge CPU opponents!

[Rankings]

Compete for high scores against players from around the world!

Become a takoyaki master!

Note: Controllers are required for local multiplayer.

store_data.about_the_game:
DeskBloom is a desktop plant-growing game that lives on your real computer desktop. After installation, your plants stay on the desktop without blocking normal work windows, and you can drag them between multiple monitors.

Your typing, studying, programming, and work rhythm help your plants grow over time. Plants can grow leaves, bloom, drop seeds, and continue growing slowly while you are offline. You can water them, talk to them, decorate your desktop garden, and collect plants of different rarities.

Each plant has its own personality, mood, memory, and growth state. Through seeds, hybrid breeding, the codex, and storage systems, you can gradually build your own desktop garden.

Key features:

- Real-time desktop plant care that stays out of your way

- Drag plants between multiple monitors

- Typing and work rhythm help plants grow

- Offline growth

- Watering, chatting, mood, hydration, and growth systems

- Seeds, hybrid breeding, storage, and codex collection

- Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary, and Mythic rarities

- Desktop decorations such as pebbles, desk lamps, and garden signs

Facing your past, it is now your job to uncover a beastly serial killer - before it is too late.

The Deadly Winter

Ten years ago, there was a murder where the victim had their hands removed, their blood drained, and only a single, chilling clue - a deadly smile. 

People tried to cover it up and move on. Now however, bodies are turning up in the exact same pattern.

Investigate 

Examine 3D crime scenes for clues at each murder scene, collecting evidence to figure out the killer.

Question

Interrogate a cast of eccentric characters, each with their own secrets and mysteries. Wait...what is that beaver doing??

Determine

Using all your clues and wits - and a little help from Laura - put the suspect to the test in highly stylized minigames that answer two questions: who is the killer of the case, and are they the beast behind it all?

store_data.about_the_game:
Rich PaPa

You literally shoot money.

Rich PaPa is a third-person action shooter where every shot costs you cash because money itself is your ammunition.

Blast through hordes of zombies, bounce shots off the environment with ricochets, and decide how much money you are willing to fire away to survive.

Your money is both your weapon and your lifeline. Spend too much in combat and you may survive the battle only to find yourself heading toward bankruptcy.

SPEND MONEY TO FIGHT

Every shot has a price.

Pulling the trigger means firing your own money, forcing you to constantly balance firepower against the cash you have left.

MASTER RICOCHET SHOTS

Use walls and the environment to bounce your shots into enemies.

A well-placed ricochet can turn a difficult encounter into an efficient kill and help you save precious money.

SPIN THE ROULETTE

Take a chance on roulette-based upgrades that can change the course of each stage.

Powerful effects can give you an edge, but every decision is part of the risk and reward of pushing forward.

SURVIVE THE ZOMBIE HORDES

Fight your way through stage-based battles filled with zombies and escalating threats.

Manage your attacks, upgrades, and remaining cash as you try to make it to the end without going broke.

HOW MUCH ARE YOU WILLING TO SPEND TO SURVIVE?

In Rich PaPa, survival is not free.

store_data.about_the_game:
YOU CAN'T SEE. YOU CAN HEAR.

That's the whole problem.

HEARKEN drops 2–4 players into a dead, pitch-black facility with one job: haul out the reagent before the shift ends. There's no flashlight. There never was one. The only thing that shows you the room is the noise you just made — and something down here is listening for it too.

Sound is the only light you get

Every footstep, whisper, and dropped crate sends out a pulse that briefly outlines the world around you — walls, doorways, your teammate three rooms over. Whisper and you'll barely see anything. Shout and the whole floor lights up like a flare... for everyone, including whatever's hunting. Consider it a doorbell.

It doesn't have eyes. It doesn't need them.

The thing down here listens, and it's very good at it. Quiet, and it loses you. Loud, and it comes — patrolling, then investigating, then closing in for real. No scripted jump-scares: the noise decides where it goes. That includes you, on comms, forgetting to whisper.

The job

Carry reagent ampoules from the storage racks to the pneumatic tube by the airlock. Run and the glass in your arms rattles — push it, and it shatters, loud enough to bring company. Hit the day's quota and the airlock opens. Miss it and the building doesn't care what you were in the middle of. Or how close you were.

Each day raises the quota. Each day the building rebuilds itself around you, so nobody gets to memorize the floor plan.

Your mic is a weapon and a liability

Proximity voice chat isn't a chat feature here — it's a light source. Talk, and you light up. Scream, and you light up the whole team. The loudest person in the room is always the one in the most danger, which in practice means whoever is currently panicking.

KEY FEATURES

  • Total darkness — no flashlight, no HUD radar. You see only what your own noise reveals.

  • A monster that hunts entirely by sound — it goes wherever the noise sends it.

  • Proximity voice chat that doubles as your light source and your biggest liability.

  • A procedurally rebuilt facility — every day is a new floor plan, and the quota only goes up.

  • Co-op revives, not permadeath — going down just means someone has to come get you, loudly.

  • 2–4 players, best experienced with people you're willing to blame later.

store_data.about_the_game:
TRANSFORM. MAKE NOISE. FOOL YOUR FRIENDS.

MOO A-DOODLE-DOO is a chaotic multiplayer hide-and-seek game where you transform into animals, objects, and ridiculous things — then use your voice to fool your friends.

Think you can hide in plain sight?

Prove it.

BECOME ANYTHING. HIDE ANYWHERE.

Turn yourself into a cow, chicken, zombie, car, singer, beatboxer, portable toilet, or whatever else you can find.

Blend into the environment.

Stay unnoticed.

And whatever you do...

Don't get caught.

FOOL THEM WITH YOUR VOICE

Your voice isn't just for chatting.

When you transform, your voice is modulated to match your new form.

A chicken should sound like a chicken.

A cow should sound like a cow.

Use your voice to imitate what you've become, distract the Seeker, and make your friends question everything they hear.

Make the right sound.

Stay perfectly still.

Act natural.

THREE ROLES. ONE CHAOTIC GAME.

SEEKER

Find the players hiding around the map.

Listen carefully.

Watch suspicious objects.

And catch anyone who doesn't belong.

HIDER

Transform into something around you and disappear into the environment.

Blend in.

Stay quiet.

Don't get caught.

TRICKSTER

Turn the game upside down.

Cause chaos, distract the Seeker, and create opportunities for the Hiders to escape.

Sometimes the best strategy isn't hiding...

It's making everyone else panic.

EVERY ROUND CREATES A STORY

Your friend hides as a chicken.

You walk right past them.

Then suddenly...

"MOO!"

Wait.

Was that a cow?

Why is that chair moving?

Who just made that noise?

And why is there a suspicious toilet running away?

MADE FOR PLAYING WITH FRIENDS

Grab your friends, jump into a match, and see who can outsmart everyone else.

MOO A-DOODLE-DOO is perfect for players who enjoy:

[]

Multiplayer party games

[/][]

Hide-and-seek and prop hunting

[/][]

Funny and unpredictable gameplay

[/][]

Deception and mind games

[/][]

Making ridiculous memories with friends

[/][]

Games where anything can happen

[/]

The more friends you play with, the more chaotic it gets.

Video & Streaming

Gameplay videos and broadcasts are welcome!

Please just follow these two guidelines:

[]

Include the title of this game in your video/stream title. (Required)

[/][]

Include the Steam store page URL in your video description or stream overview.

[/]

store_data.about_the_game:
Juicicora is a cozy co-op adventure set in a bright hand-painted world of wheat meadows, chalk cliffs, blossom trees and floating islands. Wander it alone, or share it with up to four friends.

Hop, hover and swim your way across the world, then start stringing the good stuff together. Hold charge to build speed, dash across a chasm, kick off a wall mid-climb, or come down in a charged ground slam hard enough to crack the floor. Homing-attack your way from target to target and you need never touch the ground at all.

Fruit is power here. Find it, carry it, and eat it to run faster, fire projectiles, or stranger things. Take what you have gathered to the alchemy table and mix new fruit from old, then equip a loadout and swap between them on the fly.

[h2]A world with others[/h2]

The villagers remember you. Talk to them, help them out, and their opinion of you shifts in real time -- and the ones who like you open up work, minigames and secrets the rest will not.

[h2]Dive into the Rift[/h2]

A beam of light cuts the sky above the meadow. Follow it through the portal into the Dimensional Rift, a temple of floating islands stacked above the clouds, and find out what has been sleeping at the top of it.

[h2]Dress up[/h2]

Acorn caps, wheat crowns, carved wooden masks. Your Soul is a blank canvas and everyone else can see what you did to it.

[h2]Bring friends[/h2]

Up to five Souls per world. Open your world to the public and let strangers wander in, or keep

it to the people you invited. Everything above works in co-op.

[h2]Streaming, videos and clips[/h2]

Record it, stream it, clip it, post it wherever you like -- including monetised channels. All

we ask is that Juicicora is named somewhere: the video title, the description, the stream

title, or on screen. You do not need to ask us first and you do not owe us anything.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Sun has been dead for three hundred years.

No one remembers daylight.

No one remembers warmth.

Only survival.

You awaken beneath a mountain of corpses.

You have no name.

No memories.

No idea why you're still alive.

As you struggle free from the dead, something begins to speak.

Not a voice from the darkness...

but the heart beating inside a pile of corpses.

A world trying to survive itself

You remember nothing.

Every step reveals another piece of a civilization that refused to die.

On the surface, humanity no longer fights for victory.

It fights over what it means to remain human.

Three factions struggle to shape mankind's future.

None of them are completely wrong.

None of them are innocent.

Three paths. Three futures…One species. 

Join one of them. Or walk alone.

The world has fractured into three powers, each convinced it alone can save humanity.

One believes humanity must remain human, no matter the cost.

One believes death is the only path to immortality.

One believes flesh has already reached its limit.

Humanity

The last true humans cling desperately to survival.

They breed, enslave and sacrifice individual freedom in hopes that sheer numbers and evolution will someday produce people capable of surviving this world.

Cruel...

but perhaps necessary.

The Umbral Lifebringers

Necromancers believe death is only another stage of life.

They preserve humans as intelligent undead capable of surviving for centuries, waiting for the day magic can restore them completely.

To them, the living are not enemies.

They are humanity's future.

Ironborn Consortium

Syntharites believe flesh has reached its limits.

Some seek to improve humanity through technology, replacing damaged bodies with mechanical ones.

Others believe humanity must go further — abandoning flesh entirely and embracing the machine itself.

Key Features

• Dark fantasy meets post-apocalyptic modern civilization.

• Turn-based JRPG with exploration, choice and faction politics.

• Explore a vast open world with no quest markers or quest log.

  Around 150 locations await exploration.

• Three radically different factions with competing visions for humanity.

 •Choices have consequences. The fate of people, settlements and entire communities can change long after you leave    them behind.

• Morally gray decisions with no obvious "good" ending.

store_data.about_the_game:
Long Description — About This Game

Brew Potions. Serve Customers. Survive the Consequences.

Your brother has vanished. All he left behind is a run-down alchemy shop, a suspiciously well-patched cauldron, and a city where even a soothing chamomile potion can have political consequences.

Brew & Boom is a narrative alchemy simulation about dangerous potions, difficult choices, and explosions that are, of course, performed strictly in the name of science.

Run Your Own Alchemy Shop

Order ingredients, manage your supplies, and combine potion bases with a variety of reagents. Every ingredient changes the properties of your brew—and some mostly change the likelihood of your cauldron suddenly redistributing itself across the room.

Upgrade your cauldron, expand your storage shelves, and gradually restore your crumbling workshop.

Every Potion Has Consequences

Brewing takes more than the correct recipe. Unstable mixtures can fail, destroy valuable ingredients, or end with a spectacular explosion.

Successful potions may help your customers—usually. What you sell and how you fulfil their requests will influence future encounters, the mood of the city, and the course of the story.

Cause too many explosions and the city guard may pay you a visit. For “noise complaints.” Not for the missing roof.

Customers, Conspiracies, and Questionable Ingredients

Citizens, soldiers, merchants, rebels, and figures who prefer to travel after dark will approach your workshop window.

The Paladins demand that a mysterious ingredient be added to certain potions. The Storm Banners have plans of their own. And the Silent Conclave leaves messages at night that might have been better left unread.

You decide whom to help, whom to deceive, and which potions to deliver. Your choices affect hidden faction relationships and lead the story down different paths.

Business by Day, Secrets by Night

During the day, open your window to customers, accept requests, and sell finished potions. At night, prepare supplies, organise ingredients, and deal with visitors who would rather leave no trace.

Some answers can only be found in daylight. Others do not come knocking until the streetlamps reveal little more than a shadow.

Key Features

  • Experimental brewing with potion bases, reagents, and different effects

  • A risky cauldron system featuring successes, failures, and spectacular explosions

  • A reactive story with customers, dialogue choices, and lasting consequences

  • Three competing factions with conflicting goals

  • Day and night phases featuring different encounters and activities

  • Upgradeable cauldrons, shelves, and workshop equipment

  • Multiple story paths and endings

  • Dark political intrigue, black comedy, and a surprising amount of bureaucracy surrounding exploding potions

Save the city, sell it out, or accidentally cover it in smoke. The cauldron does not judge you. The city guard does.

store_data.about_the_game:
Draw a line and connect the matching numbers.
Sounds simple — but keeping the lines from crossing while filling every single cell is another story.
LINK IT is a number-connecting puzzle game with a warm, hand-drawn paper aesthetic. Start on a cozy 5×5 grid and work your way up to sprawling boards. The rules take seconds to grasp, yet the challenge pulls you in deeper and deeper. Slow down and savor, puzzle after puzzle, the satisfaction of filling every board to perfection.

How to Play

  • Connect each pair of matching numbers with a line

  • Lines can't cross or overlap

  • Fill every cell on the board to clear the level

Features

  • 500 levels: carefully crafted with a smooth difficulty curve — the final stages push you to your limit

  • Daily Challenge: a fresh puzzle every day, the same one for players around the world

  • Endless Mode: generated on the fly and never repeating — play as long as you like

  • Relax Mode: no time limit, just the quiet joy of solving

  • Bronze / Silver / Gold medals: aim for faster, more perfect clears

  • 60 achievements to unlock

  • Warm paper-style art and a soothing feel — perfect for your commute, lunch break, or before bed

  • 12 interface languages supported

Ready? Pick up a line and start connecting.

store_data.about_the_game:
YOUR JOB IS TERRIBLE. YOUR BOSS IS WORSE. DO SOMETHING ABOUT IT.

You've had this job. Maybe you have it right now. The printer jams twice a day, the phone never stops, someone keeps sending you spreadsheets that don't reconcile, and at four o'clock a man in a slightly-too-expensive shirt appears at your desk to ask how it's all going.

Office Stress is about the part you don't get to do in real life.

MAKE IT PERSONAL

Before you start, you build two people: yourself, and him.

Name him. Pick his face. Give him the haircut. Every insult he shouts across the office has his name on it, every warning letter is signed by him, and when he finally goes down, the game says so by name. It is astonishing how much better this makes everything.

DO THE WORK. FEEL THE STRESS.

Answer the phone. Unjam the printer. Send the email. Shred the evidence. Water the plant that nobody else waters. Every chore is a little minigame on a deadline, and they don't queue up politely — they land on top of each other until you're sprinting across the office with a box of A4 wondering how your life got here.

Miss one and you get a written warning. Get enough warnings and you're fired, which is the one ending where you don't get to punch anybody.

THEN THE DOOR OPENS

Fill the stress meter and he comes out from behind his desk to tell you what he thinks.

That's when the day stops being a job and starts being a boxing match. He blocks. He telegraphs. He talks the entire time. Knock him down and the day is cleared, the paperwork is forgotten, and you go home genuinely feeling better.

AFTER HOURS

When he's gone, the office is yours. Race the chairs down the corridor. Play paper-ball basketball across the desks. And do other crazy things with your co-workers!

THREE WEEKS. TWENTY-TWO LEVELS. ONE MANAGER.

  • 12 working days of escalating chaos — by week three he patrols the floor while you work, and the only way to buy back time is to slap him on his way past

  • 10 after-hours events — chair racing, paper basketball, hide and seek, egg toss

  • Build yourself and your boss — names, faces, the lot

  • Chase the clean sheet — letter grades on every working day, gold stars on every evening, and a completion score that knows exactly how far off perfect you are

  • Six languages — English, Bulgarian, German, Spanish, French and Italian

No managers were harmed in the making of this game. Several were named, modelled, and repeatedly knocked over

That's when the day stops being a job and starts being a boxing match. He blocks. He telegraphs. He talks the entire time. Knock him down and the day is cleared, the paperwork is forgotten, and you go home genuinely feeling better.

When he's gone, the office is yours. Race the chairs down the corridor. Play paper-ball basketball across the desks. And do other crazy things with your co-workers!

THREE WEEKS. TWENTY-TWO LEVELS. ONE MANAGER.

  • 12 working days of escalating chaos — by week three he patrols the floor while you work, and the only way to buy back time is to slap him on his way past

store_data.about_the_game:
You only know what you see

Soldier Cats is a round-based 3v3 tactical shooter played by the street cats of Istanbul. Fog of war is not decoration here: your cat sees a cone, and everything outside it is simply absent. The server decides what reaches your screen, so no one reads the map through a wall.

Ten rounds, one street

Each round starts with a three-second countdown and locked controls. Then the middle zone opens, and the team that holds it takes the round. Everyone respawns at full health with cooldowns reset. First to ten rounds takes the match.

Six cats, six roles

  • Cingöz - Assault. The baseline. Useful everywhere, exceptional nowhere.

  • Havuç - Heavy. 140 HP and slow. Iron Hide lets him hold the middle alone.

  • Van Kedisi - Marksman. Owns long sightlines. 85 HP if she gets caught.

  • Nazar - Recon. Marks enemies and turns information into a weapon.

  • Pamuk - Support. Never wins alone; rounds are lost without her.

  • Duman - Assassin. Fastest, most fragile. Shadow Step gets behind you.

Three districts, three kinds of tension

  • Kadıköy — balanced ground. Open square, wet cobblestones, tram line.

  • Kapalıçarşı — a labyrinth. Arched corridors where the enemy is always one corner away.

  • Moda Sahili — open seafront. Long lines that reward marksmen and punish sprinting.

Hunt the mice

Bring a friend and defend against waves of mice in co-op. The swarm obeys the same vision rules you do: what your cone doesn't cover, you don't see coming.

The street remembers

  • Weekly seasons crown a Governor clan on every map; its members earn 20% more Points there.

  • Clans with roles, chat and invites. Three cats from the same clan get a gold banner in the pre-match lineup.

  • Levels unlock new cats and cosmetic slots. Nothing that affects power is for sale.

store_data.about_the_game:
In ReMasterOfGame, the rabbit has long understood that no one but him will clear mountains of trash, clean puddles, or carry a precious ingredient across the whole location.

Explore interconnected 2D locations, travel freely between them by elevator, meet NPCs, and take on their tasks.

Locations live their own lives while you are away, and even cleaned-up places get cluttered again. Find a balance and decide whether this world can be put in order. And whether it should be.

 Talk to NPCs, accept quests, and track your progress.

 Pick up, carry, throw, and deliver items to the right places.

 Solve environmental challenges through cleaning, mechanisms, object linking, and spatial puzzles.

 Use elevators and other interactive elements of the world.

 Watch the world change: completed actions persist when moving between locations.

 Open the quest journal and return to active tasks at any time.

You do not need to save the universe with one heroic jump. Sometimes it is enough to deliver the right things without dropping them, start a mechanism, and remember where you threw your mop when leaving this location last time.

store_data.about_the_game:
“Stars for a blanket, ground for a bed, a good horse and open country. It's all a cowboy needs.”

I'm a Cowboy, Baby! is a first-person co-op adventure about cowboys driving cattle across the Wild West. Together with your friends, you'll need to guide the herd across the frontier and get as many cattle as possible to the ranch alive.

The cattle will wander off, panic, get hungry and thirsty, and constantly find new ways to get themselves into trouble. Your job is to keep the herd together and deal with problems as they come. Sometimes it's a runaway cow. Sometimes it's a grizzly. And sometimes it's a tornado trying to carry half your herd away.

DRIVE THE HERD TO THE RANCH

Move the herd across the Wild West and get as many cattle as possible to the ranch alive. Keep them moving in the right direction — every lost or dead cow cuts into your team's reward.

KEEP THE HERD UNDER CONTROL

Cattle can stray, panic, stop moving, or wander away from the herd. Ride around them, control their movement, and use your lasso to bring back strays before they get lost. Sometimes the herd creates problems all by itself. Two cows might decide that the middle of a cattle drive is the perfect time to make another cow. Congratulations. You have more cattle now.

KEEP THE HERD HEALTHY

Watch the herd's hunger and thirst, and stop at grazing spots and water along the trail. Neglect their needs and the cattle become harder to control — or may not survive the journey.

PROTECT THE HERD

Bandits, wild animals, bad weather, and other incidents can turn a quiet cattle drive into chaos. Use your guns, horses, and lassos to protect the herd and keep it moving toward the ranch.

WORK TOGETHER

Split the work between 3–4 cowboys: drive the herd, recover strays, handle threats, and deal with problems along the trail. When everything goes wrong at once, keeping even part of the herd alive becomes a team effort.

KEY FEATURES

  • Online co-op with friends

  • You can drive a cart

  • Physics-based cow, horse, characters and enemies

  • Dynamic weather

  • Cowboy vibes

store_data.about_the_game:
Become a Guardian and set out to protect the world of the Manabies.

Explore mysterious floating islands, uncover ancient secrets, rescue magical creatures, and build your own flying home base. Discover rare Manabu seeds, raise your Manabies, strengthen your team, and face dangerous Wonderlings in action-packed arena battles.

At the heart of every adventure lies a unique battle system where visual mathematics becomes part of the gameplay. Mathematical operations unlock attacks, abilities, puzzles, and progression, turning every mission into an engaging challenge that grows alongside the player.

Manabies combines exploration, creature collection, base building, and real-time combat with an adaptive learning system that keeps every player challenged at the right level.

Explore a Living World

Travel between beautiful floating islands filled with hidden paths, resources, characters, and adventures. Complete missions, uncover new locations, and push back the mysterious Wonderlings threatening the skies.

Collect and Raise Magical Creatures

Find rare Manabu seeds throughout the world and watch them grow into adorable Manabies. Build your collection, care for your companions, and expand the team that travels with you on every adventure.

Build Your Flying Home

Upgrade your flying Guardian base into a home for your growing family of Manabies. Unlock new facilities, improve your equipment, and prepare for increasingly challenging expeditions.

Battle with Mathematics

Every encounter is driven by visual mathematical operations. Solve challenges to unleash abilities, overcome obstacles, and defeat enemies. As the adventure becomes more exciting, players naturally solve hundreds of mathematical challenges while focusing on the gameplay itself.

Grows with Every Player

Adaptive difficulty continuously adjusts the experience to match each player’s current understanding. The game covers key elementary mathematics concepts including number sense, arrays, multiplication, fractions, area models, and more.

Proven in Real Classrooms

Manabies is already being used by schools in multiple countries. During early classroom testing, 41% of students voluntarily continued playing at home after first trying the game at school, solving more than 700 math challenges per week on average.

Features

  • Explore a world of magical floating islands.

  • Fight fast-paced arena battles against the Wonderlings.

  • Discover, raise, and evolve adorable Manabies.

  • Build and upgrade your own flying Guardian base.

  • Unlock new missions, islands, and adventures.

  • Battle using a unique mathematics-powered combat system.

  • Adaptive difficulty that grows with each player.

  • Covers essential elementary math concepts through gameplay.

  • No advertisements.

  • Optional Premium subscription with additional content.

store_data.about_the_game:
You wake up underground. You don't know why you're alive. You don't know what happened up there. You just know something is very wrong down here, and you need to keep moving.

You find a room with a single stick sitting under a beam of light. It feels important. You pick it up.

Every alarm in the building goes off at once.

Turns out that stick is the only weapon you get, and it's all you need. Throw it and it ricochets off walls, ceilings, whatever's still standing, chaining through a room full of enemies before it even hits the ground. Add hitstop that makes every kill feel like it actually landed, plus a dash that never lets you stop moving, and combat turns into something closer to a puzzle you solve at full speed.

KRAVN is a fast, brutal boomer shooter set in the ruins of an underground war nobody survived to explain. You're heading deeper. Something else down here wants what's at the bottom too, and it isn't waiting around.

Hit fast. Move faster. Don't stop to think about what these places used to be.

  • Ricochet chain kills: turn one throw into a room-wide massacre

  • Every hit has impact: hitstop makes each kill feel brutal

  • Constant momentum: dash forward, close the distance, never slow down

  • PSX-era visuals: low-poly geometry, and a world that feels beautifully wrong

  • Decaying artificial worlds: descend through enormous abandoned environments built during the war

  • Riff-driven metal: heavy, aggressive music built around the violence

  • No hand-holding: descend deeper, fight your way through, and discover what waits at the Core

Given the gruesome nature of their deaths, criminal agencies suspect supernatural forces are at play. Equipped with an experimental device, you must enter the minds of the victims, relive the terrifying and harrowing memories of their final minutes, and uncover the hidden secret behind their deaths...

Each victim faces a distinct form of horror, with unique mechanics and escalating tension. A father searches for his missing daughter in Central Park while being stalked by a mysterious laughing man. A resident must survive as a wanted killer tries to break into their apartment. A TV salesman encounters disturbing glitches spreading across the store’s televisions during his final shift. Meanwhile, a commuter on the subway is terrorized by a sinister clown whose deadly stare turns the journey home into a nightmare.

Visuals and Atmosphere:

The game features hyper-realistic, highly atmospheric graphics infused with visual elements of the 1980s, completely immersing you in its gritty world.

store_data.about_the_game:
【Cozy Vinyl Organization Simulator】

You bought a bankrupt vinyl store.

Organize all 4281 vinyl records and CDs, put everything in its proper place, and turn the rundown shop into the Vinyl Store of your dreams.

【Bring Order to the Records】

  • Sort & Organize: From vinyl records to CDs, use album covers, artists, genres, and other clues to find the perfect place for every item and bring order back to the store.

  • Massive Collection: With 4281 vinyl records and CDs to organize, the store may seem overwhelming at first. Sort, shelve, and arrange your collection piece by piece as you work toward creating the Vinyl Store of your dreams.

【Make the Store Yours】

  • Clean Up the Mess: The store is a complete mess when you first arrive. Pick up the scattered records and CDs, sort them out, and slowly turn the place into a cozy record store.

  • Organize Your Way: Decide how you want to tackle the mess. Find the route and rhythm that work best for you as you move records around the store.

  • Compete for the Top Spot: Once you’ve found your fastest way to organize the store, see how you compare with other players. Your best time will be added to the online leaderboard.

【Helpful Skills】

As you progress, you’ll unlock skills that make sorting and organizing the store easier and faster.

  • Gather: Quickly bring other records from the same artist or collection directly to you, saving you the time of searching for them around the store.

  • Spotlight: Highlights records that belong to the same artist or collection, making them much easier to find among the scattered albums.

  • Auto-Shelve: Automatically places the records in your hands into their correct spots, letting you keep the shelves organized without having to place each one manually.

store_data.about_the_game:
The surface has fallen. As the outer world dissolved into an uninhabitable ruin, humanity’s last survivors retreated into isolated underground bunkers. Yet the greatest threat isn't lurking outside—it is the relentless Corrosion consuming the shelter from within.

Under the Rust is a tactical UI-driven PvE bunker management simulation. Take control of the C.O.R.E. terminal, command your crew, and balance life support systems before structural decay buries you alive.

C.O.R.E. TERMINAL COMMAND & SYSTEM DECAY

  • Retro-Terminal Interface: Oversee all critical facility operations through a tactical terminal interface. Diagnose system failures in real-time and execute vital directives.

  • Fight the Rust: Structural corrosion is your main enemy. As rust spreads, power grids, water lines, and oxygen scrubbers fail—requiring continuous maintenance and repair.

  • Life Support Balance: Maintain a delicate equilibrium between power distribution, water filtration, and oxygen supply. A single failure can trigger a catastrophic chain reaction.

                              

                              

                              

TACTICAL CREW RPG & SURFACE EXPEDITIONS

  • Deep Personnel Management: Assign operatives to key roles based on their stats (STR, PER, INT), skills (Engineering, Scavenging, Hacking), and unique personal traits.

  • Surface Expeditions & Radar: Scan surface sectors for anomalies and structural ruins. Dispatch recon teams into dangerous territory to recover vital raw materials and tech components.

                                     

                               

DIRECTIVES & EMERGENCY LOGS

  • Policy Management: Enforce strict directives, workload quotas, and emergency protocols to maintain bunker stability.

  • Real-time C.O.R.E. Logs: Every mechanical failure, crew conflict, or surface radio transmission is intercepted and displayed through system logs.

                              

                              

MODDING & SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE

  • Modular JSON Architecture: Events, construction costs, production, and consumption values are structured around JSON files. The game continues to be actively developed upon this modular foundation.

  • Multi-Language Support: The flexible language framework allows community translations and localization packs to be integrated seamlessly.

  • Dynamic Crises & Replayability: Procedural surface anomalies, crisis events, and crew dynamics ensure that every new run presents a unique survival scenario.

store_data.about_the_game:
[h2]The library is trying to kill you.[/h2]

You're just trying to get out. The books have other plans.

Every shelf is a trap. Get too close to the wrong tome and it dashes straight at you. Walk under another and it drops on your head. Land on a floating book over a bottomless void and it starts sinking the moment your feet touch it — stand still and you go down with it. Some patrol the walls. Some come screaming across the room from the left with no warning at all.

Touch any of them and you die.

[h2]No checkpoints. No mercy.[/h2]

Die and you start the level over from the beginning. Not from a nearby flag. Not from halfway. The beginning. Every death is a full reset, and every level is built to make you earn the exit.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[list]

[*][b]29 handcrafted levels[/b] of escalating library hostility

[*][b]Five kinds of murderous book[/b], each with its own way of ending your run

[*][b]Precision 3D platforming[/b] — tight controls, no excuses

[*][b]Death restarts the level[/b], so every jump matters

[*][b]It talks back[/b] — the game has opinions about how you died

[/list]

[h2]Built for the clip.[/h2]

This is a game designed to be watched as much as played. If you stream, your chat is going to have a great time. If you don't, no one has to know how many attempts level 19 took.

store_data.about_the_game:
Toys Co. is a cozy tidy-up game where 3,200+ toys have completely taken over the store. Pick them up, figure out where they belong, restore every shelf, and turn an overwhelming toy-filled mess into a perfectly organized store.

But cleaning up is only part of the fun, some toys are made to be played with.

SORT THE CHAOS

3,200+ Toys. One Very Messy Store.

Pick up toys scattered across the floor and return every last one to its proper place. Fill the shelves, clear the aisles, and slowly watch the chaos disappear.

SCAN. FIND. ORGANIZE

Where Does This Even Go?

Not sure where a toy belongs? Take it to the Toy Analyzer, scan it, and discover its correct location in the store. Then it’s up to you to put everything back where it belongs.

PLAY THE CLAW MACHINE

Cleaning Deserves a Break.

Step up to the Claw Machine, try your luck, and earn special abilities that help you deal with the mountain of toys waiting around the store. You might come for the reward. You might stay because you absolutely need one more try.

TOYS THAT ACTUALLY WORK

They’re Toys, Play With Them!

Not everything is meant to sit still on a shelf. Find interactive toys, place moving cars onto their tracks, and watch them race around the store. Some toys have a little more life in them than you might expect.

BUILD IT. PLAY IT.

The Piano Is Missing a Few Pieces.
Find the missing keys scattered around the store, rebuild the toy piano, and once it’s complete… play it yourself. Putting a toy back together is only half the fun.

Features

  • Organize 3,200+ scattered toys

  • Scan toys with the Toy Analyzer

  • Find the correct shelf for every toy

  • Play the Claw Machine

  • Unlock useful special abilities

  • Discover interactive toys around the store

  • Place toy cars on tracks and watch them move

  • Find missing piano keys and rebuild the piano

  • Actually play the piano

  • Fill shelves and restore the entire toy store

  • Cozy, satisfying tidy-up gameplay

  • Plenty of toys. Probably too many.

store_data.about_the_game:
Hunt. Collect. Survive.

Soul Finders is a fast-paced multiplayer party game set in a strange supernatural world. Explore the map, hunt wandering NPCs, collect the souls they leave behind, and build the highest score before the round ends.

It sounds simple... until the map starts hunting you back.

Every Soul Counts

Use your soul beam to hunt the inhabitants roaming the map. Defeated NPCs release collectible souls, but you are not the only player searching for them.

Move quickly, choose your route, and keep collecting. Every soul brings you closer to victory, while every mistake gives your rivals another opportunity to pull ahead.

The Map Fights Back

Each match is disrupted by dangerous supernatural events that force players to adapt.

UFO drones sweep across the map using search beams to locate careless players. Deadly weather can transform familiar areas into dangerous territory. Even the NPC standing directly in front of you might secretly be an invulnerable werebear waiting to strike.

The longer the round continues, the more dangerous the hunt becomes.

Death Creates Opportunity

Losing a life does more than slow you down. Defeated players leave behind valuable green souls that other players can collect.

One player’s disaster can quickly become another player’s advantage.

A Different Match Every Time

NPC movement, player decisions, hidden threats, changing weather, and unpredictable encounters ensure that no two rounds play exactly the same way.

You might dominate one round and spend the next running from a werebear while UFO drones search overhead.

Key Features

  • Competitive online multiplayer soul hunting

  • Fast, round-based matches

  • Hundreds of roaming NPCs to search through

  • Hidden werebear encounters

  • UFO drones that actively sweep the map for players

  • Dangerous weather and supernatural map events

  • Player deaths that create valuable collectible souls

  • Multiple maps with their own atmosphere and layout

  • Character customization

  • Controller support

Collect what you can. Survive what you cannot. Finish the match with more souls than everyone else.

store_data.about_the_game:
Five kingdoms are at war. You sell to all of them.

Thirty years of war have worn the map down to five exhausted kingdoms — and one village that belongs to none of them. Shadow Bridge stands exactly where all five borders meet. Everyone needs it. Nobody dares take it.

You are Hermos. You fought for all five banners, buried your family, and put down your sword. Now you keep a shop. It turns out the sword was never what decided the war.

Trade is the weapon

Every crate you sell lands somewhere. Good steel makes an army stronger. A cursed blade breaks in a soldier's hand, and nobody ever learns whose fault it was. Refuse to deal at all, and you lose the trust you spent years building.

  • Arm a kingdom — quality goods push a faction toward victory

  • Poison a kingdom — sell cursed work and watch it lose ground without ever knowing why

  • Walk away — the safest deal is the one you don't make, and it costs you all the same

Trust opens the map

Each faction keeps its own goods, its own materials, and its own secrets. Dwarven ore, elven craft, the Cult's darker work — none of it is for sale to a stranger. Reputation is the only key, and it is spent as easily as it is earned.

Make it, enchant it, ruin it

Buy raw materials, forge them into goods, and bind an enchantment to the result — but only if the faction that owns that magic trusts you enough to teach it. A blade blessed by the elves and a blade cursed by the Cult look exactly the same on the counter.

The village follows the winner

Shadow Bridge is neutral, not innocent. As one kingdom pulls ahead, its colors go up over the square, its people move in, and the losers quietly stop coming. The village you end the game in is the one your ledger built.

Six ways this ends

Five kingdoms, five futures — an elven enclave, a human province, a dwarven forge-town, an orcish protection racket, or something the Cult has been waiting thirty years for. Keep them all balanced and none of them win: Shadow Bridge stays free, and you are the one who founded it.

No combat. Only consequences.

There is no sword in your hands and no health bar on your screen. There is a shop, a ledger, five armies waiting on your next shipment, and a war that ends however you price it.

store_data.about_the_game:
Nothing has really changed, has it?

HugaHuga Simulator invites you and your friends into a chaotic, hilarious, multiplayer friendslop experience in the Stone Age. Go solo or gather your tribe to cause absolute mayhem together! Ever wondered what it’s like to build your stone crib, wave to the neighbors, feed the dinosaur at your front door, and invent the wheel from scratch?

And what’s the game plan when you and your crew pile into a heavy stone car, cruising around the block with raptors chasing your bumper?

Here is the primitive life experience waiting for you and your squad:

  • Gather Your Tribe (Multiplayer Co-Op): Team up with friends, manage your village together, or completely mess up each other's primitive setups for maximum chaos.

  • Your Own Stone Crib: Build dolmen-style houses with primeval architecture and customize your village yard.

  • Drive Your Primitive Ride: Load up your squad in a stone-roller car with leopard-print seats and cruise the neighborhood (no driver's license required).

  • Tame the Wilderness: Set traps together, catch small dinosaurs, and turn them into your tribe's trusty pets.

  • Master Fire & Crafting: Bang rocks together to strike a spark and craft your hunting gear side-by-side.

  • Stay Well-Fed: Go on epic group mammoth hunts or whip up a massive feast with dodo eggs.

So, ready to drop the modern-day stress, grab your crew and your spears, and step straight into the Stone Age?

store_data.about_the_game:
You've been deployed to restore the ecosystem on an erosion-ravaged desert planet. Sadly, the funding for this mission was poorly arranged, and you have almost no resources with you. You'll have to attempt to harness the power of the planet's hardiest inhabitant: a flowering species of sheep! If you take care of them they can provide you with all sorts of seeds and, most importantly, poop.

A small, cozy terraforming game with a bit of sheep simulation. 

The missions

Each mission you land in a new crater, and your goal is to fill a certain percentage of the map with plant-life. Completing missions gives you funds to spend on lots of upgrades and bonuses for new missions (yes, there's sheep bonuses too) . The amount of funds you get after completing a mission depends on various factors, like ecosystem diversity, new discovered plants, and sheep well-being.

You start off with very tiny maps and unlock larger ones as you go and your capacity to terraform larger areas grows.

Manage water, your leafy-woolly friends, and plants

Plants need both water and soil to grow. The planet's rain cycle is dormant, but there is plenty of water under the  ground to tap into. You need to use different means to distribute this water to the plants. Once water is taken care of you need to find actual seeds to plant, and make sure the sheep in the area have enough to eat so that they can produce more resources for you.

The better you balance the ecosystem, the more sheep it will be able to support without your help.

Discover the seeds of extinct plant-life

The key to a truly self-sustaining and thriving ecosystem on this planet must lie in the ancient species of plants that used to grow here... the sheep seem to be growing various flowers on their backs, perhaps those produce viable seeds.

No combat, no survival pressure

There's nothing dangerous on this planet! And while the Interstellar Exoplanet Rejuvenation Foundation didn't have the resources to provide you with proper terraforming machinery, they have taken care of all your nutritional needs for this expedition, so you don't have to worry about eating or other survival concerns.

Additionally, the foundation will occasionally send you some extra equipment and upgrades to help with your work.

You don't tell the sheep what to do, the sheep do what the sheep want to do

And sometimes all they want to do is panic and run around, or sleep all day.

store_data.about_the_game:
NEW MATCH!

You wake up on a beautiful Saturday morning and open a dating app on your phone. As you browse through the profiles, a mysterious woman catches your attention. In her photos, she appears warm, cheerful, and perfect. But when you finally meet her, you notice a disturbing difference between the person you saw on the screen and the woman standing before you.

What begins as an ordinary date gradually turns into a dark and dangerous night. You must face the consequences of your decisions, follow the clues around you, and uncover the truth behind this unsettling situation.

FEATURES

  • A story-driven, first-person psychological horror experience

  • A mysterious story that begins through a dating app

  • An atmosphere of escalating tension as the hours pass

  • Dark secrets uncovered by carefully exploring your surroundings

  • Decisions that affect the course of the game

She looked perfect in her profile. But some people are not who they appear to be on the screen.

TONIGHT COULD BE YOUR LAST MATCH!

store_data.about_the_game:
Time is the only resource that matters

There is no health bar. There is a clock, and it is always running.

Every hit you take is seconds gone. Every wrong step, every trap, every enemy that reaches you first costs time you cannot get back. When the clock hits zero, the run is over. The only way to survive is to keep moving down.

Find the exit. Decide what is worth the detour. Get out before the timer

decides for you.

Get stronger, then lose it all

Every floor you clear offers a choice. Build a run that works, push deeper than

last time, and start over when it ends.

Find out what happened to them

The dungeon has people in it. Talk to them, look for what they left behind,

and reach an ending that fits what you found.

Features

Time as health — one resource for fighting, exploring and risking

Hand-built floors, each with its own threat

Turn-based combat on a grid

Permanent progression between runs

store_data.about_the_game:
What could possibly drive a person insane? What could make them to kidnap and eat people?

You are a police officer who is working on a case of a missing man named Victor. Your search led you into the woods, where you were kidnapped by an old woman.

Your goal is to find a way out from the house in five days. Find the reasons for what happened to the people who lived in the house. If you will not make it... Then you might have no other choice but to say hello to Victor.

To escape the house, you have to unlock the main door by using items or by fixing some objects.

But be careful, granny will use her traps to stop you.

Escape the crazy house: by going through the locked door.

Find the reason for what happened to people who lived and still live there

Think you can beat the game in 4 minutes? Or maybe leave the house without sprinting? Here are some of the challenges you can try:

Challenges you can try:

                   One life: you only have one day to leave the house. You can't expand it.

                   No running: you can't run for the whole game.

                   Granny can see you everywhere: you have 10 seconds before Granny begins chasing you. And no... She will not leave you alone until you're dead...

                   Finish the game under 4 minutes: you only have 4 minutes to leave the house. It's recommended to have a timer on while you attempt this challenge.

And don't forget. You're always welcome, in Granny's home....

store_data.about_the_game:
Inspect retro CCTV footage to uncover the truth behind a psychiatric patient's hallucinations in this Thai-inspired psychological horror anomaly observation game.

Monitor surveillance cameras across multiple locations, identify anomalies, and report them before the situation spirals out of control. Every recording reveals unsettling details that blur the line between psychological trauma and the supernatural.

Story

Thailand, 1997.

Kritsana, a psychiatric patient suffering from severe hallucinations and paranoia, refuses to accept his doctor's diagnosis. He believes the figures tormenting him are not symptoms of mental illness, but real spirits haunting his everyday life.

Determined to prove the truth, Kritsana records CCTV footage from places familiar to him and sends the tapes to his psychiatrist, Dr. Thanapat, hoping the doctor will finally witness what he sees.

You are tasked with reviewing these old VHS recordings. Observe every corner carefully, because what you are about to witness may force you to question whether this is merely a psychiatric disorder... or something far more disturbing.

Your Objectives

  • Monitor CCTV cameras across multiple locations.

  • Report every anomaly you discover.

  • Observe until 05:00 AM.

You will fail if you

  • Make 3 consecutive false reports.

  • Allow 4 active anomalies to exist simultaneously.

Controls

A / D or ← / → Keys - Switch CCTV cameras 

Hold Left Click - Report an anomaly

store_data.about_the_game:
Two worlds, one war

Humanity's Aegis Command holds the surface with steel, discipline and firepower. The Kharzeth pour out of the rifts — burning, spreading, feeding on the same ground you are trying to hold.

Both sides play by the rules you already know from the classics: raise a base, feed it, defend it, and push out. Both sides break those rules in their own way.

A real-time strategy game you can stand inside

Iron Command plays on your monitor like the strategy games it grew out of. Put on a headset and the same battle is laid out in front of you: you look down on the terrain, reach out, and give orders from a tablet strapped to your wrist. Build, produce, research, check your objectives — all of it from the wrist, without ever leaving the field.

What you do

  • Build a base — command centre, refinery, power, factories, research, defences
  • Run an economy — harvest riftstones, keep the power on, expand under pressure
  • Research — upgrades that change how your units fight, not just their numbers
  • Fight — infantry, tanks, artillery, air defence, and turrets that hold a line

Content

  • Commander training — five missions that teach one mechanic each
  • Skirmish — ten maps against the AI, with difficulty and pace you set
  • Multiplayer — one on one over Steam, or directly on your own network

Playable flat or in VR

One game, one build. Start it on your monitor with mouse and keyboard, or start it in VR — the campaign, the skirmishes and the multiplayer are the same in both.
