store_data.about_the_game:
[h2]You are not armed.[/h2]

Everything on this screen wants to shoot you, and you did not bring a gun.

What you have is a blade, a parry window measured in frames, and the fact

that a reflected bullet hits a lot harder than an original one.

[b]LIGHTBLADE[/b] is a compact arcade survival game built around one action.

Point the blade. Hit the button at the right moment. The shot that was about

to kill you becomes the shot that clears the arena.

[h2]The loop[/h2]

[list]

[*][b]Parry, don't dodge.[/b] You cannot move. You can only turn, and you can

only defend. Every threat has to be answered, not avoided.

[*][b]Reflected fire is your only damage.[/b] Nothing you do kills an enemy

directly. Every kill on your scoreboard came out of an enemy's own gun.

[*][b]Perfect timing pays double.[/b] Catch a shot in the first frames of the

window and time stretches, the screen flares, and your combo climbs faster.

[*][b]Burst clears the board.[/b] Bank enough energy from clean parries and

one keypress reflects every bullet on screen at once.

[/list]

[h2]What you're up against[/h2]

[list]

[*][b]Drones[/b] — steady single shots. They teach you the rhythm.

[*][b]Burst units[/b] — three-round spreads that punish a lazy blade angle.

[*][b]Rushers[/b] — they don't shoot. They come for the core.

[*][b]Snipers[/b] — fast, quiet, and they will end a 30-hit combo.

[*][b]Splitters[/b] — kill one carelessly and it scatters on the way out.

[*][b]Wardens[/b] — every fifth wave, a boss with three attack patterns and

enough health that you'll have to parry your way through all of them.

[/list]

[h2]Built to be replayed, not finished[/h2]

Waves are endless and scale continuously — there is no ending screen to reach,

only a number to beat. Runs are short. Deaths are your fault and you will know

exactly why. The full stat readout after every run tells you how many parries

landed, how many were perfect, and where the combo broke.

[h2]Made small on purpose[/h2]

No tutorial pop-ups, no unlocks gating the good stuff, no launcher, no account.

Click and you're in the arena within two seconds. Full controller support,

remappable-free single-button design, and a mute key that actually works.

[h2]Honest scope[/h2]

This is a focused arcade game, not a 40-hour epic. If you want a leaderboard

chase you can pick up for ten minutes at a time and get visibly better at,

that's exactly what this is. If you want story, crafting, or an open world,

this isn't it.

5089470.name: Riggin Farm: Raw Land to Riches

store_data.about_the_game:
About This Game

Riggin Farm: Raw Land to Riches is a deep, long-form farming and business management RPG about two new farmers, Nick & Ashley, transforming 25 acres of undeveloped woodland into a thriving, diversified farm.

You don't inherit a barn, a tractor, or neatly prepared fields. You begin with raw land, limited money, and a decision: what kind of farm are you going to build?

Clear land. Build your home. Prepare your first growing areas. Raise livestock. Sell at farmers markets. Hire employees. Invest in infrastructure. Develop new enterprises. Survive bad weather, equipment failures, escaped animals, unexpected expenses, and all the other things that rarely appear in the brochure for starting a farm.

And then keep going.

Build a Farm From the Ground Up

Your farm develops over years, not days.

What begins as a small garden carved out of the woods can eventually become a complex agricultural business with vegetable production, livestock, markets, farm-store sales, employees, specialized infrastructure, and multiple sources of income.

You decide where to invest your time and money and how quickly you want to grow.

Expansion creates opportunity, but it also creates more work, more expenses, and more things that can go wrong.

Grow, Harvest, and Sell Realistically

Crops aren't simply planted and instantly turned into profit.

Different crops have different production cycles, harvest windows, yields, labor requirements, and market potential. Some crops can be harvested repeatedly while others give you one opportunity to get the timing right.

You'll need to decide what to grow, how much to plant, when to harvest, and where to sell it.

Producing a mountain of tomatoes doesn't mean much if your customers only want ten pounds.

Raise Livestock

Build livestock enterprises around animals such as pigs, cattle, and chickens.

Purchase animals, manage breeding, provide feed and infrastructure, maintain fencing, and deal with the unpredictable reality of keeping living creatures on a farm.

Animals can become valuable long-term assets, but they also require daily attention.

And yes, sometimes the pigs get out.

Run a Real Farm Business

Growing food is only part of the job.

You'll also have to figure out how to sell it.

Prepare for farmers markets, stock your booth, manage inventory and back stock, operate your farm store, work with customers, pursue wholesale opportunities, and decide which products deserve your limited table space.

As your farm grows, you'll make increasingly difficult decisions about pricing, labor, equipment, infrastructure, debt, and expansion.

A successful farm isn't necessarily the farm that produces the most.

It's the farm that can actually sell what it produces.

Build Your Market Booth

Farmers markets are an interactive part of the business rather than a simple "sell inventory" button.

Choose your tables, organize products, prepare back stock, and decide how to use your limited display space.

A full, attractive booth can encourage sales. Empty tables and poor product selection can hurt them.

Your market strategy may change from week to week depending on what's ready to harvest, what's sitting in inventory, and what your customers are actually buying.

Hire Employees and Manage a Growing Operation

Eventually, there may simply be too much work for two people.

Hire employees, assign responsibilities, manage labor costs, and gradually move from doing everything yourself to running a larger agricultural operation.

Growth can make your farm more profitable, but every new enterprise competes for the same limited resources:

Money. Labor. Time.

Expect Things to Go Wrong

Farming rarely follows the plan.

Storms arrive at the wrong time.

Equipment breaks.

Employees call out.

Animals escape.

Fences fail.

Crops disappoint you.

Customers ask for the one thing you just sold out of.

You might discover that the card reader wasn't charged when the farmers market opens.

Get the truck stuck.

Return from processing only to realize there isn't enough freezer space.

Some problems are serious.

Others are simply part of the story you'll tell later.

Your Farm, Your Strategy

There is no single correct way to build Riggin Farm.

You can emphasize vegetables, livestock, direct-to-consumer sales, farmers markets, the farm store, wholesale relationships, or a diversified combination of everything.

Expand aggressively with borrowed money or grow slowly using farm profits.

Hire help or stay small.

Build infrastructure early or squeeze every possible season out of what you already have.

The decisions are yours, and the consequences accumulate over decades.

A Farming RPG Inspired by a Real Farm

Riggin Farm: Raw Land to Riches is inspired by the experiences of building and operating a real diversified farm.

The game embraces both sides of farming: the satisfaction of watching something grow from almost nothing and the absolute absurdity of trying to keep an agricultural business running when nature, animals, equipment, customers, employees, and your own questionable decisions all have other plans.

Build the farm.

Grow the business.

Make mistakes.

Recover from them.

And find out whether you can run Riggin Farm better than the actual owners of the real Riggin Farm.

store_data.about_the_game:
You're a blacksmith one bad month from losing the family forge. The loan's due at the end of the month, so you take the cheap work: dredging rusted blades off dead adventurers, escorting grain carts, hauling out whatever the last party couldn't.

Then you melt it down and make something better.

GEAR IS THE CLASS

Four wanderers walk in off the road in plain travel clothes. None of them is anything in particular yet. Put plate and a tower shield on one and he's your tank. Take it off, hand him silk and a staff, and he throws fireballs instead. Same four bodies, different party.

You're never arming the mage. There's no mage until you put a staff in someone's hands.

YOU DON'T FIGHT, YOU FORGE

Once they're kitted they go down without you, and you don't have to watch. Stay at the anvil and the run sits in a corner widget: four health bars, the floor they're on, loot scrolling past as they pick it up. It goes red before a wipe, and there's a Tactical Retreat button for when you see it coming.

Or open the dungeon view and watch the whole fight, damage numbers and all. Nothing pauses either way.

THE SHOP SHOWS YOUR WORK

You start in a cracked room with one working smelter and a debt notice nailed to the door. Every rank you climb lights another station, fills the shelves, and warms the place up. By the time you're Legend of the Forge there are banners on the walls and people at the door watching you work.

AT THE ANVIL

Smelt ore into alloys. Roll prefixes and suffixes off whatever you feed the enchanter. Cut sockets, set gems, and stack same-material sets for buffs that hit the whole party. Push all of it through a research tree that takes the chores off your hands, so the smelting and the selling start running themselves.

REPUTATION OPENS THE MAP

Salvage contracts first. As your name gets around you get into Verdant Hollow, then the Ruined Outskirts, then the Warren Depths.

When you hit a wall you can't forge your way past, you hang up the hammer and hand the shop to an heir. He keeps what you earned and starts with more room to grow.

WORTH KNOWING

The sim runs whether you're looking at it or not, and it's deterministic: same seed, same choices, same outcome, every time.

It's done when you buy it. No microtransactions, no energy timers, nothing to buy later.

It goes red before a wipe, and there's a Tactical Retreat button for when you see it coming.

Or open the dungeon view and watch the whole fight, damage numbers and all. Nothing pauses either way.

THE SHOP SHOWS YOUR WORK

You start in a cracked room with one working smelter and a debt notice nailed to the door. Every rank you climb lights another station, fills the shelves, and warms the place up. By the time you're Legend of the Forge there are banners on the walls and people at the door watching you work.

AT THE ANVIL

Smelt ore into alloys. Roll prefixes and suffixes off whatever you feed the enchanter. Cut sockets, set gems, and stack same-material sets for buffs that hit the whole party. Push all of it through a research tree that takes the chores off your hands, so the smelting and the selling start running themselves.

REPUTATION OPENS THE MAP

Salvage contracts first. As your name gets around you get into Verdant Hollow, then the Ruined Outskirts, then the Warren Depths.

When you hit a wall you can't forge your way past, you hang up the hammer and hand the shop to an heir. He keeps what you earned and starts with more room to grow.

WORTH KNOWING

The sim runs whether you're looking at it or not, and it's deterministic: same seed, same choices, same outcome, every time.

It's done when you buy it. No microtransactions, no energy timers, nothing to buy later.
store_data.short_description: Your forge is cold and the loan's due at the end of the month. Take the jobs nobody else wants, hammer out the gear, and hand it to four wanderers who fight like whatever you put in their hands.

store_data.about_the_game:
Kris is an HK-94 household companion: warm-hearted, a little scratched, and thirty years out of date. In a retro-futuristic world where robots became as ordinary as cars, sleek new models have made machines like him disposable. When his certification is set to expire in 30 days, a box of old floppy disks offers him one last chance to show what he can do.

Explore a lovingly detailed town, talk with its people and solve classic point-and-click puzzles through observation, improvisation and care. Load ability disks into Kris's limited slots to repair circuits, climb, cook, clean or find another way forward. Different tools can open different solutions—but memory is finite. Keeping a new ability may mean overwriting part of the life that made Kris who he is.

BUILT TO 1993 RULES

Not a filter. Not a nostalgia toggle. A rule the whole game obeys. KRIS runs at 640×360 in one locked palette of 32 colours, and that limit is enforced rather than intended: a single off-palette pixel, or one with a soft edge, fails the build. No anti-aliasing, no smoothing, no upscaling mush — just crisp pixels, warm summer light, and screens worth sitting in for a moment before you click.

The animation obeys it too. Kris never teleports through a task. He walks over, drops to his knees, reaches up, braces against something heavy and hauls it along — over a thousand animations across forty-five characters, set frame by frame, fifty-six for Kris alone. And it is the default, not the showpiece: if you can touch it, it has a movement. Unless it is the sky.

Put this on a shelf in 1993 and nobody would have looked twice. Except at the box art.

KRIS: The Last Good Summer is a story-driven pixel-art adventure about usefulness, planned obsolescence, growing old and the people who remember us. Its retro comedy and multiple-choice conversations lead to a hearing where the people Kris helped must answer a question no specification sheet can: is a life valuable only while it is efficient?

store_data.about_the_game:
People spend their lives trying to become someone else. At the end, all they want is to die as themselves.

Meridian Archive is an independent neo-noir crime visual novel centered on its characters and the exploration of a deeply layered world.

The story takes place in Notus, in the year 2008.

Ten years ago, an unnatural fog brought with it a disaster now known as Saltification. Skin, organs, and eventually even memories begin to crystallize and harden. The disease reshaped entire cities—and redefined how much a human life is worth.

Major institutions monopolize the medical resources people need to stay alive. Industrial committees reduce survival to labor hours and production quotas. Meanwhile, gangs, smugglers, research institutes, and local authorities maintain another set of rules in the cracks left behind by the system.

The world did not end.

People went back to work.

They drink coffee, ride the subway, visit bars, and drive aging cars through crowded streets.

It is just that something, somewhere, has gone terribly wrong.

One rainy night.

A battered white Santana sits beside an abandoned highway.

When Knight wakes up, all that remains of him is his head.

Something has torn his body apart. His memories are incomplete. And in the back seat of the car sits a strange woman with the designation “701-B” attached to her ankle.

After an impossible bolt of lightning, Knight somehow comes back to “life.”

Now they have to make their way south, toward the industrial city of WestAwiok.

There, another man named Weiwei is resorting to increasingly self-destructive methods to stop his memories from disappearing.

They are what this world calls Nomads.

People who cannot contract Saltification.

And people the world would rather not have to see.

In Meridian Archive, you will follow different characters through the cities, ports, underground facilities, wastelands, and remote islands of Notus, gradually piecing together the world through their conflicts, choices, and chance encounters.

Choices made in dialogue, specific scenes, and character variables can unlock new information.

People. Places. Diseases. Corporations. Criminal organizations. Incident reports. Obsolete machines. Even things that seem completely meaningless.

All of them can become part of your Archive.

Sometimes, the liquidation report of a defunct corporation tells you more than a confession ever could.

Sometimes, an obsolete toilet with mechanical legs, endlessly spitting out thermal paper, is more honest than the government that built the world around it.

Meridian Archive is not a story about saving the world.

There are no heroes here in the traditional sense.

Some people want to smash the system apart.

Some want to outthink it.

Some only want to remember who they were yesterday.

And for some, the greatest dream they have left is to find a corner of the city the cameras cannot see, finish a terrible cup of coffee, and quietly survive until tomorrow.

In a world drifting toward stillness, formatting, and oblivion—

perhaps simply staying alive is the last form of resistance.

store_data.about_the_game:
Blackwire is a single-player hacking simulation in the spirit of the classics. You are a freelance agent with a gateway, a contract board, and a trace timer that does not care how close you were to done.

Take contracts from fictional corporations, copy files, empty an account, rewrite a criminal record, put someone in prison. Build a bounce route a dozen hops long before you touch the target, because every hop you put between yourself and them is time on the clock when they notice you. And they will notice you.

Then get out, and clean up after yourself. Their admins walk your log trail hop by hop, and the entry that names your gateway is sitting on the first server you bounced through. Scrubbing it is not a side activity. It is how you stay alive.

FEATURES

A living network — hundreds of servers, banks, registries, and mainframes. Every machine keeps logs. Every log can hang you.

The trace is the game — an active countdown while you work, a passive investigation after you leave. Outrun one, erase the other.

Follow the money — crack a bank account and chase stolen funds through chains of transfers, or wire someone else's credits to yourself.

Mainframes — crawl their internal interface lock by lock towards root, past scanners, ICE, and counter-intrusion hardware that hacks you back.

Build your rig — mainboards, cpus, drives, and a catalogue of software from bruteforce to ghost. Split your CPU between the crack and the shield and hope you split it right.

Two corporations at war — both want to hire you against the other. Both pay well. Both remember.

A story that finds you — someone is clearing freelance agents off the board, one by one. Your name is on a list you have to steal to read.

Entirely offline. No accounts, no server, a game about the fantasy of hacking, the way it looked in the movies and never was.

store_data.about_the_game:
A galaxy that doesn't wait for you

Starlathe is a 2D top-down space sim where the galaxy runs for real. Miners cut ore from asteroid fields, transporters haul goods between stations, factories consume and produce, War Fleets clash over territory — all simulated live across 150 sectors, whether you're watching or not. Nothing is faked, nothing spawns from thin air: every shipment travels, every ship flies, every wreck was someone's ship.

Earn your place

Start with a small ship and choose your path:

  • Mine asteroid fields and refine your ore into something worth more

  • Trade across a real supply chain of over 50 goods — buy where it's cheap, haul it where it's needed

  • Fight — hunt pirates for factions, or become the pirate yourself and live with your reputation

  • Craft weapons, modules and ships through refining, components and full production chains

Build and command your own fleet

Buy ships, assign them roles, and put them to work: your own miners feeding your income, transporters running your routes, escorts guarding your convoys — up to a dreadnought flagship leading your battle line. Fleet battles are fought ship to ship with turrets, rockets, beams and point defense, not dice rolls.

A galaxy with consequences

Stations die for real — evacuations, wrecks, loot fields — and factions rebuild them. Territory changes hands. Prices react to real supply and demand. The law notices smuggling and piracy. Your reputation follows you.

Explore the unknown

Fog of war hides the galaxy until you chart it. Find ship graveyards, abandoned sectors, wild space beyond the gates — and 22 skies to fly under.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Body You Draw Becomes the Solution.

Draw your own character and work together to reach the goal in this online co-op puzzle platformer for up to 4 players!

Long legs?
Huge wings?
Or spend all your INK creating something completely ridiculous?

Your character's abilities change depending on what you draw and how you spend your INK.

Run faster. Glide through the air. Stick to walls.
Pick up your friends and throw them. Grab onto each other.
Sometimes, your friends might even become part of the solution.

There's more than one way to clear a stage.

Combine your characters' unique abilities and find your own way to the goal.

✏️ Draw It. Then Play It.

Body, arms, legs, wings, shell...

Draw your character however you like, then watch your creation come to life.

And your drawing isn't just cosmetic.

How you draw your legs affects your movement, while the amount of INK you spend on your wings affects your ability to glide.

With limited INK, deciding where to use it becomes part of the puzzle.

And don't worry about drawing well.

Sometimes, the weirdest character is exactly what you need.

🐱 Five Character Types

Human
Pick up and throw friends, boxes, bombs, and more. The way you draw your arms and legs affects your abilities.

Cat
Fast on its feet. Use your claws to grab onto another player and hitch a ride.

Bird
Use your wings to glide through the air. You can also grab your friends with your beak and carry them along.

Turtle
Hide inside your shell to block incoming attacks. Turn your body to shield your friends from lasers and explosions.

Slime
Stick to walls and leap from one wall to another. You can even stick to your friends and let them carry you.

🤝 Impossible Alone? Maybe Not Together.

Throw a friend onto a platform you can't reach.

Grab on to a bird and cross a huge gap together.

Use a turtle as a shield against incoming lasers.

Send a slime up a wall to activate a switch for everyone else.

How you combine your abilities is entirely up to you.

Of course...

You might throw your friend in the wrong direction.

Everyone might fall at the same time.

Or one tiny mistake might ruin the perfect plan at the very last second.

Getting it wrong is part of the fun.

💥 It's Not Always About Reaching the Goal

Moving platforms, spikes, lasers, conveyor belts, collapsing floors, bombs, cannons, and plenty more stand in your way.

And not every stage follows the same rules.

Collect all the fish before time runs out!

Survive as the floor disappears beneath you!

Dodge a ridiculous number of bombs!

Some stages completely change the objective, so you never know what the next challenge will bring.

🎮 Features

  • Draw your own character and watch it come to life

  • Your character's abilities change based on its shape and how you spend your INK

  • Five character types: Human, Cat, Bird, Turtle, and Slime

  • Online co-op for up to 4 players

  • Pick up, throw, grab, carry, ride, and work together

  • Co-op puzzles with more than one solution

  • A variety of stages, including special challenges with completely different rules

  • A hand-drawn world inspired by notebooks and crayons

  • Succeed together. Fail together. Laugh either way.

store_data.about_the_game:
PIERLINE

Pierline is a short first-person psychological horror game about an ordinary night that takes an unexpected turn. You play as Daniel Hayes, a Florida traffic officer who decides to spend the night fishing at an old pier along the coast, after a friend recommends the place.

The pier seems quiet. The water is calm, the area is nearly deserted, and everything points to a peaceful night of fishing.

Gameplay

Explore the old pier, fish, investigate your surroundings, and interact with the environment as the night unfolds.

Pay attention to your surroundings and piece together the events that took place there.

Key Features

  • First-person psychological horror

  • Atmospheric setting inspired by the Florida coast

  • An old pier to explore at night

  • Fishing mechanics

  • Binocular mechanics

  • Environmental exploration and interaction

  • Short, focused narrative

  • Realistic visuals with an analog/VHS-inspired atmosphere

  • Approximately 20 minutes of game

store_data.about_the_game:
Panda Fishing: The Way of Angling is a 2D fishing simulation game rooted in real Taiwan-style angling logic.

You play as an angler, starting from urban waterways and gradually exploring distinctive fishing spots across the country. Each fishing trip is a complete strategic preparation—you must carefully match rods, line sets, hooks, floats, and baits based on your target species and water conditions. Float-tuning, bottom detection, bite-reading—every step tests your understanding of the fish.

Authentic Angling Simulation
The game deeply simulates the core logic of Taiwan-style fishing: high-to-low float tuning, sensitivity switching, bait state adjustment, and line setup matching. This is not a simple "cast and wait" game—it requires you to make real-time decisions based on changing fish behavior.

Rich Equipment System
From budget rods to premium flagship models, from sleeve hooks to Qianyū hooks—dozens of rods, line sets, hooks, floats, and baits are available for free combination. Different setups suit different fish conditions. Every combination is a new experiment.

Immersive Fishing Experience
Fresh hand-painted 2D art style, combined with realistic float movements, bite feedback, and natural ambient sound effects—bringing the calm and focus of riverside fishing to your screen.

Exploration & Collection
Unlock diverse fishing locations—from urban canals to Shengzhong Lake, each with unique fish species, water conditions, and weather patterns. Complete your fish collection, keep your own fishing log, and leave your angling memories behind.

Gear up, and cast your line. The stories beneath the surface await.

store_data.about_the_game:
Tonight's guest doesn't know he's on television. You're the ghost performer on the Ghostly Late Night Show. Out on stage, an audience is waiting. Behind the portal door, Billy is trying to make himself a sandwich. Your job is to make that funny.

▸ You direct the act

Fifteen handcrafted episodes, each packed with gags waiting to be set off. Which ones you rig, in what order, and when you let them fire is your call. Set three to land in sequence. Or set up one and let Billy do the rest of the work. Move a chair six inches and the whole act reroutes. Same room, different show, every time.

Timing, escalation, surprise, payoff. That part's on you.

▸ Pick an orb, open a door

Every episode starts on stage, in front of the crowd. Choose from a shelf of glowing orbs — each one holds a moment from Billy's day. Load it into the portal machine and the door opens onto that scene: cooking, watching TV, exercising, cleaning, trying to relax. Different orb, different room, different set of things to go wrong.

▸ Don't let him see you

Billy can spot a ghost. Stay out of his line of sight while you set everything up.

Duck behind furniture, freeze, wait for him to turn around.

Get caught and the act is over. The audience will not be kind.

▸ Hand-animated slapstick

Every gag in the house is hand-animated in classic cartoon style — squash, stretch, and comic timing, the way slapstick is supposed to move. Trip the right prop and you get a full piece of physical comedy, not a physics accident.

▸ The audience decides

When it's done, step back through the portal and take the stage. The crowd

rates your performance in stars.

Weak show, polite applause. Great show, and new episode orbs unlock.

▸ Sandbox: keep everything you unlock

Every episode you finish adds its signature prop to Sandbox mode — no script, no timer, nobody watching the clock.

Just the whole toybox and whatever you can build out of it.

The more episodes you clear, the more there is to combine.

▸ Bring a friend

Online co-op for 2–4 players. More ghosts, more mess.

▸ Two ways to play

Flatscreen with keyboard and mouse, or VR with any OpenXR headset. Same game,

same episodes, one purchase.

 

▸ Features

• Online co-op for 2–4 players

• Creative sandbox that grows with every episode you finish

• Record your cartoon and replay on a big cinema screen.

• SteamVR and VR Headsets with 6DOF

• PC Standalone - Keyboard and Mouse

• PC Standalone - Gamepad

• Voiced in 15 languages

store_data.about_the_game:
Deadship Protocol is a bullet heaven for 1–4 players. Play online or on the same couch, or take on the ship alone. Fight hordes of energy-feeding aliens, recover eight Protocol Cores, and choose powerful upgrades before the reactor runs out of power.

1–4 PLAYER CO-OP

Play online or on the same couch with up to three friends, or face the run alone. Split up to search the ship, hold the reactor, and revive downed crewmates. Someone must stay near the reactor.

LEAVE THE REACTOR TO SAVE IT

The Purge needs eight Protocol Cores, and every one lies beyond the reactor room. Leave the ship's last power source undefended, push through the swarm, and carry each core home before the aliens drain it dry.

BUILD A SCREEN-CLEARING ARSENAL

Weapons fire automatically, so focus on moving, dashing, and aiming your Operator's emergency special. Choose from four Operators and combine more than 20 upgrades into coil fire, caustic payloads, drones, and critical hits.

ARM THE PURGE

Each recovered core makes you stronger and brings the Purge closer. Bring back all eight, survive the Devourer, and finish the run in about 12–18 minutes. Generated ship layouts and changing upgrade choices make every attempt play differently.

store_data.about_the_game:
The corruption beneath the harvest has awakened.

What begins in a familiar pumpkin patch leads through candlelit graveyards, crooked bridges, enchanted forests and increasingly impossible places. Every realm is a detailed animated gothic diorama, filled with flickering light, moving weather, hidden routes and enemies designed to test a different part of your defence.

Build an arsenal, not a disposable loadout

Towers you purchase enter your Tower Bank. Redeploy the towers you already own on later battlefields, improve them through multiple visible upgrade tiers, or sell them at a loss when a new strategy demands it. The choices made early in the campaign shape the resources and options available later.

Read the threat before the wave arrives

Enemy portraits reveal what is approaching and identify armour, immunity and movement type. Physical, fire, shock and magic attacks each have battles where they excel — and enemies that punish relying on only one answer. Ground traps, support structures, air threats and water routes keep each map tactically different.

Survive a campaign that keeps changing

Waves are authored as distinct tactical problems rather than repeated stat ramps. Gold does not come from kills alone: hire miners to work the ground behind your lines and they earn their cost back over many trips, so every hire is weighed against a tower you could build right now. Choose when to expand, when to upgrade, and when to send the next wave in early for bonus gold. Later realms demand that you balance immediate survival against the resources needed for the battles ahead.

A haunted world built to move

Lanterns flicker, shadows breathe, rain strengthens, rivers flow and the landscape reacts around the battle. Each realm has its own landmark, colour language, route design, ambient soundscape and Halloween identity while remaining part of one connected journey.

Key features

  • A fifteen-level gothic Halloween campaign.
  • A persistent Tower Bank that carries owned towers and upgrades forward.
  • A gold economy of real decisions: hire miners that pay back over time, or call the next wave in early for a bonus.
  • Distinct physical, fire, shock, magic, support and path-trap strategies.
  • Four visible upgrade tiers for the starting tower set.
  • Ground, flying and water-route enemies with armour and immunity counters.
  • Hand-authored waves, bosses and economy choices rather than repeated stat ramps.
  • Animated 3D-rendered battlefields with dynamic lighting, weather and sound.
  • Central audio mixing with separate music, ambience and effects controls.

store_data.about_the_game:
Beach Manager Simulator is a first-person management game about running a busy public beach.

Your beach starts small: a stretch of sand, a few guests, limited equipment and a business that needs to survive the day. Visitors pay to enter, look for a place to relax, buy items from your beach market and leave behind trash as the beach gets crowded.

Every decision affects the flow of the day. Dirty sand lowers satisfaction. Empty shelves disappoint guests. Missing loungers cost you income. A well-kept beach brings more visitors, better earnings and new opportunities to expand.

RUN THE BEACH

Open the beach, welcome guests and keep the area under control. Place loungers and umbrellas, manage the space and make sure visitors have what they need before small problems become expensive ones.

KEEP GUESTS SATISFIED

Guest satisfaction is the heart of your business. Clean areas, available equipment and stocked shelves help your beach reputation grow. Neglect the basics and your daily income will suffer.

CLEAN THE SHORE

Trash builds up as the day goes on. Pick it up, clear dirty spots and keep the coastline presentable. A clean beach is not just cosmetic - it directly affects how guests feel about your business.

STOCK THE BEACH MARKET

Your market gives visitors a reason to spend more money. Keep products available throughout the day and react before empty shelves start hurting satisfaction.

SEARCH FOR LOST VALUABLES

Use your metal detector to search the sand for lost items. Some discoveries can be sold for extra income, helping you buy upgrades and grow faster.

EXPAND YOUR BUSINESS

Start with a small beach area and unlock larger sections over time. More space means more guests, more income, more trash and more pressure to manage everything efficiently.

KEY FEATURES

First-person beach management gameplay

Paid beach entry and daily income

Guest satisfaction system

Beach cleaning and trash collection

Lounger and umbrella management

Beach market stocking

Metal detector and lost valuables

Upgrades and beach expansion

Single-player simulation experience

store_data.about_the_game:
“Looking for a Property?”

While your classmates are landing jobs at well-known companies, you find yourself completely worn out by the job hunt.

Then one day, you happen to notice a help-wanted ad in town and end up taking a job at Odate Real Estate, a small neighborhood real estate agency.

Working alongside your boss, Hisui Odate, your job is to listen to your customers, search through countless listings, and recommend a home that suits each of them.

Rent. Floor plan. Distance from the station.
But those aren't always the only things your customers are looking for.

Listen closely to what they say, uncover the wishes hidden between the lines, organize their priorities, and find your own answer to the question of where they should live.

Listen and Find Out What They Really Want

Every customer begins with a conversation.

“I want somewhere close to the station.”
“I'd prefer a quiet neighborhood.”
“I want to keep the rent low, but I'd still like a spacious room.”

You won't always be able to satisfy every request at once.

What matters most to them?
What are they willing to compromise on?

Use every word as a clue and think carefully about the kind of life your customer is really looking for.

Search for Properties

Once you understand what your customer wants, it's time to use the property search terminal at your desk.

Search through listings using a variety of criteria, including rent, floor plan, location, and distance from the nearest station.

Narrow down the results, compare the available properties, and choose the one you want to recommend.

Sometimes you'll find exactly what the customer is looking for. Other times, something will have to give.

Which conditions you prioritize is up to you.

Make Your Recommendation

Once you've chosen a property, present it to your customer.

How they react depends on what you learned from the conversation—and on the property you decided to recommend.

A room that checks every box on paper isn't necessarily the perfect home for that person.

Consider each customer's circumstances and help them find the place that makes them think, “I want to live here.”

After Work...

When the workday ends, sometimes you simply head home.

You might suddenly remember that your taxes are due and panic, or look at your bank balance with a satisfied grin.

And on some evenings, Hisui might invite you out for a drink.

At your usual Chinese restaurant or local izakaya, she may open up about the problems facing the little real estate agency—and perhaps even tell you about her own past.

A Story About the City and Real Estate

As you continue working day after day, the situation surrounding the agency gradually changes—and so does your relationship with Hisui.

What kind of real estate agent will you become?
What kind of place will you help this little agency become?

The choices are yours.

Features

  • A customer service simulation where you uncover each client's needs and circumstances through conversation

  • Search for properties by rent, floor plan, location, distance from the station, and other conditions

  • Decide what to prioritize when no property can satisfy every request

  • Customer reactions and evaluations that change depending on the properties you recommend

  • Manage your money, prepare for unexpected expenses, and make ends meet

  • A story-driven adventure following everyday life at Odate Real Estate and your relationship with Hisui Odate

  • Retro PC-inspired visuals and UI with a city pop atmosphere

store_data.about_the_game:
It has been raining for three days. Or the city is crying. Hard to say — you're a detective, not a weatherman.

The last shawarma in town is gone. The owner is destroyed. The police have "real crimes". You work for seeds, and you just took the case.

A noir told in black, grey, and a single colour of gold.

What you do

  • Interrogate impossible witnesses. A pigeon who sells the truth by the seed ("the coo — that's the VAT"). A vending machine that has stood in the underpass for eleven years and answers only in products. A femme fatale who wandered in from a more expensive movie.

  • Spend seeds, not money. In this city the whole economy — even justice — runs on sunflower seeds. Every question costs. Haggle if you dare.

  • Read the evidence. Examine crumpled foil under a magnifier, crack a four-digit order archive, finish a femme fatale's lines before the pause becomes an answer.

  • Reach the truth you were avoiding. Multiple endings. One of them you will not like — because a man doesn't remember what he didn't pay for.

Features

  • A dense, hand-written noir-comedy script — every line played straight.

  • Five little cases-within-the-case: foil analysis, haggling, the order archive, a duel of lines, and the detective's notebook.

  • Branching investigation with several endings and a case file that remembers your best run.

  • Fully bilingual — English and Russian, switchable any time, with adjustable text speed.

  • Adaptive picture: resize the window freely or go fullscreen — no black bars, ever.

  • 100% drawn in code — not a single sprite. Rain, neon, wet asphalt and smoke, all procedural.

  • Short and dense. A case you can close in one rainy evening.

Justice was done — and it tasted of onions.

store_data.about_the_game:
HARDCORE ROUND-BASED SURVIVAL

HIVEROT is a zombie FPS focused on intense gunplay, in-match progression, and enemies that physically react to every hit.

Fight through increasingly difficult rounds, earn points, build a loadout, unlock the map, and prepare for whatever joins the next wave. There is no final round. Survive for as long as you can.

MANY DIFFERENT ENEMY TYPES

The horde becomes more dangerous as the game progresses. Fight standard zombies alongside flying skulls, electric conduits, ranged laser-wielding brutes, massive spiders, tentacled monstrosities, and many other enemy types.

All enemies stagger under gunfire, lose limbs, collapse, crawl after taking heavy damage, burn, break apart, and fly through the environment under powerful impacts.

Each map has its own enemy roster and special rounds system that introduces new threats, forces you to rethink your strategy, and adapt your loadout and positioning.

BUILD POWERFUL LOADOUTS

You earn points by damaging enemies, and can spend these points to purchase weapons and ammunition, access new areas, activate various traps, upgrade your weapons, and buy perks that change your stats and abilities. Additionally, timed power-ups and special rewards can turn a failing run around or give you an opportunity to try a different strategy.

MORE THAN 50 WEAPONS

Use pistols, shotguns, rifles, submachine guns, machine guns, explosives, melee weapons, and heavy weapons with distinct handling, recoil, reload animations, movement characteristics, and attachments.

Discover experimental weapons that create black holes, suspend enemies in anti-gravity fields, spread infections, launch targets across rooms, burn groups, and much, much more.

VARIED MAPS

Each map contains its own unique layout, purchases, power systems, objectives, and secrets to discover.

PLANNED MULTIPLAYER AND FREE DEMO

4 player co-op is planned for full release. A free single-player demo will be released before the end of 2026.

store_data.about_the_game:
About This Game

Enter a cursed world where survival alone is not enough.

Unhallowed Survivors is a dark fantasy bullet heaven roguelite built around distinct heroes, signature weapons, escalating hordes and dangerous choices.

Choose your hero and enter corrupted battlefields filled with cultists, restless dead and twisted creatures. Move manually while your hero attacks automatically, collect experience, level up and transform a single signature weapon into a specialized build.

MASTER DISTINCT HEROES

Every hero fights differently.

Instead of collecting the same universal weapon pool every run, each hero carries a unique core weapon with their own mechanics, upgrades and specialization paths.

Fight at range with the Excommunicated Huntress, carve through enemies with the Shadowblade, or spread poison, curses and volatile alchemy as the Plague Doctor.

SPECIALIZE YOUR WEAPON

Every run begins with your hero's core weapon in its basic form.

Hunt down the first cursed reliquary and choose one of your unlocked specializations. Your choice lasts for the rest of the run and reshapes which weapon upgrades become available.

Build around critical strikes, elemental effects, bleeding, poison, crowd control, explosions and other hero-specific mechanics.

HUNT CURSED RELIQUARIES

Survival is only part of your objective.

Cursed reliquaries awaken throughout each run. Reach them and decide how far you are willing to go.

Seal them to secure lasting map progress.

Desecrate them to gain powerful advantages for the current run — at the cost of a curse.

Power can save your run. It can also make what comes next considerably worse.

FACE ESCALATING HORDE COMBAT

Enemy pressure increases as the run progresses.

Fight growing hordes, ranged threats, elites, mini-bosses and corrupted stage bosses while maintaining control of your positioning and build.

Combat effects are designed around readability: dangerous attacks, enemies, pickups and boss telegraphs must remain visible even when your build begins to escalate.

GROW BETWEEN RUNS

Victory and defeat both leave a mark.

Progress through new stages, unlock additional heroes and specializations, improve your mastery and expand the possibilities available in future runs.

Bosses, reliquaries and long-term progression gradually push you deeper into the corrupted world.

Build your hero. Hunt the reliquaries. Embrace forbidden power.

BUY ONCE. PLAY WITHOUT PRESSURE.

Unhallowed Survivors is a one-time purchase.

There are no in-game shops, no premium currencies, no pay-to-win mechanics, no pay-to-progress systems and no advertising inside the game.

Your first 3 Charakters, progression & accomplishments are earned by playing the game, not by spending more money.

Buy the game. Own the experience. Play at your own pace.

Magi Hearts are the foundation of your build.
Enemies drop Magi Hearts that carry unique abilities. Bind them to your weapons and turn them into active skills, passive effects, auras, and more.
Magi Hearts can also be combined and evolved into new skills, opening up new possibilities as you experiment with different combinations. Surround yourself with dark magic, rain fire across the battlefield, tear through enemies with blood, summon creatures to fight for you, or come up with something completely your own.
Your weapons, equipment, and Magi Hearts all come together to shape your build. Every run gives you a new set of possibilities.

A WORLD OF FACTIONS

Every faction fights differently.
Battle your way through the Cultists and their dark rituals, face the undead warriors of the Vikings, and hunt down the bloodthirsty Vampires. Each faction has its own enemies, attacks, and tricks to learn.
As you venture further, you'll face stronger enemies and bosses that will put everything you've built to the test.
And these are only the factions you'll meet at the beginning of your journey.

Every run is another chance to go further.

When a run ends, start again. Try a different weapon. Build around a different Heart. Evolve your skills into something new. Take a different path.
There's always another combination to try.

store_data.about_the_game:
Build a temple that sings

SoundStone is a meditative building sandbox where every line becomes both architecture and music. Draw directly onto a living stone plate, then watch walls, raised courtyards, stairs, gateways, and elevated walkways grow from your plan.

Build compact sanctums or sprawling temple precincts. Raise and lower regions, link separate courts with walkable arcades, open routes through gateways, and reshape the same plan as your ideas evolve.

Architecture becomes an instrument

The geometry that shapes the site also shapes its sound. Retune walls, place resonant structures, and discover how proportion, route, pitch, and light turn each construction into a playable composition.

Shape every site

  • Draw walls and close them into raised courtyards.
  • Connect high regions with generated walkways, supports, and gateways.
  • Add entrance stairs and create processional routes through the site.
  • Build vertically and open individual bays as arcades.
  • Carve stepwells and quarry halls when a design calls for depth.
  • Tune structures into scales, consonance, and evolving musical patterns.
  • Choose golden or red sandstone, white marble, weathered granite, Deccan basalt, Hoysala soapstone, or laterite.
  • Change lighting moods without changing your plan.
  • Experiment with undo, redo, save, load, and a guided building tutorial.

SoundStone is being developed in Early Access with an expanding construction sandbox, deeper musical behaviours, and continued visual and usability polish.

store_data.about_the_game:
Somebody is hacking into a network and it's your job to find out who, how, and what they're about to do next.

Root Cause is a solo investigation thriller built around one feeling: the moment a mess of logs and false leads suddenly clicks into a story that makes sense. You're not clearing rooms or managing a base. You're correlating. Building a case out of evidence that doesn't want to cooperate, and staking your reputation on what you think it means.

The hook


You work the night shift, alone, from your apartment. An alert opens. Somewhere in your customer's network an attacker is already moving, and their next step, encrypt something, steal something, jump to another machine, is on a countdown you can't see, but you can sense. Every question you ask costs you time off that countdown. Every wrong guess buys them room to work.

Why it stays interesting


Real intrusions don't hand you a smoking gun. They hand you a process that looks almost normal, an account that logged in via odd methods, a file sitting somewhere it shouldn't be. You've got a few tools and no hand-holding: figure out what each piece of evidence actually means, pin it into the story in the right order, and make the call, contain it, escalate it, or decide it's nothing at all. Sometimes it really is nothing, and turning a quiet night into a crisis is its own kind of stress.

Why it sticks with you


Get the story wrong and it follows you. The threat actor you misjudged shows back up wearing a different name tag.

What it isn't


No combat. No stealth. No twitch reflexes. If you've ever wanted to get a sense of what digital forensics and incident response is all about then jump on in -- minus the pager and the burnout.

You're the only one on shift tonight. Good luck.

store_data.about_the_game:
COLLECT LIFE FROM EARTH'S REAL PAST

Epochlings is a creature collector about building a permanent collection across Earth's natural history.

Travel through 11 ancient eras, discover creatures inspired by organisms that actually lived on our planet, capture them before their time passes, and preserve them beyond extinction.

Build your roster, strengthen your Epochlings, fuse lifeforms separated by hundreds of millions of years and prepare your team for automatic battles across a changing timeline.

JOURNEY THROUGH 11 ERAS OF NATURAL HISTORY

Begin among some of the earliest complex ecosystems of the Cambrian and travel forward through the Ordovician, Silurian, Devonian, Carboniferous, Permian, Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous, Paleogene and Neogene.

Each era has its own environments, creature roster and progression.

Time does not stand still. As you advance through an era, species appear, flourish and disappear. Creatures available during one part of an era may no longer exist later, while new and rarer lifeforms emerge as history moves forward.

Push deeper for new opportunities — or rewind and explore the timeline again.

DISCOVER 99 CREATURES

Build a collection of 99 creatures across 11 eras, including each era's apex boss.

Epochlings are heavily stylized and deliberately cute, but the creatures beneath that style are inspired by organisms from Earth's real natural history.

From strange Cambrian life and ancient sea predators to giant arthropods, early reptiles, dinosaurs and prehistoric mammals, every era introduces a different part of life's history.

Capture creatures before their place in the timeline disappears and preserve them permanently outside the normal flow of time.

Your collection survives even when their species does not.

COLLECT • PRESERVE • FUSE ACROSS TIME

Finding creatures is only the beginning.

Creatures preserved outside the timeline can be developed, upgraded and combined with lifeforms from completely different eras.

Use fusion to create new Epochlings from creatures that evolution kept millions — or even hundreds of millions — of years apart.

Experiment with different creatures, traits and abilities. Develop combinations that fit your strategy and decide which Epochlings deserve a permanent place in your collection.

Your roster becomes increasingly unique as repeated journeys through time give you more creatures and more possibilities to work with.

PREPARE YOUR TEAM. THEN WATCH THE BATTLE UNFOLD.

Combat is built around preparation rather than constant micromanagement.

Choose your Epochlings, develop their strengths, combine complementary abilities and assemble a team suited to the encounter ahead.

Once battle begins, your creatures fight automatically.

A powerful individual creature helps.

A carefully constructed team can matter even more.

FACE AN APEX ENCOUNTER IN EVERY ERA

Every era culminates in its own Era Boss.

Eleven eras mean 11 distinct apex encounters, from ancient ocean predators to some of the most formidable creatures represented in the collection.

Reaching them requires surviving increasingly dangerous stages of their era and preparing a team capable of handling what waits at the end of that timeline.

Defeat the apex of an age and continue your journey through natural history.

REWIND HISTORY. KEEP YOUR COLLECTION.

Eventually, time turns back.

A rewind sends you through history again, but the creatures you preserved outside the normal timeline remain with you.

Your captured Epochlings, their development and the fusions you created become the foundation for your next journey.

Missed a species?

Need another specimen for a fusion?

Want to reach a part of the era that defeated you before?

Go back.

History will repeat itself.

Your collection does not have to.

BUILD A COLLECTION THAT HISTORY NEVER COULD

Epochlings combines:

  • 99 collectible creatures

  • 11 eras of Earth's natural history

  • 11 Era Bosses

  • Cross-era creature fusion

  • Persistent creature progression

  • Preparation-focused automatic battles

  • Changing ecosystems and creature availability

  • Time-loop progression and rewinds

  • A permanent collection preserved beyond extinction

Discover life from Earth's past.

Preserve what time would erase.

Combine creatures evolution kept apart.

Build a collection beyond time.

BUY ONCE. PLAY WITHOUT PRESSURE.

Epochlings is a one-time purchase.

There are no in-game shops, no premium currencies, no pay-to-win mechanics, no pay-to-progress systems and no advertising inside the game.

Your creatures, progression and accomplishments are earned by playing the game — not by spending more money.

Buy the game. Own the experience. Play at your own pace.

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome, adventurer!

Behold, the great kingdom of Reveria, split into three large districts with the island city of Cathar at its center. It's a place of beauty and wonder, where the next adventure is always just around the corner. But it's also a place of conflict and strife, where the law of the strongest reigns supreme.

You find yourself in the town of Hostilium in the outreaches of Reveria’s Western District. It is a lawless place outside the influence of the throne. At least for now... While the nefarious Dragon King tightens his grip around the area, rebellion starts brewing. It is fertile ground for up and coming adventurers like yourself to make their fortune. The nobodies of today can be the heroes of tomorrow.

Grow your legend

Assemble your party and gather your equipment. Set out to brave the Reverian wilderness. Explore ancient crypts, abandoned mines, and dark caves. Encounter gnarly beasts and seasoned fighters.

In Reveria, you start as a lowly, aspiring adventurer. Gradually, you get involved in a conflict that is much bigger than you were anticipating. From helping the local shopkeep with their rat infested basement and beating up the nearby goblin tribe, you eventually find yourself fighting the forces of corruption that have infested the region.

Back to the roots

Reveria is a turn-based RPG, inspired by old school fantasy and Dungeon & Dragons. In fact, it is my attempt to turn a multi-year homebrew D&D campaign into a narrative-driven videogame. I took an artistic license to reinterpret some of the craziness that happens during real-life tabletop sessions, but I hope that Reveria nonetheless still gives you that iconic TTRPG sandbox feeling of semi-cluelessly wandering around the world and stumbling into a wide variety of quests. This is a labor of love and I'm incredibly excited with the world. I hope you like it. Here's to the next adventure!

store_data.about_the_game:
Sticks & Strings is a first-person archery PvP shooter for up to 8 players. Pick a target, draw your bow, and aim carefully. No hitscan and no full-auto. Make every shot count.

Fifteen Game Breaking Changing Powerups

  • Go invisible with Phantom — just watch out for True Sight

  • Leap up high with Cloud Hopper and rain arrows down on your foes

  • Fire three arrows at once with Multi-Nock, or go full artillery with Black Powder's explosive tips

  • Teleport across the map with Soul Shot

  • Keep an eye out for special bows and arrows

  • And more...

Online PvP

Play with up to seven other friends. Host a private match or join a public lobby with "Quick Join." 

No Friends?

Add some bots to your lobby. They can run, jump, fight, and use powerups just like a real player. But be careful, some of them have gotten quite good at shooting. 

Fully Customizable Game Settings

Prefer skill over luck? Hosts can change powerup spawns to "Never" and run it as a pure, no-frills draw-and-shoot duel — no crutches, no gimmicks, just whoever's actually better with a bow. Or grab seven other friends and crank powerups to the max and see who can survive the longest. Enable teams to play a 4v4, a 2v2v2, or maybe a 1v5. It's up to you. 

Three Maps, Two Gamemodes

Fight it out across the Ruins, the Forest, and the Graveyard in Elimination or Deathmatch, with host-configurable win conditions — first to a kill count, last one standing after time runs out, or best of however many rounds you decide.

35 Achievements

Do something cool in game and get a nice achievement on your profile. Try to collect them all!

Play It Your Way

Full key rebinding for every action. Plenty of in-game options. Change your name and your character's color. Public or private lobbies with quick join. No accounts beyond Steam.

store_data.about_the_game:
Live an entire life in the wild.

Wild Legacy is an open-world animal survival game where you grow from a vulnerable young animal into a powerful adult, build a home, raise a family, lead a pack or herd, claim territory, and leave a legacy that lives on after you.

Death is not the end of your journey. If your family or pack survives, you can continue your story through another member, inheriting the world you've helped create.

Become part of a living ecosystem

The wilderness doesn't exist for the player.

Predators hunt.

Prey migrate.

Families grow.

Rival packs expand.

Animals compete for food, water, shelter, and territory while the world continues to evolve around you.

Dynamic weather, changing seasons, day and night, and realistic animal behaviors create new challenges every time you play.

Build a family, not just a character

Life in Wild Legacy is about more than survival.

Find a mate.

Raise offspring.

Build dens and homes.

Lead a pack.

Protect your family.

Expand into new territories.

As your influence grows, you'll establish additional homes across the wilderness, assigning wolves to guard, hunt, scout, or raise the next generation while you continue exploring with your active hunting group.

Every animal plays differently

Every playable species is designed with its own gameplay loop, progression, and behaviors.

The first complete campaign focuses on wolves, while additional playable animals are being expanded into their own fully featured campaigns.

Planned playable animals include:

  • Wolf

  • Fox

  • Bear

  • Raven

  • Deer

  • Moose

  • Rabbit

  • Boar

  • Cougar

  • Tiger

  • Crocodile

  • Raccoon

Each species is designed around its own strengths, survival strategies, homes, family systems, and progression.

Key Features

  • 🐺 Live the complete life of a wild animal

  • 🌲 Explore a large open world filled with dynamic wildlife

  • ❤️ Find a mate and raise a family

  • 🏕️ Build, upgrade, and defend multiple homes

  • 👥 Form packs or herds with intelligent AI companions

  • 🌧️ Survive changing weather, seasons, hunger, thirst, injuries, and fatigue

  • 👣 Hunt, track, sneak, and survive using each species' natural abilities

  • 🗺️ Claim and defend territories against rival groups

  • 📖 Continue your journey through your surviving family after death

  • 📸 Photograph wildlife, discover rare animals, and record your memories

  • 🎮 First-person and third-person gameplay

  • 🤝 Local co-op and player-hosted multiplayer (planned during development)

Leave a Wild Legacy

The world remembers what you build.

Your homes remain.

Your territories remain.

Your family continues.

Your story doesn't end when one animal dies—it continues through the legacy you've left behind.

store_data.about_the_game:
You draw the part by hand. The machine cuts exactly what you drew. That's the problem.

Tolerance is a 1–4 player co-op comedy about running a same-day CNC machine shop like a short-order kitchen. Orders pour in, the clock never stops, and every premium job ends the same way: someone has to trace the part by hand — and the machine will faithfully cut every wobble, hiccup, and panic-jerk in your line. A steady hand earns a PERFECT stamp and up to +50% pay. A shaky one earns a lopsided bracket and three friends asking who did this. Ship it anyway.

There are no assigned roles and no private wallets - one till, one bank, one shift outcome. Whoever grabs the board becomes the dispatcher. Whoever's hauling stock is the runner. Whoever picks up the calipers just volunteered for QC, and whoever's holding the wrench when the intruder walks in is now the bouncer. Meanwhile the shop itself fights back: fires spread, machines jam and break down, the breaker trips under load, and that part someone threw across the floor? It can knock you flat.

Grow the shop from a humble pine woodshop up through oak and steel to titanium - each material a genuinely different beast, not a reskin. There's no level select and no act structure: your BILLS are the difficulty. Every machine you buy raises the daily nut and the ceiling together, one-cut jobs deepen into multi-op chains, and the campaign ends when you land THE AEROSPACE CONTRACT - one perfect titanium part, the tightest tolerance in the game. Bank your crew's cash into seven permanent shop upgrades, work your way up the contract phone, and unlock endless mode when you land it. Prefer to suffer alone? Solo isn't a stripped-down afterthought - it's the tuned baseline. The shop is exactly as unreasonable with one machinist as with four.

FEATURES

  • Wonky in, wonky out - hand-trace every premium part and the machine cuts your literal line, flaws and all. Nail the trace for a PERFECT stamp and up to +50% pay.

  • 1–4 player online co-op, everything shared - one till, one bank, one shift result. When the part's wrong, everyone made it wrong.

  • Roles you claim, never assigned - dispatcher, stock runner, machinist, inspector… plus bouncer, electrician, and mechanic when the shift goes sideways.

  • A shop that fights back - spreading fires, jammed machines, tripped breakers, breakdowns to repair, thrown parts that floor you, and a saboteur who responds well to a wrench.

  • A real campaign - climb the pine → oak → steel → titanium ladder at your own pace: your bills set the bar, big-name contracts are the milestones, and landing the aerospace contract is the ending.

  • Permanent progression - 7 buyable shop upgrades that change how the floor actually runs.

  • Endless mode - beat the finale, then see how long the shop survives you.

  • Genuinely playable solo - the one-machinist shop is the tuned baseline, not a compromise.

Precision optional.

store_data.about_the_game:
DODGEBALL DISORDER

Dodgeball Disorder is a chaotic online multiplayer dodgeball game where throwing the ball is only half the battle. Dodge, catch, aim, and send your opponents flying with physics-based hits, ridiculous ragdoll reactions and face expressions.

Step into a school gym where a normal dodgeball match has somehow turned into complete disorder. Play with or against other players, survive the chaos, and try to leave with at least a small amount of dignity.

THROW. DODGE. SURVIVE.

Every hit matters. Time your throws, avoid incoming balls and use movement to stay in the fight. Hard hits can send players tumbling across the gym with physics-driven reactions.

DIFFERENT WAYS TO CAUSE PROBLEMS

Matches can completely change depending on the game mode.

Classic
Score hits for your team. When the match ends, the team with the most hit points wins.

Last Team Standing
Getting hit has consequences. Keep your team alive and make sure the other one runs out of players first.

Free-For-All
No teams. No friends. Everybody is a perfectly acceptable target.

Prison Dodge
Getting hit sends you out of the main play area. Use the recovery zones around enemy territory to fight your way back into the match.

PHYSICS-BASED CHAOS

Players react differently depending on how they are hit. Dodgeballs, movement and ragdoll physics turn simple throws into unpredictable moments.

Sometimes you make the perfect throw.

Sometimes your teammate takes it directly to the face.

Both count as gameplay.

A GYM WITH QUESTIONABLE SUPERVISION

The school gym is filled with props, signs, ridiculous posters and small environmental jokes. Look around between throws — although staring at the walls during a dodgeball match is generally considered a bad survival strategy.

ONLINE MULTIPLAYER

Jump into online matches, compete against other players and communicate using in-game text and voice chat.

Dodgeball Disorder is easy to understand: get the ball, throw the ball, and preferably don't be the person the ball hits.

store_data.about_the_game:
Match words. Clear the board. Learn as you play.

FlashWords: Wordfall is a language-learning word game built around a simple falling-block mechanic.

Words fall from above in one language while their translations wait below. Guide each falling word to its correct match to clear the blocks and keep the board under control.

The idea is simple, but as more words enter the mix, recognizing the right translation quickly becomes part memory, part reflex, and part puzzle.

Learn through play

Instead of studying vocabulary from a static list, FlashWords: Wordfall puts words into an active game loop. You repeatedly see, recognize, and match vocabulary while playing.

Earn points as you play and use them to unlock new word packs, expanding the vocabulary that can appear in your games.

Features

  • Falling-word gameplay — Match words with their translations before the board fills up.

  • Learn vocabulary while playing — Repeated exposure helps reinforce words naturally through gameplay.

  • Multiple languages — Play with different language combinations and build your vocabulary across supported languages.

  • Unlockable word packs — Earn points and open new sets of vocabulary as you progress.

  • A growing challenge — More vocabulary means more possible matches to recognize and remember.

  • Simple to understand — Familiar falling-block ideas combined with word matching make it easy to pick up and play.

Whether you want to practice a language you are already learning or simply enjoy word games, FlashWords: Wordfallturns vocabulary practice into a game of recognition, timing, and matching.

store_data.about_the_game:
The city of Dis was sealed years ago. The plague stayed in. So did you. Climb out of the quarantine zone one district at a time — through a horde that has stopped wandering and started listening.

EVERY LOUD PLAY RINGS THE DINNER BELL

Scrap is power: bombs, overcharges, upgrades. But every scavenge and every big swing raises the Noise meter — and at 4, 7, and 10 something new claws out of the dark. Fight quiet and bank the stealth bonus, or embrace the bell and build a deck that feeds on what answers it.

YOUR ENEMIES HAVE DECKS TOO

Combat is deck versus deck. Enemies queue their moves from real card decks — peek at what's coming, steal their best card, jam junk into their queue, or force a discard. They'll do it right back: stalkers read your loud plays, wardens stamp junk into YOUR deck.

THE INFECTION IS A CLOCK AND A FUEL TANK

Corrupted cards are the strongest in the game — and they cost infection. Ride the fever bands for power, spend it on plague skills, purge it at rest sites. Hit 100 and you Turn. The run ends.

OVERCHARGE — SPEND SCRAP, STAY SILENT

Any card with an overcharge line can be played hot for extra scrap: more damage, more draw, a clean burn with no infection. The quiet build's answer to the demolition build's bombs.

A CITY THAT REACTS

Systemic crises interrupt fights when your dials run hot — low HP, high noise, a fattening scrap purse all trigger mid-combat wagers with real teeth. Events are commitments, not vending machines: promises kept and broken follow you up the tower.

A STORY TOLD IN INK

Motion-comic chapters with full narration unlock as you climb: the horde that remembers your name, the Checkpoint that counts climbers, and what's really waiting on the surface. Every unlock is content — new cards and relics recovered issue by issue.

  • 60+ hand-inked cards across four archetypes (Bruiser, Scavenger, Plague, Tactician)

  • Enemy decks you can read, rob, and wreck

  • Noise, Scrap, Infection, Deck Warfare — four economies, one climb

  • Systemic crises and commitment events that react to how you play

  • Comic story chapters + unlock track between runs

  • Districts with run-warping conditions, elites, and a Checkpoint to beat

Combat is deck versus deck. Enemies queue their moves from real card decks — peek at what's coming, steal their best card, jam junk into their queue, or force a discard. They'll do it right back: stalkers read your loud plays, wardens stamp junk into YOUR deck.

THE INFECTION IS A CLOCK AND A FUEL TANK

Corrupted cards are the strongest in the game — and they cost infection. Ride the fever bands for power, spend it on plague skills, purge it at rest sites. Hit 100 and you Turn. The run ends.

OVERCHARGE — SPEND SCRAP, STAY SILENT

Any card with an overcharge line can be played hot for extra scrap: more damage, more draw, a clean burn with no infection. The quiet build's answer to the demolition build's bombs.

A CITY THAT REACTS

Systemic crises interrupt fights when your dials run hot — low HP, high noise, a fattening scrap purse all trigger mid-combat wagers with real teeth. Events are commitments, not vending machines: promises kept and broken follow you up the tower.

A STORY TOLD IN INK

Motion-comic chapters with full narration unlock as you climb: the horde that remembers your name, the Checkpoint that counts climbers, and what's really waiting on the surface. Every unlock is content — new cards and relics recovered issue by issue.

  • 60+ hand-inked cards across four archetypes (Bruiser, Scavenger, Plague, Tactician)

  • Enemy decks you can read, rob, and wreck

  • Noise, Scrap, Infection, Deck Warfare — four economies, one climb

  • Systemic crises and commitment events that react to how you play

  • Comic story chapters + unlock track between runs

  • Districts with run-warping conditions, elites, and a Checkpoint to beat
store_data.short_description: A comic-ink roguelike deckbuilder where noise is a resource. Scavenge loud and the horde answers in waves — or fight quiet and stay poor. Outplay enemies that run decks of their own: peek, steal, and sabotage their next move while an infection ticks toward turning you.

store_data.about_the_game:
Prigod Idle is an idle auto-battler RPG. You choose a hero, equip their gear and abilities, and send them out to fight. They handle the combat, but the build is yours.

Ifyou are stopped by a boss, look at what it does and change your setup. Swap a weapon, socket different gems, try another pet or choose a different tech tree branch. Sometimes one good change is enough to turn a loss into a win.

New heroes and items are not only there to make your stats bigger. They give you more builds to try and more ways to handle your next adventure.

BUILD YOUR HERO

  • 37 heroes, and every one of them plays differently

  • Gear with sockets, enchants and set-defining relic abilities

  • 68 relics, 42 pets and 23 legendary Fables to collect

  • Four tech trees and six prestige branches to shape long-term power

WHEN YOU GET STUCK, CHANGE THE BUILD

  • A long campaign with special bosses that have their own mechanics. If you can't defeat an enemy, try something new!

  • Dungeons, Peril tiers, Event enemies, a recurring World Boss and the PvP Colosseum, each with different fights to prepare for

  • A route map every run: pick your path, your fights and your rewards

EARN YOUR BUILD IN FIGHTS AND MINIGAMES

  • 10 events with exclusive heroes and gear

  • 22 minigames: dig for gems, brew potions, drop Plinko chips, and many more

  • Build out your homestead, get pets, and fill the Prigod Dex

NO INGAME STORE. OFFLINE PROGRESSION. PLAY IT FULLY IDLE IF YOU WANT

  • Full offline progress, including offline dungeon clears

  • Gems are earned by playing. No ads, no energy walls, no microtransactions

YOUR DESKTOP COMPANION

  • Runs on the side while you do other things

  • Prestige unlocks new modules for automation

  • A compact portrait window that fits beside anything, or extra panels for more infos

Try the free demo! Your demo progress carries into the full game.

store_data.about_the_game:
HELL IS NEON COLORED

Descend through a procedurally built underworld drawn in five colours and lit entirely by the things trying to kill you. Every floor is generated the moment you enter it. Every weapon is something you assembled. Every sound you hear the score, the explosions, the sword — is synthesized note by note while you play. There are no audio files in this game.

BUILD THE WEAPON, NOT THE LOADOUT

A weapon here is three decisions.

A powering decides when it may fire and what that costs — an energy pool, a heat sink that locks out when you push it, a magazine, a flywheel you wind up by standing still, a tithe paid in your own health, or a gun that only fires on the beat of the music.

A weapon decides what comes out.

A rider decides what happens next.

Over three hundred authored combinations, and every pairing is balanced by construction: the powerings differ in how they fail, never in how much they pay. Play the one that matches how you move.

FIVE BANDS OF HELL

MORTAL is the base game. Clear it and descend to the HELL difficulties. Difficulty here buys new threats rather than longer health bars: mobs start carrying your own weapons against you, minibosses appear inside ordinary waves, and bosses arrive as formations of linked bodies — a bar that sweeps, a serpent that follows its own head, a pair bound together until the last phase splits them.

A SOUND CHIP, NOT A SOUNDTRACK

Ten chiptune tracks and ninety-nine sound effects run on one emulated eight-voice sound chip, generated sample by sample as you play. The score reads the run: it speeds up when you grab a power-up, sinks into its own low end when you are losing, and audibly thins out when a firefight steals its voices — because on real hardware, it would have.

Unlock the Audio Studio and it is handed to you. Pick the track, drive the tempo, stack a second layer in sync with the first, drag a ten-band EQ, watch a spectrum analyser, and record the result to a .wav file you can open anywhere.

FEATURES

  • Three modes — Quick Play (a single descent), Endless (climb until it kills you), and the Gauntlet (a run of levels with a boss at the end)

  • Five character slots with an eight-track progress bench

  • 223 (95 Steam tied) achievements paying out score, mode unlocks and eighteen cosmetics — trails, a hue-rotated arsenal, and nine followers including three pocket bosses

  • Seven enemy affixes and themed packs, each taught once and then remembered forever

  • Hunts — a mimic disguised as a wall, a quarry that runs the fight toward you, an assassination target behind a ring of guards

  • Full controller support, and every control on both keyboard and pad is rebindable

  • Deep video and audio options — bloom, dynamic lighting, wall shadows, screen shake and hit stop each with their own switch and strength. A full EQ panel to tweak sound your way while you play.

  • Customizations galore. Pets, trials, costumes, weapon recolors, and others abound.

PHOTOSENSITIVITY

This game uses bright, high-contrast neon visuals, bloom and screen flashes. A photosensitivity warning is shown on every launch, and the effects that cause it — bloom, camera shake, motion effects — can each be turned down or off from the options menu.

store_data.about_the_game:
Bring the arcade home!

TRACE is a colorful, explosive rhythm game built to capture the energy of the arcade on your PC. The arcade may be hours away, but your PC is a feet away. No giant arcade cabinet required.

Follow the rhythm! All 360° of it!

Notes aren't confined to a few lanes, the entire circle is your playfield. Follow the music around the ring as notes come from all directions, with different note types constantly changing what you need to do. Fly your mouse around the circle to hit traces, fight your muscle memory with dodge notes, and follow directional notes to spin, spin, spin! 

Pick a song. Pick a difficulty and GO!

TRACE is built around the arcade rhythm game loop: hop straight in with all the songs unlocked, choose a chart, chase a better accuracy, and climb the global rankings!  

Note: This game was ported from Roblox

TRACE contains lots of flashing lights and colors. Discretion advised for those vulnerable to such.

store_data.about_the_game:
Dahlonega, Georgia. 1829.

The gold is down there. The ground will not tell you where.

Swing a pick into Georgia red clay and find out what you struck. Sometimes it is nothing, forty times in a row. Sometimes the shovel turns over something that stops you where you stand.

Go deeper for the good stuff. Deeper is also where the ground starts fighting back.

Follow a hunch sideways and you might hit a run of ore that goes on and on. Or you might chase it half a day and get eleven dollars for your trouble. That is prospecting. You do not find out until you dig.

Haul it up, sell it before the assayer shuts, and start buying the town, one business at a time. Ruby runs the saloon, and she is always where the party is at during the night.  But don't stay up too late, you have to hit the mine early!

The Fun

  • Dig, strike, and find out what you struck

  • Every swing is a guess you paid for

  • Chase a seam across the hill and hope it holds

  • Go deep for the good stuff, and see what is waiting down there

  • Blow a hole with some dynamite!  But look out, who knows how long it's been sitting. 

Own every business in town, or die of exhaustion trying
