store_data.about_the_game:
Rail Capital is a real-time railway strategy and economic management game inspired by the Robber-Barons, shared networks, shifting ownership and decisions of 18xx board games.

Beginning in 1820 with little more than some cash and an ambitious plan, you'll found a railway, issue shares and raise the money needed to lay track, build trains and win important auctions of train prototypes, blueprints and company bonuses.

After laying track and designing services to decide exactly what each carriage should load, carry and unload you'll keep an eye on public and privately securable contracts, invest in prospective industries and place warehouses to gather the cargo.

Every railway exists within a wider economy. Passengers expect useful connections, industries buy raw materials, factories transform cargo into valuable products, and ports provide access to distant markets. Prices respond to supply and demand, while warehouses, contracts and specialist freight routes create opportunities for careful logistics planning.

Your company’s money is not your own. Revenue can be retained for expansion or paid as dividends to shareholders. Buy and sell shares, defend your presidency, challenge rival boards and pursue mergers. Prototype locomotives, blueprints and freight consignments also pass through live railway auctions.

Compete against distinct AI personalities or other players in real-time multiplayer games. Explore seeded sandbox maps, handcrafted scenarios, guided campaigns, daily challenges and the Iron Road rogue-lite mode, where your company advantages carry across a branching railway journey.

Watch the network come alive as trains climb hills, enter tunnels, cross rivers and steam between growing towns. Build an efficient railway, a powerful company and, ultimately, your own Rail Capital!

store_data.about_the_game:
In the ruined wasteland, survive first — then grow stronger.

The dead roam and supplies are scarce. Starting from a single safe house, you must carve out a life in the apocalypse.

Run Your Safe House
Talk to the shopkeeper and quest NPCs, trade weapons and supplies, and take on contracts. Build and expand your base until the safe house becomes a true home in the wasteland. Every return restores your strength and prepares you for the next sortie.

Sortie, Scavenge, Extract
Explore procedurally generated cities and villages, scavenge loot, and fight mutated enemies and bosses. Manage hunger, thirst and stamina — and when your backpack fills up, every choice matters. Loot only truly belongs to you once you reach the extraction point.

Build Your Way
Deep gear stats and an ability tree with freely allocated attribute points; skills can even auto-cast per slot. Tank the horde in heavy armor or melt it with raw firepower — the choice is yours.

Purge Mode
A wave-based dungeon mode separate from the main story: pick a stage, survive escalating waves, earn Purge Points, and unlock harder challenges.

Auto-Combat Idle Grinding
Want loot without the micro? Turn on auto-combat — your character fights, moves, picks up gear and repairs automatically. Take manual control whenever you like.

A Complete Survival Loop
Quest tracking, world map and minimap markers, three save slots with character profiles, and a full journey from tutorial to boss fights.

store_data.about_the_game:
[h2]An entire club in your hands[/h2]

You take over a team and you answer for it. Not just for Sunday's line-up: for the wage that fits the budget, for the kid you bring up from the academy, for the offer that lands for your best player the night before the derby.

The board hired you with an expectation — a place in the table, a run in the cup, the books in the black. Meet it and you keep the job. Fall short and there are consequences, and they arrive before the season is over.

[h2]Sunday, 4pm. Kick-off.[/h2]

The match unfolds and you follow it move by move. Speed it up when things are calm; pause when they tighten.

Losing on 60 minutes? Change the mentality, take off a holding midfielder, throw on another striker. But you only get five changes across three stoppages — the real rule — and burning them early leaves you with no answer when someone pulls up injured.

The manager in the other dugout is doing the same. Behind, he pushes forward; ahead, he shuts up shop. The game does not sit and wait for you.

[h2]A settled side plays better[/h2]

Naming the same eleven builds understanding, and that is worth points on the pitch. Rotate too much and it breaks down. But the calendar shows no mercy: cup on Thursday, league on Sunday — and a tired starter gives you less than a fresh substitute.

Every player has morale, form and a specific role. A centre-back shoved out to full-back plays worse — the engine knows it, even when the team sheet looks right on paper.

[h2]The transfer market is a negotiation, not a button[/h2]

You make the offer. The other club takes days to reply, and may come back asking for more. Meanwhile another side joins the race for the same player — and whoever offers the better project, not just the bigger fee, gets him.

Once the clubs agree, you still have to convince the player. Wages, signing fee, length of contract. He can turn you down and hold out for a move that matches his standing.

When the cash does not stretch, there are ways round it:

  • Pay in instalments — take the signing now and pay over time, with interest. Come up short on the due date and the debt grows, and the board hears about it.

  • Trigger the release clause— the club cannot refuse. But it costs, and the player still has to want the move.

  • Loan— split the wages, negotiate an option to buy, and bar him from playing against you.

  • Give up a sell-on percentage — cheaper today, and you hand over part of tomorrow's profit.

The books close at the end of the month

Sponsorship, TV money, gate receipts and the club shop on one side. Wages, upkeep and the instalments you took on against them. Every first of the month the balance lands — and it is the measure of what you can do in the market.

A small club does not buy a star. But it can raise one.

The academy takes years, and it is yours

The kids at the training ground develop slowly. Promote too early and you hand a raw teenager to the first team; hold him back too long and you waste his best years. And at 21, anyone not promoted walks away for nothing.

You get a limited number of promotions each season. Choose well.

27 leagues. A world that plays on without you.

Brazil, England, Spain, Italy, Germany, France, Portugal, Argentina and more — 690 clubs and 15,000 players contesting their own championships, domestic cups and continental tournaments.

Clubs sign from each other, go up, go down and change managers while you look after your own. Want a lighter world? Choose which leagues the game simulates.

Your way

A full database editor ships with the game: names, squads, attributes, stadiums and images. What you build can be exported to a file and shared with other players.

Full interface in Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), English and Spanish.

store_data.about_the_game:
Every bubble holds a reward—and a new threat.

Bubblecore: Survivors is an endless single-player tower defense roguelite where you decide when the next attack begins.

A mysterious world of resource-filled bubbles surrounds the Citadel. Pop one to instantly claim wood, stone, food, ether, or another valuable reward. But beware: every bubble also releases a group of monsters that immediately advances on your Citadel.

Expand carefully and reinforce your defenses one step at a time, or pop several bubbles at once to accelerate your growth at the risk of unleashing an overwhelming horde. The farther you travel from the center, the greater the rewards—and the deadlier the enemies trapped inside.

Build Your Defenses

store_data.about_the_game:
Take to the skies...

...and enjoy the peaceful life of a seaplane delivery pilot

Explore a world of scattered islands, take on delivery jobs, and build your own little business from the cockpit of your cargo seaplane. Fly at your own pace, discover new destinations, and enjoy the freedom of traveling between islands while keeping your plane and cargo in good shape.

Master Your Seaplane

Take control of your cargo seaplane and handle its systems as you fly. Use the landing gear, flaps, lights, and other controls to prepare for takeoff, enjoy smooth flights, and make careful landings at your destinations.

Manage Jobs and Money

Choose from available delivery jobs and decide which ones to take. Earn money by completing deliveries and use your earnings to keep your plane running, improve its parts, and prepare for new adventures.

Handle Cargo With Care

Every package is worth money, so treat your cargo carefully. Load and drag packages without damaging them, transport them safely, and deliver them in good condition. Damaged cargo means less money in your pocket.

Maintain and Upgrade Your Plane

Your seaplane is your most important tool. Pay for repairs when things wear down and invest your earnings into upgrading different parts of the aircraft. Keep improving your plane and make each flight a little better.

Explore the Islands

Fly between many beautiful islands and discover new places along the way. Take on deliveries to different destinations, find your favorite routes, and enjoy the feeling of being out on the open water and in the sky.

Take a Break

Flying and making deliveries can be a busy day, so remember to look after yourself along the way. Grab something to eat or drink, relax between jobs, and enjoy the slower side of life as a pilot.

store_data.about_the_game:
Test your aim and puzzle-solving skills across a huge variety of challenging levels! Shoot colorful balls from the edges of the playing field and match them with balls of the same color to clear the board.

But as you progress, the puzzles become more complex. Explosives, magnets, rockets, traps, moving obstacles, bombs, locks, barriers and other special elements will constantly change the way you approach each level. Use their unique properties to create chain reactions, open blocked paths and find the best way to clear the field.

Game Features

  • Colorful ball-matching gameplay — shoot balls from the sides of the field and destroy matching colors.

  • Dozens of unique mechanics and obstacles — each new element introduces a different challenge.

  • Strategic puzzles — carefully choose the direction and timing of every shot.

  • Powerful special elements — use explosions, rockets, magnets, bombs and other objects to clear large areas.

  • Moving and changing targets — some objects change their position or color, requiring quick thinking and precise shots.

  • Varied objectives — clear the entire field, activate special objects, collect items, form words and overcome unique challenges.

  • Competition mode — challenge the computer on identical levels. You and your opponent receive different sets of balls, and the first player to completely clear their field wins.

Every level is a new puzzle. Plan your shots, use the environment to your advantage and clear the field with as few moves as possible!

store_data.about_the_game:
Once In Sakartvelo is an anthology of short, first-person horror games, each set in a real corner of Georgia.

Episode One: Out of Service

You missed the last train.

It is past midnight in Nadzaladevi, on Tsotne Dadiani Street. The walk to the Metro should take five minutes, but someone has been following you at a steady distance ever since you left your friend’s apartment building.

This is not a story about stopping a killer or solving a mystery. It is about one ordinary night on a real street, and what it took to survive the walk home.

Key Features

  • Real Location: Set on an actual, named street in Tbilisi - not a fictional town.

  • No Combat: Survival depends on staying calm, keeping quiet, and executing high-stakes quick-time events under pressure.

  • Phone-Based Storytelling: Conversations, texts, and auto-replies drive the entire narrative. No voice acting.

  • Microphone Noise Detection: The killer is listening. Keep your real-world breathing and room noise down during intense encounters, or risk giving away your position (includes an optional toggle to turn off).

  • Multiple Outcomes: One true ending, alongside several ways for the night to go wrong.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Galaxy is at War

War has consumed the Galaxy.  Systems burn, old alliances collapse, and mighty fleets battle for control of what remains of the once proud Human Galactic Empire.

Those capable of commanding these vast armies are known as the Warcaste, a caste of brilliant military leaders who will stop at nothing to secure victory.

Choose your faction, build your fleet, take command and join the Warcaste.

More than a Card Game

In Warcaste, to claim victory you must have more than just strong cards.

Battlefield positioning matters.

Deploy your units, maneuver your fleet across contested zones, and defend your territories as you break your enemies lines to destroy their worlds.

Every turn forces you to decide where to commit your forces, when to attack, and when you need to hold your ground.

Choose Your Doctrine

Every deck begins with a Doctrine.

Your Military Doctrine defines your strategy, giving each deck its own identity. 

With 12 Doctrines in the first set, you can build aggressive fleets to overwhelm the opponent, control the battlefield through carefully timed abilities, create powerful combo turns, or out power your opponent through superior defense and resources. 

Build Your Fleet

Build your decks from a collection of more than 200 cards from set 1.

Unlock new cards as you progress through battles in Story Mode.  Experiment with different combinations, discover powerful synergies and build the fleet you want to command.  Unlock all 4 unique factions from set 1.

Story Mode

Enter the war-torn galaxy of Warcaste through the dedicated Story Mode.

Fight across a campaign map, complete unique missions, and unlock new cards and decks as the story unfolds.

Experience the conflict that drives the Warcaste galaxy.  The factions of Warcaste fight against an approaching eldritch threat as their civilization collapses into total war.  Will you survive?

Solo Play

Test your decks against computer controlled opponents.  Practice new strategies and experiment with deck builds as you prepare for PvP.

Online PvP

Put your skills to the test against other commanders in 1v1 online PvP.

Prove you are truly Warcaste as you battle against other players, master your faction and claim victory.

No In Game Purchases

No microtransactions.  Warcaste is designed to reward playing the game, not having a bigger wallet.

Playing Warcaste earns you in-game credits that can be used to open packs containing full-art and foil versions of cards.  These rewards are cosmetic only.

The cards you need to play are available from day one.

Take Command

Build Your Fleet

Control the Battlefield

Destroy Your Enemy

Become Warcaste

store_data.about_the_game:
Ever wish traffic was the whole game?

Ever played Cities: Skylines and wished you could spend less time building a city and more time figuring out how to make its roads actually work?

Highways & Co. is a traffic simulator game about designing road networks, solving traffic problems, and finding out whether your solution holds up under pressure.

Build the road. Open it to traffic. Find the problem. Fix it. Repeat.

Build the road you want

Create smooth highway ramps and functional slip roads. Build an expensive bridge over the railway, or settle for a level crossing. Upgrade a 2 lane road to a 3 lane road, or build a 3+2 lane asymmetrical road.

Build roundabouts or traffic lights. Manage lane connections and priority. Use different road types and elevations to create the network you need.

There is rarely just one way to solve a problem.

Then see if it works

When you're ready, open the network and let the traffic flow.

Every vehicle has a route, and its own driving behavior. Traffic merges, changes lanes, queues, and reacts to the network you've built.

Every destination has a required traffic threshold. Keep the network moving well enough to meet them all.
When something goes wrong, figure out why. Add capacity. Change a connection. Reroute traffic. Rebuild the junction.

KEY FEATURES


  • Ten road types, from country lanes and streets to four lane motorways
  • Set lane counts independently for each direction
  • Seven height levels, including cuttings, tunnels and viaducts
  • Signals, give way junctions, roundabouts and channelized slip roads
  • Precise lane connections and priority controls
  • Widen roads, convert them to one way, and change their class without rebuilding them
  • Railways and level crossings
  • A hand crafted campaign of challenging sites
  • Deterministic traffic simulation

Build your own pinball table

Every run starts from scratch. Between stages you buy bumpers and drag them onto the table wherever you want them. Where they sit decides how the ball travels, how your combos chain, and how long you survive.

Combine and discover

Two bumpers make a new one. A coin bumper and a timer bumper become something neither of them was. You only find out what a recipe produces by building it once — and from then on it stays unlocked for good, across every future run.

Five worlds, five bosses

Each world has its own table, its own backdrop and its own boss who steals your lives and your bumpers. Beat them to unlock new balls.

Six balls, six rule sets

Every ball plays differently and bends different rules. Only the first one is yours from the start — the rest you take from the bosses.

Perks

Small items with a lasting effect on your current run. Some work quietly in the background, others save you exactly once. What you find is up to the shop.

Endless mode and leaderboards

Stage 50 is not the end. Keep going and measure yourself against everyone else on the leaderboard — each ball has its own ranking, and your best run is listed there with its time and score.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Moonlit Observatory is breaking apart — and every wave is worse than the last.

SLICKWAVE is a hand-painted top-down action roguelite built around focused 15-minute runs. Guide the Moonbound Mage through 14 escalating waves, shape a new spell build on the fly, and defeat the guardian waiting at the heart of the Observatory.

SURVIVE A SCREEN-FILLING SPELLSTORM

Enemies attack from every direction while your arsenal grows from a few careful shots into a storm of missiles, meteors, auras, wards, lances, traps, and explosive arcane effects. Keep moving, read dangerous telegraphs, and turn the entire arena into your weapon.

  • 14 escalating waves with rising enemy density and new threats.
  • Fast 15-minute runs built for immediate action and one-more-run momentum.
  • Automatic or manual aiming — let spells find targets or take precise control while moving.
  • A final guardian battle that tests the build you created.

BUILD YOUR OWN ARCANE ENGINE

Choose from nine active spells and carry up to six at once. Every level forces a real decision: raw damage, crowd control, defense, mobility, or the missing piece of a larger synergy.

  • Choose one of two behavior-changing branches at Level III.
  • Pair Level V spells with the right relics to unlock powerful evolutions.
  • Carry up to three relics that reshape the strengths of your build.
  • Spend Fate Shards to reroll rewards when a run refuses to cooperate.

LEARN THE OBSERVATORY. BREAK THE NEXT RUN.

Earn Essence in battle and invest it in permanent upgrades between attempts. Study discovered skills, relics, and enemies in the Moonlit Codex, review your run history, and return with a better plan.

A HAND-PAINTED MOONLIT WORLD

Between runs, return to the Observatory hub: prepare for the next descent, inspect your discoveries, and choose the next goal for your growing archive.

ONE MAGE. FOURTEEN WAVES. COUNTLESS BUILDS.

Every run begins small. Every great build ends as a tidal wave.

Warm water, cold nights, and hearts that melt.

Burned out by city life, 24-year-old Kazuki quits his job and travels to a snowy mountain village. Waiting for him is Yumegiri-sō, the traditional hot spring inn left behind by his late grandfather. Once filled with laughter and guests, the inn now has empty rooms, a leaking roof, and only one winter season left before its debts come due.

A luxurious resort across the valley is ready to buy the property. Kazuki could sell everything and walk away—or stay and fight alongside the four adult femboys who already call Yumegiri-sō home.

  • Yuki: A shy but gifted chef who expresses affection through every meal.

  • Haru: An energetic mechanic who keeps both the boiler and everyone’s spirits running.

  • Rin: A composed accountant who has been carrying the inn’s debts alone.

  • Sora: An enigmatic permanent guest who knows more about Kazuki’s grandfather than they are willing to reveal.

Help with the inn’s daily life throughout the winter, take part in light minigames ranging from cooking to repairs, and shape your relationships through dialogue choices. Grow closer to one of the residents and uncover their fears, dreams, and reasons for holding on to Yumegiri-sō.

Each route offers a distinct emotional story, adult intimacy, and multiple endings determined by your choices. If romance is not what you are looking for, you can also pursue a warm, platonic finale about finding a family—and a place to belong.

Features

  • Four romance routes featuring adult femboy/futanari characters

  • Good, normal, and bittersweet parting endings

  • An additional platonic found-family finale

  • Dialogue choices that shape your relationships

  • Minigames based on cooking, repairs, accounting, and winter chores

  • A cozy, snow-covered Japanese hot spring setting

  • A character-driven story about romance, healing, and belonging

store_data.about_the_game:
Garden Pressure — is a cozy incremental game about an automatic farm that stops being cozy very fast. Buy seeds, pay for water, collect vegetables and try to survive a season. You just need to… grow everything all at once!

Seeds are finding free spots by themselves, plants are slowly growing, and you just need to keep track of water and harvest on time. But every crop requires a special approach: cheap vegetables make profit fast, while expensive ones freeze money for a long time, especially if you collect them too soon or let them dry up.

Expand you shop’s selection and collect your own set of crops for a season. Strawberries, pumpkins, sunflowers, mushrooms, flowers, exotic fruits — each crop has its price, water consumption and special upgrade. Grow all six crops at the same time to reach Full variety and lead the farm to a successful finale.

As you level up, choose upgrades that can fully change the farm:

  • Make plants grow faster and receive more money and experience

  • Unlock new crops and collect profitable combinations

  • Reduce water consumption and weed spawning

  • Find rare upgrades with unusual effects

  • Turn some crops into lucky crops, water carriers and golden harvest

You can’t operate such a farm manually. Unlock mechanisms, buy them in the shop and gradually create your own automation system. A collecting robot will take care of mature crops, a bee will make plants grow faster, a drone will work the soil, automatic watering will save your tank and a basket will let you collect half of your harvest in one click.

However, the farm is not going to make your life easier. Crows steal your harvest. Mole steals plants, hedgehog checks a whole row, spider wraps vegetables in a cocoon and strong wind replants crops without your permission. Government letters demand urgent deliveries, impose restrictions and suddenly remind you about taxes.

Sometimes a Pandora crop can appear on a seedbed. You can’t collect it automatically and the result of collecting it manually is unpredictable: free water, golden plants and explosion of seeds or drought, cocoons, mechanism failure and real chaos. It’s up to you whether you risk it or let it occupy one unit.

Every season becomes a new run. Meet the global conditions, unlock meta nodes and change the rules for future runs. Turn off weeds spawning, unlock new mechanisms, strengthen Full variety and remove the upgrade limits, but remember — the more upgrades you take with you, the longer you need to survive.

Can you build a perfect automatic farm or will you be left with no water, money or hope, while a crow flies away with your last pumpkin?

store_data.about_the_game:
No piloting skills required.

Build a robot.

Work out how it should fight.

Then hand it over to the AI.

“SIGNOS” is a fully automatic battle simulation in which the robots you design fight each other.

The player never takes control during a battle.

Should it move?

Should it search for the enemy?

Should it attack?

How should it judge the situation?

It all comes down to the logic you built.

How will the tactics you imagined actually play out on a real battlefield?

Seeing that through — that is what a SIGNOS battle is.

Build Your Machine

Combine all kinds of parts on the 18cm-tall hobby robot “SIGNOS” to create a machine that is yours alone.

Head, chest, arm and leg parts each have their own performance.

Durability, weight, EN consumption, processing power, firing arc.

A heavy build loaded with high-firepower weapons.

A machine that leans on its shield to grind out a win.

A machine that prioritizes mobility to control the distance to its opponent.

The parts you choose change the way your machine fights.

And then — what logic will you build into it?

Combine machine design with tactical design and complete a SIGNOS that is entirely your own.

Build Tactics with Thought Tiles

Place Thought Tiles such as “Move,” “Search,” “Attack” and “Judge,” then connect the nodes to build your behavior logic.

For example:

Search for the enemy

↓

store_data.about_the_game:
The Fallen Kingdom is a fantasy tactical strategy game featuring brutal small-scale combat, deep unit progression, and diverse heroes and magic. Use simple controls to deploy troops, hold key positions, and wear down undead forces with powerful ranged firepower. Lead an expedition to defeat the evil undead tyrant—carve your way through ravaged lands with tactics and magic.

Command heroes and units in coordinated combat to withstand wave after wave of undead enemies. Every decision matters—do you unleash a skill to clear a crowd of enemies, or save it for the stronger waves ahead? Do you send shield-bearers to the front line, or keep archers in the back for sustained damage? Every map is different, and you must constantly adjust your tactics to face new challenges.

Hunt the Undead Tyrant: You will lead an expeditionary force deep into the cursed lands ravaged by the undead, marching against the evil undead tyrant. Along the way, you will face different enemy types and terrains—each battle consumes your troops and resources. Whether you can ultimately break into the tyrant's throne room depends on every choice you make along the journey.

Brutal Combat: The battles in The Fallen Kingdom are brutal. Fallen soldiers are gone forever—no matter how long you have trained them, one wrong decision can wipe them out. Attrition is a constant threat throughout the campaign. You must constantly weigh progress against losses. There is no second chance—every battle depletes your expeditionary force.

Heroes & Magic: Each hero possesses unique skills and spells that can turn the tide at a critical moment. If a hero falls in battle, they will return in the next encounter—they do not permanently die. But losing their support in a fight can still cost you dearly in that battle.

Grid-Based Movement: The battlefield is divided into a grid of positions. Simply click and drag to deploy your troops anywhere on the field. Melee units hold the front line, while ranged units provide fire from the back. The movement system is intuitive and straightforward, allowing you to focus on tactical decisions rather than complex controls.

Troop Progression: Your army is not static. Through combat, you earn gold and population resources, which you can use to expand your forces, replenish losses, and upgrade elite units into stronger variants. But even a well-upgraded force can suffer heavy losses from a single misstep. Growth and risk always go hand in hand.

store_data.about_the_game:
THERE'S A BOMB STRAPPED TO YOUR CHEST AND IT'S GOING TO EXPLODE WHEN YOU RUN OUT OF AMMO!

Don't let the cute characters deceive you, RIGGED2EXPLODE is a brutally hard tactical shooter where you need to manually check your ammo count, lean around corners, and make every bullet count.

TACTICAL FPS GAMEPLAY

Combat is fast and deadly, so you can't just run around shooting from the hip.

  • You must check your ammo manually, so make sure you count your shots during a shootout.

  • Take your time scouting a level, a hasty turn around an unchecked corner can get you killed.

  • Stop and listen. Noticing sounds from enemies, security cameras, and turrets will save your life.

EVERY BULLET COUNTS

Carefully decide how to use each bullet. Not only can they kill enemies, bullets are used to get upgrades and pickups necessary to overcome the challenges ahead. 

USE THE ENVIRONMENT

You're going to need tactical advantages to stay alive.

  • Shoot out lights to hide in the dark.

  • Create smoke clouds to gain cover.

  • Trick turrets into shooting enemies in the line of fire.

  • Lead enemies into mines to save your bullets.

store_data.about_the_game:
THE ARENA IS ALIVE

Vector Surge is a fast, uncompromising twin-stick arena shooter set inside a reactive signal field. Move, aim, dash and detonate your way through geometric swarms while the grid bends, pulses and fractures around every collision.

Almost everything you see is constructed live. Ships, enemies, projectiles, formations, effects, grid reactions and combat patterns are drawn from procedural vector geometry rather than conventional sprite sheets. Encounters remix enemy families, elites, hazards and formations on the fly. In Universe mode, procedural objectives, loot, mutations, routes and escalating sector conditions turn that same arena into a long-form expedition that is different every time you enter it.

There are no safe corners. Your multiplier is always fading. The best score is always one riskier kill away.

SIX WAYS TO ENTER THE STORM

Every score protocol rewrites the rules of the arena.

  • Overclock: Three minutes. Unlimited lives. Build momentum quickly and turn every second into score.

  • Safehouse: One life, no bombs and shrinking sanctuaries. Your weapons only function inside the safe zone.

  • Endurance: Limited lives and bombs, no time limit and an arena that keeps getting worse.

  • Gatecrash: No weapons. Cross signal gates to destroy nearby enemies and survive through movement alone.

  • Crosscurrent: Break apart advancing horizontal and vertical rocket formations before the field closes around you.

  • Circuit 20: A twenty-stage formation campaign with strict timers, three lives and a tactical salvage window between encounters.

Each protocol has its own online leaderboard. Chase the next pilot displayed on your HUD, overtake the archive and keep pushing until the field declares: YOU LEAD.

BUILD A SHIP THAT REMEMBERS

Universe mode turns the arcade arena into a persistent campaign.

Choose a hull, enter a generated expedition and fight through sectors of increasingly hostile space. Earn credits and XP, install permanent enhancements, expand your module bay and develop a different build for every ship in your fleet. Each hull tracks its own mastery, doctrines, enhancements, prestige and online record.

Level gains pause the action and offer three temporary augments. Stack fire cadence, critical damage, piercing, chain lightning, dash attacks, salvage bonuses, defensive reserves and more. Then evolve compatible modules into run-defining weapons such as the Arc Caster, Event Horizon Lance, Crystal Storm, Gravity Bomb or autonomous Storm Array.

Your run does not follow a fixed level list. Timed objectives emerge from the field, capital victories open a branching Storm Atlas and every route changes what comes next. Choose combat, elites, salvage, repairs, anomalies, resource exchanges or another capital signal. On rare sectors, a trader may intercept the route carrying equipment normally found only inside crates, but reaching them is never guaranteed.

FACE CAPITAL SIGNALS

Six capital families wait inside the storm, each with distinct movement, attacks and battlefield logic:

  • Dreadnova

  • Prism Warden

  • Rift Carrier

  • Grid Architect

  • Salvage Devourer

  • Null Engine

Later sectors and higher Storm Tiers can mutate these bosses with accelerated, armoured, mirrored, brood, volatile, Repulsar and multiplier-siphoning properties. Familiar threats become dangerous new combinations, forcing you to read the encounter instead of memorising a single pattern.

And then there is the Grid Breaker.

When its signal arrives, the music dies. Alarms seize the arena. The camera pulls back. The grid itself shatters before the boss enters the field.

CHOOSE HOW THE STORM ENDS

Universe difficulty is not a basic health slider. Storm Tiers alter the entire pressure model: enemy speed, hull strength, formation size, spawn cadence, elite density, projectile velocity, boss movement and attack frequency all intensify together.

Tier 10 is designed as an endgame challenge. Beyond it waits [b]Gates of Hell[/b], an unreasonable terminal tier with no gentle opening and no promise of fairness.

Four campaigns remix the expedition further, while rotating contracts, mastery ranks, hull doctrines and prestige provide reasons to rebuild your fleet and return with a new plan.


PROCEDURAL BY DESIGN

Vector Surge is built around systems rather than pre-rendered spectacle.

  • Runtime-drawn vector ships, enemies, projectiles and effects

  • A connected hexagonal grid that reacts to combat, music and boss intrusions

  • Procedurally assembled waves, formations, objectives and sector pressure

  • Branching route choices and changing resource trades

  • Generated loot rolls, augment drafts and evolving weapon combinations

  • Boss families that combine with escalating mutations

  • Persistent hull progression across otherwise unpredictable expeditions

The result is an arena that remains visually coherent but refuses to remain static. Every run speaks the same geometric language; no two runs arrange it in quite the same way.

BUILT FOR IMMEDIATE CONTROL

  • Responsive keyboard and mouse or twin-stick controller play

  • Fast dash with a brief invulnerability window

  • Limited screen-clearing bombs

  • Close-range bonuses, multi-kill rewards and a decaying score multiplier

  • Distinct enemy silhouettes and readable attack telegraphs under heavy pressure

  • Persistent local progression with separate per-mode and per-hull online leaderboards

  • Adjustable screen shake, flashes, particles, post-processing, vibration and audio levels

  • Optional local MP3 and Ogg Vorbis music support. Your files remain on your machine.

  • Windows and Linux support

LEAVE A SIGNAL NOBODY CAN OVERTAKE[

Play for three minutes or disappear into a Universe expedition. Chase a perfect Circuit. Reforge a mastered hull. Push one Storm Tier too far. Find a build the procedural field was never supposed to allow.

The storm will keep changing.

Your score is the only proof you were there.

store_data.about_the_game:
Bring Every Line Back Into Place

Stillflow is a minimalist connection puzzle game built around rotating lines. Each level is made from straight lines, curves, T-junctions, crosses, and ring terminals. Rotate each piece, study the direction of its ports, and make neighboring lines meet until the entire network is complete.

When the final port connects, the finished pattern turns a soft teal. A gentle light flows along the completed lines, bringing each puzzle to a quiet close.

Rotate, Observe, Connect

The rules are simple, but every puzzle rewards careful observation:

  • Left-click to rotate a piece clockwise; right-click to rotate it counterclockwise.

  • Ports on neighboring pieces must match exactly.

  • Ring terminals are valid endpoints for a line.

  • Straight lines, curves, T-junctions, and crosses cannot leave exposed ports.

  • The level is complete when every line turns teal.

100 Handcrafted Puzzles

Stillflow contains 100 fixed puzzles. The journey begins with compact 3×3 layouts and gradually expands to 7×5 boards. As you progress, the networks become richer and more intricate, asking you to trace crossing paths, understand each connection, and restore a complete line pattern.

Every level has a definite solution. There are no randomly generated answers and no steps that depend on luck—only observation, experimentation, and the freedom to solve each puzzle at your own pace.

Nothing but Quiet Focus

Stillflow has no timer and no failure penalty. A dark backdrop, restrained minimalist lines, gentle ambient music, and subtle interaction sounds come together to create a calm and focused puzzle experience.

Master volume, background music, and sound effects can be adjusted separately. You can also switch between fullscreen mode and several 16:9 window resolutions. The interface supports 30 languages, allowing more players to enjoy this quiet journey of connection.

Features

  • 100 handcrafted line-connection puzzles with a gradual difficulty curve

  • Straight lines, curves, T-junctions, crosses, and ring terminals

  • Minimalist dark visuals with a gentle flowing-light completion effect

  • No timer or failure penalty—solve every puzzle at your own pace

  • Separate controls for master volume, background music, and sound effects

  • Fullscreen mode and multiple 16:9 window resolutions

store_data.about_the_game:
The yard is under attack. The cats were napping there.

Cute Kitty WAR is an arena survival game about the fiercest neighborhood watch ever assembled: 48 cats, each with their own rules, defending a suburban backyard against waves of pests that are somehow both adorable and completely out of line.

A run is 12 waves. Between waves, spend your hard-earned materials in a shop that tells you the truth — every card shows the real math, every number is honest. Build toward a bruiser, a gunner, a gardener with a structure empire, a luck goblin — 48 cats and 18 weapon classes bend the rules in 48 different directions.

Then the sky opens. Storms roll in as real weather — rain carpets, wind, lightning, flooding ponds — and the yard fights on underneath it.

And if you win? The fence holds a secret. An earned endless mode where the yard's folklore comes marching — weakest to strongest, at a pace YOU set. How deep you go is a dedication, not a difficulty slider. We won't spoil what walks at the end of that procession.

Features

  • 48 playable cats — real rule-changing kits, their own starting gear, and a journey to complete

  • 97 weapons across 18 classes — every one with honest, readable math on its card

  • 171 items — engines, pacts, pets, and cures that stack into ridiculous builds

  • 143+ creatures including 10 authored bosses with fixed, learnable kits — fights you master, not fights that cheat

  • 1–4 player couch co-op — deliberately friendlier than solo; bring the family, the shop splits into strips

  • Danger 0–5 — higher danger buys harder decisions, not just bigger numbers; danger 5 fields the twin bosses

  • A living storm system — five escalating weather levels that change how the yard reads and plays

  • An earned endless — the procession past the fence, paced by your own dedication dial

  • Kittain's Log — a full codex: creature discovery, trophy wall, the yard ladder

  • Every telegraph is fair — attacks are forecast where they land; if you got hit, you could have moved

store_data.about_the_game:
The frontier is vast and unclaimed. Strip ore, chart trade routes, and raise colonies on distant worlds, then decide who you're building them for. The Federation, the Rebels, and the Syndicate hold ground across six connected star systems, and every move tips the balance between them. Push far enough into hostile territory and you'll find the Dominion, massing an invasion fleet at the edge of known space.

Build an economy that runs without you. Mining outputs work the belts around the clock, stripping ore whether or not you're in the system, or logged in at all. Set up convoy routes that carry ore back to your colonies on their own schedule, turning it into credits while you're away.

Grow colonies from bare rock into sprawling outposts. Every world starts with a landing pad and a handful of empty plots. Fill them with habitat domes, hydroponics farms, research centers, drone bays, and more, as a outputs grow into colonies worth defending.

Repel the Dominion when they come for your ship. A boarding lance clamps onto the hull and cuts through, and the fight plays out across your own decks in real time. Raiders push in from the airlock and the engine bay and make for the bridge while fire spreads room to room behind them.

Prestige through five distinct starships. You start in the wayfarer freighter, a hauler with nowhere far to go yet. Prestige and trade it in for a hull built to push further: the excavator for mining the belts, the survey vessel for researching the solar systems, the gunship for hostile encounters, and the adventurer for the far side of known space. 

Take the fight to the Dominion. Everything builds toward Ashgate, where the Dominion has massed a capital fleet no single power can break alone. Earn enough standing with both the Federation and the Rebels and you can call the Ashgate Star Invasion: a full-scale assault with allied warships at your side against the Dominion.

Get out and walk. Leave the pilot's seat and your ship becomes a place to explore: walk its decks, pass the crew at their stations, take a game of checkers in the recreation hall. Down on the surface, walk your colony among the domes and roads, or check a buggy out to range farther.

Feature list

  • Asteroid mining, trading, and mission-running across six connected star systems, with star gates to fast-travel between them once discovered.

  • Colonies with an expanding plot grid and a wide range of structure types, from habitat domes and research centers to a recreation hall and a motor pool.

  • Automated drones and idle convoy routes that earn resources while you're away, including offline.

  • Three-faction diplomacy (Federation, Rebels, Syndicate) with a fourth, hostile power (the Dominion) watching from the edge of the map.

  • Real-time space combat against pirates, faction rivals, and Dominion warships.

  • Dominion boarding raids: defend your ship deck-by-deck in real-time firefights with standing orders for your trained crew.

  • Walkabout exploration on foot through your ship and colony, plus planet surface exploration on foot or by motor pool buggy.

  • A checkers mini-game in the recreation hall and ambient crew chatter.

  • A 5-ship Prestige progression line with 40 permanent upgrades that carry across runs.

  • A scripted, multi-faction endgame battle: the Ashgate Star Invasion.

  • 100 Steam achievements across 9 categories, each ranked by rarity.

Ship silhouettes were inspired by Stephen Challener's "Space Ship Building Bits, Vol. 1" and BizmasterStudios' "SpaceShip Building Kit" no original artwork is included.

store_data.about_the_game:
The desktop is spiraling out of control.

Desktop Monsters is a compact 2D tower defense game set on a stylized computer desktop. Build digital defenses, manage limited resources, and protect the Desktop Node against increasingly dangerous waves of bugs, pop-ups, cache fragments, malware slimes, and malicious processes.

BUILD YOUR DIGITAL DEFENSE

Choose from three towers with distinct roles:

• Cursor Turret — Delivers steady, reliable damage.

• Firewall Node — Slows enemies and helps control crowded routes.

• Antivirus Beam — A costly late-game defense that chains its attack between multiple targets.

Position each tower carefully, balance immediate protection against long-term upgrades, and adapt your strategy before the next wave arrives.

CHOOSE YOUR ROUTE

• Standard Route — A focused 10-wave campaign built around the core tower defense loop.

• Extended Route — A longer 15-wave campaign with more demanding late-game enemy combinations.

• Endless / Overtime — Continue defending after the regular route ends and see how long your setup can survive.

Additional challenge configurations, including Budget Lock, Cache Surge, and Archive Pressure, change the rules and force you to rethink familiar strategies.

FACE THE TROJAN CORE

The Trojan Core is protected by active Shield Processes. Destroy the supporting processes first, then concentrate your defenses on the exposed core before it overwhelms the Desktop Node.

DEFEND ACROSS DIFFERENT DESKTOPS

Battle across five desktop layouts: Desktop Classic, Laptop Workspace, Ultrawide Desk, Compact Monitor, and Large Desktop. Each layout changes route spacing, tower coverage, and the way pressure builds around your defenses.

Build efficiently, respond to each threat, and keep the Desktop Node online.

store_data.about_the_game:
Your map is full, your fleet is limited, and every delivery is racing against the same clock. CargoTempo is a route-planning management game about turning delivery chaos into a plan that works. Assign orders to specialized vehicles, arrange every stop, and balance deadlines, capacity and operating costs. Then start the day and see whether your plan holds.

  • Which vehicle takes the urgent express delivery?

  • Which orders belong on the same route?

  • Is another vehicle worth the additional cost?

  • A motorcycle is fast but cannot carry large orders. A van stays flexible. A truck carries far more, but it is slower and more expensive to operate.

  • Choose what must leave today, what can wait, and which risk you cannot afford to ignore.

Split orders across your fleet, reorder stops and transfer deliveries between routes. Compare expected arrival times, capacity, revenue and operating costs before you commit. A short route can still fail if the wrong vehicle carries the wrong order, or if a critical stop comes too late. Every change affects the result. Turn an overloaded set of deliveries into a clean network of routes that makes the best possible use of your fleet.

When planning is complete, send out the fleet. Your vehicles leave the depot and execute their routes in parallel. Watch deadlines close in, deliveries complete and every tradeoff play out across the city. A strong plan becomes a smooth delivery network. One poor decision can put the entire day at risk.

Successful days earn operating capital.

Invest it in specialized vehicles and company policies that reshape your strategy. Build around speed, carrying capacity, express deliveries, lower operating costs or safer deadlines. Every purchase opens new possibilities and creates new tradeoffs for the days ahead. Expand carefully. A larger fleet can solve more problems, but only if you use it efficiently.

Each run takes place in a procedurally generated city with different roads, districts and delivery destinations. Learn the network, spot efficient combinations and adapt your strategy as the pressure rises. There is no perfect route for every situation. Build the best plan for the city, orders and fleet in front of you.

FEATURES

  • Plan several delivery routes at the same time

  • Assign and transfer orders between motorcycles, vans and trucks

  • Balance deadlines, capacity, arrival times, revenue and operating costs

  • Watch your entire fleet execute its routes in parallel

  • Handle standard, express, large, priority and critical deliveries

  • Expand your fleet and choose company policies during each run

  • Play compact, multi-day runs in procedurally generated cities with new route problems

you can enjoy a different combination every time.

■ From Human to Something Else

Am I changing my gear, or am I changing my body?

The line between the two grows increasingly blurred the deeper I dive.

store_data.about_the_game:
One shift. One screen. The windows overlap - and whatever you cannot see starts lying to you.

You are on probation at Meridian, Internal Resolution, Tier 1. Extended Coverage, 18:00 to 02:00, formally voluntary. You have an Employee ID instead of a name, a queue that refills faster than you empty it, and SYNERGY OS 4.2 - an internal tool that has been patched for years and is proud of its version number. Somewhere in this building, people are signing work orders they could not have signed. Nobody has asked you to look into it. You are simply the last person the paperwork passes through.

THE WORK

Every ticket is a small case, and the answer is never in the ticket. It is in the contradiction between two other windows: a work order signed by someone who was on approved leave, a badge that opened a floor it was never cleared for, a letter whose signature block does not match the last eight from the same author. Pull both records into evidence, then approve, deny, escalate, or hold. Saying yes is easy. Saying no has to be justified with a reason code, picked from twenty-two that are almost identical on purpose. A refusal backed by two records that contradict each other is worth three times a merely correct answer. Nobody in this company will ever call that detective work. There is a form for it, so it is a form.

THE RULE

A window covered by more than 30% stops syncing. It does not warn you. It does not grey out. It keeps showing the data it had the last time you looked, with complete confidence, and the only tell is a timestamp in a footer you were not watching. The desk is 1920x1048. Everything you need does not fit on it, and that is not an oversight, that is the game. Stale is not only a number that moved: a letter you have already read can be extended while its window is covered, and the Inbox goes on filing it as read until it can see the record again. Sooner or later you will refuse the wrong person on evidence that was true twenty minutes ago. It will be filed under your badge, and it will stay filed.

YOUR DESK IS A BUILD

Sixteen programs, a memory budget, and a limited number of slots. Between shifts you decide what you will not see tonight. The AI that highlights contradictions costs 39% of your memory and is wrong about one hint in six - and a wrong hint looks exactly like a right one, because a hint that admitted its own doubt would not be a product. The legacy search always tells the truth and takes eight seconds to do it. What is not installed does not exist: not "harder to find", not "hidden behind a check". Every working build is blind in a different direction, and none of them clears a shift at 100%. You choose your blind spot before the evening starts, and then you work inside it for eight hours.

WHAT THIS GAME DOES NOT HAVE

No jump scares. No monsters. No chases. No characters and no dialogue - the only faces here are badge photographs inside a personnel record, and a record can be out of date. No fake Windows dialogs. No explanation at the end. Nothing here is ever loud. The horror is the distance between what the system says and what the data shows, and you are the one who has to close it. Nothing will lunge at you out of the dark. Something will simply, quietly, turn out to be true - and it will still be true tomorrow, in writing, with a procedure number on it.

THE COMPANY WOULD PREFER A DIFFERENT ANSWER

Once an evening, from the third shift on, the records say deny and a standing notice from another department asks you to approve - politely, with a procedure number and no signature. Your two scores move in opposite directions: one measures whether you did as you were told, the other whether you were right. Obedience is cheaper. Nothing on the screen ever tells you which column is the one that counts, and you find that out only when somebody reads both of them back to you. Some evenings the building wants something on the spot: a mandatory procedural check, numbered and timed, lands in the middle of the desk and covers whatever was under it. You can drag it somewhere cheaper. You cannot close it, and the clock does not stop while you work it out.

MERIDIAN IS DELIGHTED WITH YOUR PROGRESS

Nothing here is ever threatening and nothing is ever explained. The notifications congratulate you. "Great news! Your Compliance Score is trending up" slides in seconds after you deny access to someone who is dead in one database and still badging onto the third floor in another. The wellness program grants a fourth pause on shift 3, extends it on shift 5, takes one back on shift 7, and by shift 9 it is called Peak Season Protocol and there are none. People leave the personnel database and their tickets keep arriving, on time and correctly formatted. Somewhere around the seventh evening the workstation stops behaving like a tool, and the tone of the notifications does not change at all.

THE MAIL IS ADDRESSED TO THE ASSIGNMENT

Correspondence in this building is filed against a post, not a person, so from the second evening a routing mailbox starts writing to yours. Every letter is ordinary, and every header can be checked against tonight's roster, the clock, or a revision counter - and one field an evening does not survive the check. A distribution list carrying a badge that is not in the building. A read receipt stamped eight minutes before delivery. An enclosure taken at an hour that has not happened yet. You answer with a form code and never with words: acknowledge, return, forward, hold, or no reply due. Attach a record if you like; nothing requires it and nothing thanks you for it. On the last evening a reply arrives in a closed thread, to a disposition filed under your name that you did not file - and the shift report counts it among yours.

NINE SHIFTS, AND ONE A DAY AFTER THAT

156 tickets across nine evenings, about three hours. Exactly one new kind of contradiction or one new interface violation per shift - never two. Failing a shift does not restart the campaign: you keep your progress and start the next evening from a worse place, which is also how it works out here. Daily Shift picks one evening from the date, so it is the same evening for everyone playing today, and gives you a single line to compare with.

ACCESSIBILITY

Unlimited pauses, a slower clock, quiet failures, reduced motion, three colour vision palettes with a non-colour state marker on every window, a brightness and a phosphor-glow slider, toasts that can stop counting as occlusion, full key rebinding, and four separate volume sliders. None of it changes the simulation: a recorded shift played with accessibility on matches the same shift played without it.

DISPLAY

The desk is one fixed screen of 1920x1080 and the game never reflows it. It scales the finished frame to your monitor as a whole, so a pixel stays square; on 1920x1080 and 3840x2160 it is exact. A display smaller than 1920x1080 will letterbox it.
store_data.detailed_description:
One shift. One screen. The windows overlap - and whatever you cannot see starts lying to you.

You are on probation at Meridian, Internal Resolution, Tier 1. Extended Coverage, 18:00 to 02:00, formally voluntary. You have an Employee ID instead of a name, a queue that refills faster than you empty it, and SYNERGY OS 4.2 - an internal tool that has been patched for years and is proud of its version number. Somewhere in this building, people are signing work orders they could not have signed. Nobody has asked you to look into it. You are simply the last person the paperwork passes through.

THE WORK

Every ticket is a small case, and the answer is never in the ticket. It is in the contradiction between two other windows: a work order signed by someone who was on approved leave, a badge that opened a floor it was never cleared for, a letter whose signature block does not match the last eight from the same author. Pull both records into evidence, then approve, deny, escalate, or hold. Saying yes is easy. Saying no has to be justified with a reason code, picked from twenty-two that are almost identical on purpose. A refusal backed by two records that contradict each other is worth three times a merely correct answer. Nobody in this company will ever call that detective work. There is a form for it, so it is a form.

THE RULE

A window covered by more than 30% stops syncing. It does not warn you. It does not grey out. It keeps showing the data it had the last time you looked, with complete confidence, and the only tell is a timestamp in a footer you were not watching. The desk is 1920x1048. Everything you need does not fit on it, and that is not an oversight, that is the game. Stale is not only a number that moved: a letter you have already read can be extended while its window is covered, and the Inbox goes on filing it as read until it can see the record again. Sooner or later you will refuse the wrong person on evidence that was true twenty minutes ago. It will be filed under your badge, and it will stay filed.

YOUR DESK IS A BUILD

Sixteen programs, a memory budget, and a limited number of slots. Between shifts you decide what you will not see tonight. The AI that highlights contradictions costs 39% of your memory and is wrong about one hint in six - and a wrong hint looks exactly like a right one, because a hint that admitted its own doubt would not be a product. The legacy search always tells the truth and takes eight seconds to do it. What is not installed does not exist: not "harder to find", not "hidden behind a check". Every working build is blind in a different direction, and none of them clears a shift at 100%. You choose your blind spot before the evening starts, and then you work inside it for eight hours.

WHAT THIS GAME DOES NOT HAVE

No jump scares. No monsters. No chases. No characters and no dialogue - the only faces here are badge photographs inside a personnel record, and a record can be out of date. No fake Windows dialogs. No explanation at the end. Nothing here is ever loud. The horror is the distance between what the system says and what the data shows, and you are the one who has to close it. Nothing will lunge at you out of the dark. Something will simply, quietly, turn out to be true - and it will still be true tomorrow, in writing, with a procedure number on it.

THE COMPANY WOULD PREFER A DIFFERENT ANSWER

Once an evening, from the third shift on, the records say deny and a standing notice from another department asks you to approve - politely, with a procedure number and no signature. Your two scores move in opposite directions: one measures whether you did as you were told, the other whether you were right. Obedience is cheaper. Nothing on the screen ever tells you which column is the one that counts, and you find that out only when somebody reads both of them back to you. Some evenings the building wants something on the spot: a mandatory procedural check, numbered and timed, lands in the middle of the desk and covers whatever was under it. You can drag it somewhere cheaper. You cannot close it, and the clock does not stop while you work it out.

MERIDIAN IS DELIGHTED WITH YOUR PROGRESS

Nothing here is ever threatening and nothing is ever explained. The notifications congratulate you. "Great news! Your Compliance Score is trending up" slides in seconds after you deny access to someone who is dead in one database and still badging onto the third floor in another. The wellness program grants a fourth pause on shift 3, extends it on shift 5, takes one back on shift 7, and by shift 9 it is called Peak Season Protocol and there are none. People leave the personnel database and their tickets keep arriving, on time and correctly formatted. Somewhere around the seventh evening the workstation stops behaving like a tool, and the tone of the notifications does not change at all.

THE MAIL IS ADDRESSED TO THE ASSIGNMENT

Correspondence in this building is filed against a post, not a person, so from the second evening a routing mailbox starts writing to yours. Every letter is ordinary, and every header can be checked against tonight's roster, the clock, or a revision counter - and one field an evening does not survive the check. A distribution list carrying a badge that is not in the building. A read receipt stamped eight minutes before delivery. An enclosure taken at an hour that has not happened yet. You answer with a form code and never with words: acknowledge, return, forward, hold, or no reply due. Attach a record if you like; nothing requires it and nothing thanks you for it. On the last evening a reply arrives in a closed thread, to a disposition filed under your name that you did not file - and the shift report counts it among yours.

NINE SHIFTS, AND ONE A DAY AFTER THAT

156 tickets across nine evenings, about three hours. Exactly one new kind of contradiction or one new interface violation per shift - never two. Failing a shift does not restart the campaign: you keep your progress and start the next evening from a worse place, which is also how it works out here. Daily Shift picks one evening from the date, so it is the same evening for everyone playing today, and gives you a single line to compare with.

ACCESSIBILITY

Unlimited pauses, a slower clock, quiet failures, reduced motion, three colour vision palettes with a non-colour state marker on every window, a brightness and a phosphor-glow slider, toasts that can stop counting as occlusion, full key rebinding, and four separate volume sliders. None of it changes the simulation: a recorded shift played with accessibility on matches the same shift played without it.

DISPLAY

The desk is one fixed screen of 1920x1080 and the game never reflows it. It scales the finished frame to your monitor as a whole, so a pixel stays square; on 1920x1080 and 3840x2160 it is exact. A display smaller than 1920x1080 will letterbox it.

store_data.about_the_game:
Horde Up Ahead is a tower defense roguelite about holding your ground against increasingly massive zombie hordes.

You are trapped in a central tower with nowhere to run. Take aim and fight back with your own weapon, then build automated turrets around the tower to turn the battlefield into a wall of fire.

Place AR, Shotgun, Sniper, and M249 turrets, choose where they face, and build a defense capable of handling ever-growing swarms. Spend the Gold you earn during a run to upgrade your turrets and increase their firepower as the pressure rises.

But every run is only part of the battle.

Use permanent resources between runs to unlock and improve upgrades in the Merchant, strengthen your defenses, and prepare for larger hordes. Progress further, grow stronger, and push the numbers higher.

DEFEND THE TOWER

The tower is your last line of defense. Zombies can approach from different directions, forcing you to build around the threats you face.

FIGHT BACK YOURSELF

Your turrets are not your only weapons. Aim and shoot zombies manually when your defenses need extra help.

BUILD YOUR FIREPOWER

Deploy different turret types with their own strengths, ranges, fire rates, and roles. Position them carefully and let them automatically tear into the horde.

UPGRADE DURING THE RUN

Collect Gold from fallen enemies and spend it on turret upgrades while the battle is still going.

GROW STRONGER BETWEEN RUNS

Invest permanent resources in the Merchant and build long-term progression across multiple upgrade branches.

FACE BIGGER AND BIGGER HORDES

What begins as a manageable attack can grow into thousands of zombies pressing toward the tower at once.

Build. Upgrade. Shoot. Survive.

There is a Horde Up Ahead.

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to a magical medieval city where running an alchemy shop is never as simple as it sounds!



Step into the role of an inexperienced orc alchemist and build your own potion business in a world full of magic, colorful characters, unexpected situations, and adult adventures. Take orders from customers, explore the city, meet its inhabitants, and uncover their personal stories as your little shop grows.



Master the art of potion making by interacting directly with your ingredients. Crush, heat, mix, and combine components while carefully following recipes to create powerful and unusual brews. Earn money from your customers, discover new ingredients, unlock recipes, and improve your alchemical skills as you progress.



Along the way, you'll meet a memorable cast of characters, each with their own personalities, desires, and stories. Your choices and actions can influence relationships and lead to unexpected situations, while adult encounters become part of your journey through this strange and seductive magical city.



Can you become a master alchemist, keep your shop running, and discover what secrets are hiding behind your potions?

Game features

🧪 Interactive Potion Crafting

Create potions through hands-on alchemy. Crush ingredients, heat mixtures, combine components, and carefully follow recipes to achieve the desired results.

🏪 Run Your Own Alchemy Shop

Take customer orders, earn money, discover new ingredients, unlock recipes, and develop your shop as you progress from an inexperienced brewer to a skilled alchemist.

💋 Adult Story & Character Encounters

Meet a colorful cast of characters with their own personalities, desires, and personal stories. Follow their journeys through memorable encounters and plenty of playful adult situations.

🔮 Choices & Consequences

Your actions can change relationships and influence how stories unfold. Experiment with different solutions and discover unexpected consequences along the way.

🧬 Progression & Rare Ingredients

Expand your alchemical knowledge by unlocking new recipes, ingredients, and brewing techniques. Discover unique essences and use them to create increasingly powerful potions.

store_data.about_the_game:
The deeper you go, the less you can afford to be there

STRATA is an arcade descent through rock that is destroyed cell by cell. You pilot a drilling capsule from a dome on the surface, and everything below the first metre is procedurally generated geology: dirt, clay, stone, shale, granite, basalt, obsidian, ironstone. Each layer is harder than the last, and your drill head either cuts it or it does not.

Depth is the score. Depth is also the bill.

One resource, two jobs

Drilling makes heat. Firing your gun makes heat. It is the same bar. That is the whole game in one sentence: "cut ten more metres" and "survive the next wave" are the same number, split two ways. Waves come for the dome whether you are there or not, and the dome does not defend itself well. Every time you choose to go one seam deeper, you are choosing what the surface loses.

The rock remembers

The world is not a backdrop with a tunnel drawn through it. Every cell you cut stays cut. The shaft you dug on your third run is still your shaft — the mine is a record of your decisions, written into the map. And it fights back. Cave-ins bury the way home. Gas pockets telegraph themselves, then blow a room out of the wall. Water holds you. Lava flows downhill through the tunnels you opened for it. Welded cells refuse the drill you are carrying. Something is following you in the dark, and it is not the thing attacking the dome.

Light is information

Your headlamp narrows as you descend. Ore glows through stone. At depth you do not navigate by looking at the rock — you navigate by looking at what shines through it. Nothing here is an effect for the sake of one; the lighting is how you read the level.

What you keep

A run lasts two or three minutes. What survives it is credits, and credits buy a permanent rig: hull, fuel, cooling, cargo, and five drill heads that open five classes of rock. The full tree runs to fifty thousand credits, and the bottom of the world does not open until you have paid for it. On top of that: run contracts that pay only if you surface, dome specialisations that change what the run is for, relics, fossils, a depth log, and a core at the bottom that is not the end of the game but the start of the second half of it.

Built without a single asset file

There is no art in this game. No sprites, no fonts, no audio files, nothing on disk but code. The font, the sky, the planets, the nebulae, the capsule, every sound — all of it is generated at startup, every time you launch. The download is a few megabytes and the whole thing is one person's source tree.

Features

  • Fully destructible procedural geology, eight rock classes deep

  • Heat is shared between mining and defence — the run is one long trade

  • A dome that is attacked while you are away, and that you have to come back for

  • Persistent progression: five equipment lines, five drill heads

  • Run contracts, dome specialisations, relics, fossils, a depth log

  • Ten achievements — from your first delivered ore to the third core sample

  • Hazards that telegraph before they kill: cave-ins, gas, water, lava, seismics

  • Save and resume a descent mid-run

  • A tutorial that is a mode, not a wall of tooltips

  • Two languages: English and Russian

store_data.about_the_game:
A Horror Puzzle Experience

Ashworth is a story-driven horror puzzle game where exploration, puzzle solving, and survival go hand in hand.

Explore a forgotten place buried beneath the earth and uncover the story hidden within its halls. Solve puzzles, search for clues, and slowly piece together what happened here but be careful. The deeper you go, the more the place begins to reveal things that were never meant to be found.

Uncover the Story

The story isn't given to you all at once.

Discover letters, hidden details, solve puzzles. Each discovery adds another piece to the mystery, gradually revealing what is Ashworth and why you were brought there.

Solve. Explore. Survive.

The place is filled with puzzles designed to challenge your observation and understanding of the environment. Some answers may be right in front of you. Others require you to connect pieces of information you've discovered along the way.

But solving puzzles isn't always safe.

Something else is moving through the place.

When you're being hunted, there may be no way to fight back. You'll have to run, hide, escape, and use the environment around you to survive.

Your Choices Are Simple

Explore the unknown.

Find what is the place?

Uncover the truth.

And as the story unfolds, you may finally understand why someone waited years for Kristina to arrive.

Welcome to Ashworth.

store_data.about_the_game:
Spin. Build. Reincarnate.

ManiWheel is an idle incremental game about combining letters and accumulating Virtue and Mercy.

A mani wheel is a sacred object used in Tibetan Buddhism. Spinning it is said to grant the same virtue as reciting scripture. In this game, you will place various letters on your mani wheel and link together the effects they activate as it spins, gradually building your own engine for generating Virtue.

Combine Letters and Build Your Own Mani Wheel

Letters have a wide variety of effects. Some generate Virtue, some accelerate the wheel, some strengthen adjacent letters, and others generate new letters.

Even a small effect can produce dramatically different results depending on its position, activation order, and connections with the letters above, below, left, and right. Acquire new letters, experiment with their placement, and discover increasingly powerful interactions.

Gather Souls and Combine Front and Back Effects

As you progress, you will unlock Souls that drift around the mani wheel, as well as Letter Fusion, which allows a single letter to carry two separate effects.

Souls produce nothing on their own, but when combined with the right letters, they can generate Virtue, Mercy, or even new letters. Fuse high-rarity letters to create more complex, dual-sided letters whose front and back effects activate in sequence.

Once you have accumulated Mercy, open the Reincarnation Map. Gradually unlock adjacent spaces to permanently strengthen your mani wheel or preserve letters to carry into your next reincarnation.

Each reincarnation expands your options, allowing you to experiment with new combinations and entirely different paths of progression.

store_data.about_the_game:
Three heroes. Three decks. Three hands. One turn to spend them

Most deckbuilders hand you a single deck. OBOLUS hands you three — on the table at

the same time, each with its own cards, its own hand, and its own coin to spend.

Every turn you decide not just what to play, but who plays it, and in

what order.

Your healer's spare obol can pay for the brawler's finisher.

Your gambler can set up a kill your knight is one card short of landing.

That's the difference between a card game and a party.

The coachman takes his fee along the way

Sorel drives you from land to land and never quotes a price up front. Six worlds

lie between you and whatever is waiting at the end, and each one plays by a rule of

its own — the road you walk is made of cards, dealt three at a time. Take the

battle, take the merchant, take the shortcut. The other two are gone the moment you

choose, and the road never doubles back.

Everything on offer costs something

  • Blessings that make you stronger and ask for something in return.

  • Merchant, a scavenger, and a smith's anvil that reforges what you already carry.

  • A crucible that melts two relics into one and keeps the best of both.

  • A gambling den where a game of Eighteen decides whether you set out with a gift or a debt. Nobody makes you sit down.

And the Sovereigns below

Some caves you can walk straight past. The things sleeping in them are not bosses

in the ordinary sense — they are puzzles with teeth, they are optional, and they

give up their armour only to a party built to take it.

What's in the box

  • 22 playable characters, and no two of them play alike — a bell-ringer charging a peal, a painter who copies the moves of whatever he's looking at, a smith who forges mid-fight, a symbiote that rots a whole enemy line.

  • 787 cards and 71 enemies, elites and bosses across six worlds.

  • Hardcore mode. No potions, no saves, and a fallen hero stays down. One

    run, all the way.

  • Full controller support, Steam Deck included.

  • English and Italian.

store_data.about_the_game:
Text appears only in menus, while the gameplay itself is completely intuitive and contains no words at all. Simple and accessible — even kids can easily enjoy it!

Organize my Shop 2: Pet Shop is an immersive sorting and organizing game designed to help you fully relax. Put on your favorite podcast or movie, clear your mind, and dive into a cozy, comforting organization process ✨

There are no timers, no penalties, no rush, and no overwhelming systems — just you, deeply satisfying gameplay, and hundreds of adorable items to sort.

In this second installment, a brand-new pet shop awaits you with unique levels and a huge variety of themed pet supplies! 🐱🐶

What you'll find in this game:

  • 🍖 A wide selection of food for pets, birds, and rodents

  • 🥫 Juicy canned food and tasty treat pouches

  • 🛌 Soft, cozy pet beds and litter/bedding

  • 🦮 Pet apparel, collars, and harnesses

  • 💊 Specialized veterinary diet food and medical supplies

  • 🐹 Cute decorative items for rodent cages

How to Play?

Unsorted items arrive continuously on the conveyor belt. Your goal is to drag and neatly arrange them on the shelves following clear visual cues 💡

Some items can be stacked 2-3 high to create neat little towers, helping you manage shelf space in a practical and visually pleasing way! 🧺

Game Features:

  • ⭐ Unique Levels Every Time: Every level offers fresh combinations of shelves and items. No repetitive gameplay — only near the end will you unlock a massive final level featuring all items at once!

  • ⭐ Chaos Mode Unlocked by Default: The fan-favorite Chaos Mode is available right from the start without needing any paid DLC.

  • ⭐ Auto-Save: Your progress saves automatically at any point during any level. Play for a few quick minutes or settle in for an entire evening at your own pace.

Bring perfect order to every shelf and create the pet shop of your dreams! 🐾✨

store_data.about_the_game:
They are small. They are ceramic. They are thousands.

Somewhere on a forgotten front, a weird-science experiment went very wrong. Now every garden gnome in the country wakes up at night, and they all march in the same direction: yours. Projekt Gartenzwerg is a co-op horde defense FPS for 1 to 4 players. Dig in, load your rifle and survive until dawn.

Your gunfire is your light

The horde attacks in the dark. Campfires and searchlights carve out small islands of safety, but beyond them the night is full of little painted faces. Pull the trigger and your muzzle flash lights up the field for a heartbeat. That heartbeat is how you find out what is really coming for you. It is always worse than you hoped.

An honest WW2 arsenal and some very bad ideas

From the MP40 to the Panzerschreck, every weapon kicks, flashes and throws hot brass. When bullets stop being enough, the lab has prototypes for you: arc rifles that chain lightning through the tide, incendiary rounds, and a flamethrower for when the perimeter gets personal. Whatever you bring, bring enough ammo.

The perimeter will not hold itself

Every gnome you shatter drops scrap, and scrap keeps you alive. Slam down barricades in the middle of a wave, deploy gun nests and mortars, aim a searchlight down the worst approach. The horde tears breaches into your walls, and it falls on you to plug the gap while your friends cover you. Some nights you fix the wall. Some nights you become the wall.

More than one way to spend a night

Fortify a farmhouse, funnel the tide into a mountain pass, or fight from flooded trenches under a full moon. And when holding still is not enough, escort an armed rail car through a dead forest: keep the engine running, mount the MG42 machine gun, and shoot the trees down before the horde swarms the tracks. Each mission asks a different question. The answer is always firepower.

Better with friends, deadly without them

Up to four players stand together. When one of you goes down, someone has to cross the field under fire and spend six long seconds pulling him back up, hands busy, head down, gnomes closing in. Win a sector and a harder version of it opens, from Recruit all the way to Nightmare. Earn Wunderpoints and unlock new gear for the next stand.

Features

  • 1 to 4 player online co-op horde defense

  • A living tide of ceramic gnomes, hundreds on screen

  • Light as a mechanic: muzzle flashes and searchlights reveal the horde

  • 14 WW2 weapons plus weird-science prototypes

  • Buildable defenses and breaches to repair under pressure

  • Several mission types, from static sieges to a rail car escort

  • 4 difficulty levels and Wunderpoints progression

The garden is coming. How long can you hold?
